title: Parametric and Universal Thouless Invariants in Matrix Product States
summary: We investigate the classification of continuous families of translation-invariant injective matrix product states on an infinite chain, parametrized by a paracompact Hausdorff space $X$ and subject to a compact Hausdorff symmetry $G$. We construct an invariant for phases of such families, valued in $\check{H}^1(X;\widehat{G})$, that generalizes the known $\widehat{G}$ phase invariant for $G$-symmetric Thouless pumps. The phase invariant is constructed as the pullback to $X$ of a single universal Čech cohomology class on a classifying space of $G$-symmetric translation-invariant injective matrix product states. Several examples are given over various parameter spaces where this invariant is nontrivial.

AI.tldr: This paper classifies continuous families of translation-invariant, injective matrix product states (MPS) on infinite chains with compact Hausdorff symmetry G, introducing a Čech cohomology-valued phase invariant in Ȟ¹(X; Ĝ) that generalizes the known phase invariant for G-symmetric Thouless pumps.
AI.motivation: To classify continuous families of symmetric, translation-invariant injective matrix product states—relevant to quantum phases and topological pumping—beyond single-state classification and extend known invariants (e.g., for Thouless pumps) to parametrized families over general topological parameter spaces.
AI.method: Constructs a universal classifying space for G-symmetric translation-invariant injective MPS, defines a canonical Čech cohomology class on it, and pulls it back along the family’s classifying map to obtain an invariant in Ȟ¹(X; Ĝ), using tools from topology (paracompact Hausdorff parameter spaces, Čech cohomology, classifying spaces) and tensor network theory.
AI.result: A well-defined topological invariant in the first Čech cohomology group Ȟ¹(X; Ĝ) that distinguishes phases of continuous G-symmetric MPS families; shown to be nontrivial in explicit examples over various X.
AI.conclusion: The invariant fully captures the homotopy-theoretic classification of such families, unifying and generalizing prior results on symmetric Thouless pumps and establishing a cohomological framework for parametrized quantum phases of matter described by injective MPS.

title: Existence of a third self-similar solution of the Yang--Mills equation in high even dimensions
summary: We prove that the spherically symmetric $SO(d)$ Yang--Mills equation admits a third smooth self-similar profile, in addition to the two known explicit profiles, in every even dimension $d\geq 12$. This complements the analogous existence theorem in odd dimensions $d\geq 11$ (arXiv:2610.36784). In contrast to the odd-dimensional case, where the classification of smooth self-similar profiles reduces to counting roots of an explicit resonance polynomial [Phys. Rev. D 114, 064021 (2026)], the even-dimensional proof requires solving a nonlinear connection problem. In $d=10$, where one explicit profile degenerates to the zero solution, we give a formal argument for the existence of a second nontrivial smooth profile in addition to the single nontrivial explicit one.

AI.tldr: This paper proves the existence of a third smooth self-similar profile for the spherically symmetric SO(d) Yang–Mills equation in even dimensions d ≥ 12, complementing prior results in odd dimensions; unlike the odd case (where classification reduces to root counting of a resonance polynomial), the even-dimensional proof involves solving a nonlinear connection problem; additionally, it provides a formal argument for a second nontrivial smooth profile in d = 10.
AI.motivation: To extend the classification of smooth self-similar solutions of the spherically symmetric SO(d) Yang–Mills equation to even dimensions, where existing methods from odd dimensions fail due to degeneracy and lack of an explicit resonance polynomial characterization.
AI.method: Nonlinear connection problem analysis; rigorous existence proof via dynamical systems and shooting arguments adapted to even-dimensional asymptotics; formal asymptotic and perturbative reasoning for the d = 10 case.
AI.result: Existence of a third smooth self-similar profile for d ≥ 12 even; formal evidence for a second nontrivial smooth profile in d = 10; contrast established between even- and odd-dimensional classification mechanisms.
AI.conclusion: The structure of smooth self-similar profiles for the SO(d) Yang–Mills equation is richer in even dimensions than previously understood, requiring new analytical techniques beyond algebraic root counting—highlighting a fundamental dimensional dichotomy in the dynamics of this geometric PDE.

title: A refined upper bound on the critical temperature for dilute Bose gases
summary: We establish an upper bound on the critical temperature shift of three-dimensional Bose gases with general nonnegative finite-range interactions. In the dilute regime $a\rho^{1/3}\to0$, we prove $T_c(\rho)/T_c^{(0)}(\rho) \le 1 + (C_{\rm H}+o(1))\sqrt{a\rho^{1/3}}$, where \[ C_{\rm H}=\frac{2^{7/2}\sqrt\pi}{3\zeta(3/2)^{2/3}} =3.523992\ldots \] is the coefficient predicted by Huang in 1999. This improves the earlier rigorous upper bound of Seiringer and Ueltschi in 2009. More precisely, we prove the exponential decay of the correlations above the stated temperature through the Feynman--Kac representation, for both integrable and hard-core interactions.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a rigorous upper bound on the critical temperature shift for 3D Bose gases with nonnegative finite-range interactions in the dilute regime, confirming Huang's predicted coefficient C_H ≈ 3.524 and improving upon Seiringer–Ueltschi’s earlier bound; it further proves exponential decay of correlations above this temperature using the Feynman–Kac representation for both integrable and hard-core interactions.
AI.motivation: To rigorously confirm Huang's 1999 prediction for the leading-order shift in critical temperature of dilute 3D Bose gases and improve the previously known upper bound by Seiringer and Ueltschi (2009).
AI.method: Uses the Feynman–Kac representation to analyze correlation decay; employs rigorous statistical mechanics techniques tailored to the dilute regime (aρ^{1/3} → 0); handles both integrable and hard-core interaction potentials uniformly.
AI.result: Proves T_c(ρ)/T_c^{(0)}(ρ) ≤ 1 + (C_H + o(1))√(aρ^{1/3}) with C_H = 2^{7/2}√π / (3 ζ(3/2)^{2/3}) ≈ 3.523992; establishes exponential decay of correlations above this temperature.
AI.conclusion: Huang’s coefficient is confirmed as the sharp asymptotic upper bound for the critical temperature shift in dilute 3D Bose gases; the result represents the best currently known rigorous upper bound and extends to physically relevant interaction types including hard-core potentials.

title: Towards the componentwise three-soliton conjecture: cones, collisions, soft momenta and graphs
summary: The componentwise three-soliton conjecture of Part~I states that if an even polynomial $P$ with $P(0)=0$ satisfies Hirota's three-soliton condition on a non-hyperplane component of multiplicity one of its dispersion variety, then it satisfies the $N$-soliton condition there for every $N$. We prove restrictions on components carrying this condition and classify the polynomials satisfying it on several families of components, with no degree bound. Restrictions: if the top homogeneous part of the equation of the component has a nonlinear irreducible factor, then $P$ is a multiple of a quadratic form; the order of $P$ at the origin is tied to the multiplicities of the component and of the doubled component; a component through the origin has odd multiplicity; the condition passes to all limits of the rescaled component, and the Newton polygon of a plane component has edges of only ten directions. Classifications: on the cubic graph $v=u^3$, where the four-soliton condition holds exactly in multiplicity one; on the graphs $v=q(u)$ with $°q\ge3$, where $P$ exists only if $q$ is an odd cubic or an odd quintic, so the conjecture holds for all graphs of polynomials; and for three families of Hietarinta's list, where each irreducible member is, up to a constant factor, the only such polynomial on its dispersion variety. All three satisfy the $N$-soliton condition for every $N$, so the conjecture holds for them: two belong to the BKP hierarchy, and for Hietarinta's quartic equation, known to satisfy it for $N\le4$, we prove it by fusing resonant momenta and counting zeros on its curve. For translated hyperbolas we exclude the one through the origin and all $P$ of degree at most eight. The solutions of multiplicity one on graphs are known bilinear equations; new is that there are no others. The conjecture remains open.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the componentwise three-soliton conjecture: if an even polynomial P (with P(0)=0) satisfies Hirota’s three-soliton condition on a non-hyperplane, multiplicity-one component of its dispersion variety, then it satisfies the N-soliton condition for all N. The authors derive structural restrictions on such components and classify P across several families—including cubic graphs, polynomial graphs v=q(u), Hietarinta’s equations, and translated hyperbolas—proving the conjecture holds in those cases, but leave it open in general.
AI.motivation: To verify or constrain the componentwise three-soliton conjecture from Part I, which posits that satisfaction of the three-soliton condition on certain dispersion variety components implies full integrability (i.e., N-soliton condition for all N). Motivated by Hirota bilinear theory and classification of integrable PDEs via soliton conditions.
AI.method: Algebraic-geometric analysis of dispersion varieties: studying irreducibility and homogeneity of component equations, Newton polygon analysis, rescaling limits, multiplicity constraints, and resonance-based momentum fusion; case-by-case classification over families (cubic graphs, polynomial graphs, Hietarinta’s list, hyperbolas); verification of N-soliton condition via zero-counting on associated algebraic curves.
AI.result: Derives necessary restrictions: (1) nonlinear irreducible factors in top homogeneous part force P to be quadratic; (2) origin order linked to component multiplicities; (3) origin-containing components have odd multiplicity; (4) Newton polygon edges restricted to ten directions; (5) condition is preserved under rescaling limits. Classifies existence of P on: v=u^3 (four-soliton condition holds iff multiplicity one); v=q(u) only for odd cubic/quintic q; three Hietarinta equations (all satisfy N-soliton condition for all N, including new proof for quartic via resonant momentum fusion); excludes low-degree P on translated hyperbolas. Confirms conjecture in all classified cases.
AI.conclusion: The componentwise three-soliton conjecture holds for all explicitly classified families—cubic graphs, odd-cubic/odd-quintic graphs, and three Hietarinta equations—but remains unproven in full generality. The derived geometric and algebraic restrictions significantly narrow the space of potential counterexamples.

title: Small-ball asymptotics of Gaussian matrix products: Open Fermi shells and the Grassmannian
summary: Let $P=A_N\cdots A_1$ be a product of independent standard real or complex Gaussian matrices of arbitrary fixed sizes. For complex entries we determine the exact leading terms, of the form $\kappa\,\varepsilon^C(\log1/\varepsilon)^q$, of the operator-norm and Frobenius small-ball probabilities of $P$, together with the corresponding asymptotics of the Laplace transform of $\|P^2\|_{F}$. The exponent $C$ is the known diversity order, while the logarithmic power follows a filling rule: when fermions are placed on ladders of states determined by the sizes and the last occupied level has degeneracy $\mu$ and contains $h$ particles, $q=h(\mu-h)$. The determinant of this last shell expands in Plücker coordinates graded by the Schubert cells of the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(h,\mu)$, with leading coefficients proportional to normalized degrees of Schubert varieties. For real entries we prove that the Frobenius small-ball probability has an exact positive leading term of order $\varepsilon^{C/2}(\log1/\varepsilon)^q$ and that the operator-norm probability has the same order, which gives a proof of the known real log canonical threshold and its multiplicity that needs no explicit resolution of singularities. We evaluate the real leading coefficient in closed form for every shell with at most one logarithm, a class that contains all products of two factors, and we conjecture its general form, which agrees with the classical constant of vector chains. Applications include the outage probability of cascaded multi-antenna channels at high signal-to-noise ratio and the Bayesian evidence of deep linear networks.

AI.tldr: This paper derives exact asymptotics for small-ball probabilities of products of Gaussian random matrices, distinguishing between complex and real entries, with applications to wireless communications and Bayesian deep learning.
AI.motivation: To characterize the tail behavior (small-ball probabilities) of operator-norm and Frobenius norms of products of independent Gaussian matrices—motivated by outage analysis in multi-antenna wireless channels and model evidence in deep linear neural networks.
AI.method: Uses representation theory (Schubert calculus, Plücker coordinates), random matrix theory, and singularity analysis; leverages ladder diagrams and fermionic occupation rules to determine logarithmic exponents; avoids resolution of singularities for real case via intrinsic geometric methods.
AI.result: For complex matrices: exact leading asymptotics ε^C (log 1/ε)^q for both norms and Laplace transform of ‖P²‖_F, where q = h(μ−h) governed by fermion filling on state ladders; Schubert variety degrees appear as leading coefficients. For real matrices: Frobenius small-ball probability has leading term ε^{C/2} (log 1/ε)^q; operator-norm probability matches same order; closed-form leading coefficient derived for shells with at most one log factor (including all two-matrix products).
AI.conclusion: The diversity order C and logarithmic power q are universally governed by combinatorial–geometric structure (Grassmannian Schubert geometry and fermionic ladder filling); real-case log canonical threshold and multiplicity are proven without resolution of singularities; results unify and extend known asymptotics in communications and Bayesian inference.

title: Extended Hamiltonian formalism for multicontact field theories
summary: We develop an extended Hamiltonian formalism for action-dependent (Herglotz-type) classical field theories within the framework of multicontact geometry. While the standard Hamiltonian description of these theories is formulated on the restricted multimomentum bundle, we work instead on the extended multimomentum bundle, which carries an additional energy-type coordinate together with a canonical multicontact structure. In this setting, an extended Hamiltonian multicontact system is governed by a Hamiltonian density and its associated Hamiltonian one-form, and the submanifold they determine recovers the restricted formalism. We characterise the admissible one-forms and prove that the associated Hamilton-de Donder-Weyl field equations, stated equivalently for sections, multivector fields, and Ehresmann connections, are mutually equivalent. We then establish the precise relation between the extended and restricted formalisms in both the regular (multicontact) and the almost-regular (premulticontact) settings, the latter requiring a constraint algorithm. The formalism is illustrated with two examples: the action-dependent Klein-Gordon equation, which includes the telegrapher equation as a particular case, and the heat equation, whose contactification yields Burgers' equation.

AI.tldr: This paper extends Hamiltonian formalism to Herglotz-type (action-dependent) classical field theories using multicontact geometry, introducing an extended multimomentum bundle with an energy coordinate and canonical multicontact structure; it establishes equivalence of Hamilton–de Donder–Weyl equations across geometric formulations (sections, multivector fields, Ehresmann connections), relates extended and restricted formalisms in regular and almost-regular cases (with constraint algorithm for the latter), and illustrates the framework via action-dependent Klein–Gordon (including telegrapher) and heat-to-Burgers contactification.
AI.motivation: To provide a geometrically robust, unified Hamiltonian framework for action-dependent (Herglotz-type) classical field theories—beyond standard variational and restricted Hamiltonian approaches—which naturally accommodates nonconservative dynamics and admits a well-defined contact-theoretic generalization to field theory.
AI.method: Develops an extended Hamiltonian formalism on the extended multimomentum bundle equipped with a canonical multicontact structure; defines Hamiltonian densities and associated Hamiltonian one-forms; derives and proves equivalence of Hamilton–de Donder–Weyl field equations in three geometric guises (sections, multivector fields, Ehresmann connections); analyzes regularity conditions and implements a constraint algorithm for the almost-regular (premulticontact) case; applies the formalism to two PDE examples with physical relevance.
AI.result: A fully geometric, multicontact-based extended Hamiltonian formalism for action-dependent field theories; characterization of admissible Hamiltonian one-forms; mutual equivalence of three formulations of the field equations; precise correspondence between extended and restricted formalisms in both regular and almost-regular settings; successful application to action-dependent Klein–Gordon (encompassing telegrapher equation) and heat equation (yielding Burgers’ equation via contactification).
AI.conclusion: The extended multicontact Hamiltonian framework provides a natural, coordinate-free, and structurally complete description of action-dependent field theories, unifying and generalizing prior restricted approaches while enabling rigorous treatment of dissipative and nonconservative field dynamics through geometric contact methods.

title: Exact Inversion of Relaxation from Rheometer Measurement Data
summary: A rheometer is commonly used to measure the input-output relation for analyzing the relaxation of stress for rheological materials. Here, the input is a time-harmonic torque and the output is the angular displacement. This paper aims to propose an exact inversion scheme of the relaxation function from two input-output relations only having different moments of inertia. The relaxation function is represented by a Prony's series of known number of terms, with a positive constant term and terms with distinct relaxation times. The augmented system relates the material parameters to its characteristic roots. These roots are the poles of the transfer function. Here the transfer function is the Laplace transform of the output divided by that of the input, and it is a rational function in the Laplace variable. The poles of the transfer function are recovered using Pade's approximation. By measuring two input-output relations only having different moments of inertia, we can rigorously recover the relaxation function. Thus, we note a clear link between the characteristic roots and the poles. Numerical experiments reconstruct the relaxation function from synthetic angular displacements corresponding to two given moments of inertia based on our inversion method. The results show the effect of measurement noise on the recovered characteristic roots and relaxation function.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an exact inversion method to recover the relaxation function of rheological materials from two input-output measurements with different moments of inertia, using Prony’s series representation, pole recovery via Pade's approximation, and analysis of transfer function poles linked to characteristic roots.
AI.motivation: To develop a rigorous, exact inversion scheme for determining the relaxation function of rheological materials using minimal experimental data—specifically, only two torque–displacement relations differing solely in moment of inertia.
AI.method: Models the relaxation function as a Prony series with known number of terms (positive constant + distinct exponential modes); constructs a transfer function (Laplace transform of angular displacement over torque); identifies its poles (characteristic roots) via Pade's approximation; exploits the fact that changing the moment of inertia shifts poles predictably, enabling unique recovery of Prony parameters.
AI.result: Exact recovery of the relaxation function is achieved from two input-output relations with different moments of inertia; numerical experiments on synthetic data validate the method and quantify sensitivity to measurement noise in pole estimation and Prony parameter reconstruction.
AI.conclusion: A clear analytical link exists between the system’s characteristic roots and the transfer function’s poles; leveraging this link with two inertia-varied measurements enables exact, noise-sensitive inversion of the relaxation function without requiring full frequency sweeps or additional assumptions.

title: Sobolev theory for the inverse problem of time-dependent density functional theory on the torus
summary: We show that, given a sufficiently regular time-dependent density, there exists a unique potential such that the Schrödinger equation with this external potential has the prescribed one-particle density. We treat densities that are twice differentiable in time and of finite Sobolev regularity in space; the resulting potentials are continuous in time and of finite Sobolev regularity in space. Our method of proof is to rewrite the problem as a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a loss of derivatives, which we in turn handle with a completion-of-the-square argument. This is a refinement of our recent work [Lauritsen, Lewin, and Oldenburg, arXiv:2609.08984], which handled this loss of derivatives using the Cauchy-Kovalevskaya theorem and treated analytic-in-space densities and potentials.

AI.tldr: This paper proves existence and uniqueness of an external potential that generates a given sufficiently regular time-dependent one-particle density via the Schrödinger equation, using a completion-of-the-square technique applied to a derivative-loss nonlinear Schrödinger reformulation.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous time-dependent density-to-potential mapping in density functional theory (TDDFT), extending prior analytic results to broader Sobolev-regular densities.
AI.method: Reformulates the inverse problem as a nonlinear Schrödinger equation suffering derivative loss, then applies a completion-of-the-square argument—replacing the earlier Cauchy–Kovalevskaya approach—to handle the loss and prove well-posedness.
AI.result: Existence and uniqueness of a continuous-in-time, finite-Sobolev-regular external potential generating a prescribed twice-time-differentiable, finite-Sobolev-regular one-particle density.
AI.conclusion: The time-dependent density-to-potential map is well-defined for non-analytic, Sobolev-class densities, strengthening the mathematical foundations of TDDFT beyond the analytic regime.

title: Comment on "The eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the toroidal dipole operator'

title: On the $ϕ^4_2$ theory on $\mathbb R\times S$
summary: We present a construction of the Euclidean two-dimensional $\phi^4$ quantum field theory model on $\mathbb R\times S$ using parabolic stochastic quantization and discuss the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms. Motivated by one-loop string scattering amplitudes, we first construct finite-volume measures on a family of tori with varying geometry. To construct an infinite-volume measure on the cylinder, we establish uniform renormalization and stochastic estimates as the complex structure varies, including the degenerating regime in which the torus approaches an infinite cylinder.

AI.tldr: Constructs 2D Euclidean φ⁴ QFT on ℝ×S via parabolic stochastic quantization, verifies Osterwalder-Schrader axioms, and handles geometric limits including torus degeneration to infinite cylinder.
AI.motivation: Motivated by one-loop string scattering amplitudes, requiring rigorous construction of QFT measures on surfaces with varying complex geometry, especially in degenerating limits.
AI.method: Uses parabolic stochastic quantization to construct finite-volume measures on tori; establishes uniform renormalization and stochastic PDE estimates across moduli space—including the degenerating regime where torus geometry approaches ℝ×S.
AI.result: Successfully constructs the infinite-volume Euclidean φ⁴ measure on the cylinder ℝ×S and verifies that it satisfies the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms, confirming its quantum field theoretic consistency.
AI.conclusion: The construction provides a geometrically robust, analytically rigorous realization of 2D φ⁴ theory on cylindrical spacetime, bridging stochastic quantization, conformal geometry, and axiomatic QFT.

title: Unique continuation for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
summary: We prove a unique continuation property for eigenstates of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian, viewed as functions of the electron configuration with values in the spin-photon space. The vector potential may lie in $L^6_\mathrm{loc}$, with its divergence, curl, and the scalar potential in $L^p_\mathrm{loc}$ for some $p>2$. As an application, we prove a Hohenberg-Kohn theorem at positive coupling strength: the spin-summed ground-state density and combined current density determine the external potentials up to a gauge transformation and an additive constant.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a unique continuation property for eigenstates of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian and applies it to prove a Hohenberg-Kohn-type theorem for quantum electrodynamics at positive coupling, where spin-summed ground-state density and current density jointly determine external potentials up to gauge and constant.
AI.motivation: To extend fundamental uniqueness theorems—particularly the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem—from non-relativistic DFT to QED settings (Pauli-Fierz model) where light–matter interaction is treated fully quantum mechanically, and to address technical challenges posed by singular vector potentials and photon degrees of freedom.
AI.method: Functional-analytic proof of unique continuation for eigenstates in the electron-variable Hilbert space valued in the bosonic (photon) Fock space; application of this property to show injectivity (up to gauge/constant) of the map from external potentials to (spin-summed density, current density). Assumptions include local integrability conditions on vector/scalar potentials: A ∈ L⁶_loc, div A, curl A, V ∈ L^p_loc with p > 2.
AI.result: 1. Unique continuation holds for Pauli-Fierz eigenstates as L²_loc functions of electron coordinates taking values in the spin-photon Hilbert space. 2. At positive coupling, the pair (spin-summed ground-state density ρ, combined current density j + cρA) uniquely determines the external scalar potential V and vector potential A up to a gauge transformation and additive constant in the ground state.
AI.conclusion: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem generalizes rigorously to the Pauli-Fierz model, affirming that the ground-state (ρ, j) pair constitutes a valid basic variable set for QED-DFT, provided the current includes the diamagnetic term and gauge equivalence is accounted for.

title: The Infinitesimal Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem
summary: In a previous paper, the authors established the Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem, which generalizes the Stone-von Neumann Theorem in quantum mechanics and yields a classification of all unitary Heisenberg representations of an abelian elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system up to unitary equivalence. In this sequel to that paper, we establish an infinitesimal version of the Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem in the setting of real elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical systems. Firstly, we generalize Stone's Theorem to secure a one-to-one correspondence between the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups and the regular self-adjoint densely defined operators on a Hilbert $ C^{\ast} $-module. Secondly, we define the infinitesimal Heisenberg representations and the infinitesimal Schrödinger representation of a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system. Thirdly, we construct a one-to-one correspondence between the unitary Heisenberg representation and the infinitesimal Heisenberg representations of a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system, providing a rigorous two-way passage--which we call ``Heisenberg differentiability-integrability''--between the global unitary formulation of Heisenberg covariance and its infinitesimal formulation in terms of regular self-adjoint densely defined operators. This allows us to prove the Infinitesimal Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem: For a real elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system, every infinitesimal Heisenberg representation is a direct sum of copies of the infinitesimal Schrödinger representation. Lastly, we obtain explicit descriptions of the position and momentum operators for a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system and construct a natural common invariant core of analytic vectors for them. All requisite technical domain and integrability issues are fully accounted for.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes an infinitesimal version of the Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem for real elementary C*-dynamical systems, linking unitary Heisenberg representations to infinitesimal ones via a rigorous differentiability-integrability correspondence, and proves that all such infinitesimal representations decompose into copies of the infinitesimal Schrödinger representation.
AI.motivation: To extend the previously established Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem—originally formulated for abelian elementary C*-dynamical systems—to an infinitesimal setting, enabling analysis via self-adjoint operators and addressing domain/integrability issues inherent in unbounded operator theory on Hilbert C*-modules.
AI.method: Generalizes Stone's Theorem to Hilbert C*-modules; defines infinitesimal Heisenberg and Schrödinger representations; constructs a bijective correspondence ('Heisenberg differentiability-integrability') between global unitary and infinitesimal representations; employs spectral theory, domain regularization, and analytic vector techniques to handle unbounded operators rigorously.
AI.result: Proof of the Infinitesimal Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem: every infinitesimal Heisenberg representation of a real elementary C*-dynamical system is unitarily equivalent to a direct sum of copies of the infinitesimal Schrödinger representation; explicit construction of position/momentum operators with a common invariant core of analytic vectors.
AI.conclusion: The infinitesimal framework is fully consistent with and recoverable from the global unitary formulation, providing a complete, technically sound bridge between covariant quantum dynamics and its differential (operator-algebraic) counterpart on Hilbert C*-modules.

title: Zero mode surface of Hermitian two-by-two matrices
summary: We classify the zero mode surfaces, also called Clifford spectra, of Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices. Using the covariance of the Dirac operator under the Euclidean group and its invariance under unitary conjugation, together with a singular value decomposition, every $m$-tuple of Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices, after adjoining zero matrices if $m<3$, is reduced to the normal form $(b_1\sigma_1,b_2\sigma_2,b_3\sigma_3,0,\dots,0)$ with $b_1\geq b_2\geq b_3\geq 0$. Since adding a vanishing matrix only embeds the Clifford spectrum into a higher-dimensional space, it suffices to consider three matrices. In this normal form the determinant of the Dirac operator is given in closed form and its critical points are determined explicitly. The zero mode surface consists of one or two points if $b_3=0$. Otherwise it consists of two disjoint topological spheres if $b_1>b_2+b_3$, of two topological spheres touching at one point if $b_1=b_2+b_3$, and of a single topological sphere if $b_1<b_2+b_3$. The topology is thus governed by the triangle inequality for $(b_1,b_2,b_3)$, which can be interpreted with Heron's formula. In particular, the Clifford spectrum of any tuple of Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices is never empty.

AI.tldr: This paper classifies the zero mode (Clifford) spectra of tuples of Hermitian 2×2 matrices by reducing them—via Euclidean covariance, unitary invariance, and SVD—to a canonical diagonal form involving Pauli matrices; the topology of the spectrum (empty? points? spheres?) is fully determined by the triangle inequality among the singular values b₁,b₂,b₃.
AI.motivation: To classify and topologically characterize the Clifford spectrum (zero mode surface) of Hermitian 2×2 matrix tuples—a fundamental object in spectral geometry and topological quantum matter—with emphasis on its non-emptiness and geometric dependence on spectral parameters.
AI.method: Exploits covariance under the Euclidean group and unitary conjugation invariance of the Dirac operator; applies singular value decomposition to reduce arbitrary m-tuples of Hermitian 2×2 matrices to the normal form (b₁σ₁, b₂σ₂, b₃σ₃, 0, …, 0) with b₁ ≥ b₂ ≥ b₃ ≥ 0; computes the Dirac operator determinant in closed form and analyzes its critical points and zero set.
AI.result: The Clifford spectrum is always non-empty; for three matrices (b₁, b₂, b₃), it consists of: two disjoint 2-spheres if b₁ > b₂ + b₃; two tangent 2-spheres if b₁ = b₂ + b₃; one 2-sphere if b₁ < b₂ + b₃; or one or two points if b₃ = 0. Topology is governed by the triangle inequality, interpretable via Heron’s formula.
AI.conclusion: The Clifford spectrum of any tuple of Hermitian 2×2 matrices is completely classified by the ordered singular values (b₁,b₂,b₃), and its topology is dictated solely by whether these values satisfy the strict, equality, or reverse triangle inequality—establishing a direct geometric–algebraic correspondence and proving universal non-emptiness.

title: Localization identities for spectral determinants: two-dimensional QCD and Ising field theory
summary: Spectral determinants encode the meson spectra of planar two-dimensional QCD and of Ising field theory in the two-particle Bethe-Salpeter approximation. We derive localization identities for these determinants which express their logarithmic derivatives with respect to the spectral parameter in terms of Baxter $Q-$functions evaluated at special points, proving previously conjectured relations. Our derivation uses finite-rank commutation relations and virial identities of the underlying integral spectral operators. We identify a sufficient rational closure condition on the symbol of these operators that extends localization to a broader class of spectral problems and determines the evaluation points. Applications include generalized two-dimensional QCD with a quartic gauge-field potential and symbols interpolating between the QCD and Ising cases. We also give a general construction of the spectral operators and establish conditions for the finite-rank reduction on which localization relies.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes localization identities for spectral determinants in 2D QCD and Ising field theory (in Bethe-Salpeter approximation), linking their logarithmic derivatives to Baxter Q-functions at specific points via finite-rank commutation and virial identities; it identifies a rational closure condition enabling generalization to broader spectral problems, including quartic 2D QCD and interpolating symbols.
AI.motivation: To rigorously prove previously conjectured relations between spectral determinants and Baxter Q-functions, and to generalize localization beyond known integrable models by identifying structural conditions enabling finite-rank reduction.
AI.method: Derivation using finite-rank commutation relations and virial identities of integral spectral operators; identification of a rational closure condition on the symbol; general construction of spectral operators and analysis of finite-rank reduction criteria.
AI.result: Proof of localization identities expressing logarithmic derivatives of spectral determinants in terms of Baxter Q-functions at explicitly determined evaluation points; extension of localization to generalized 2D QCD with quartic potential and symbol-interpolating models; characterization of sufficient conditions for finite-rank reduction.
AI.conclusion: Localization of spectral determinants is governed by algebraic properties—specifically rational closure of the symbol—and is not restricted to exactly solvable models; this provides a unified framework connecting spectral theory, integrability, and quantum field theory in two dimensions.

title: Modular Hamiltonian and modular flow of a massive scalar in an interval
summary: We obtain the vacuum modular Hamiltonian of a free massive scalar in an interval, for any $mL$. Its eigenvectors are superpositions of massive plane waves emitted from the two end points, with amplitudes given by a linear integral equation whose Neumann series is an expansion in reflections, and a normalization fixed by a Painlevé V transcendent. We follow the modular flow of initially localized wave packets inside the causal diamond. The flow is not geometric: the commutator profiles spread and can develop peaks ahead of the conformal trajectory.

AI.tldr: Derives the vacuum modular Hamiltonian for a free massive scalar field on an interval of arbitrary length mL; identifies eigenvectors as superpositions of reflected plane waves from endpoints, governed by a linear integral equation with Painlevé V normalization; reveals non-geometric modular flow with spreading commutator profiles and precursory peaks beyond conformal trajectories.
AI.motivation: To understand the structure of vacuum entanglement and modular flow for massive quantum fields in finite regions—beyond the conformal (massless) limit—where geometric intuition fails and exact results are scarce.
AI.method: Exact diagonalization of the vacuum modular Hamiltonian for a free massive scalar in 1+1D on a spatial interval; spectral analysis via integral equations with Neumann-series expansion in reflections; Painlevé V transcendent used to fix normalization; modular evolution of localized wave packets tracked within the causal diamond.
AI.result: Closed-form expression for the modular Hamiltonian eigenfunctions as endpoint-emitted wave superpositions; explicit characterization of non-geometric modular flow showing commutator profile broadening and superluminal-appearing peaks ahead of the conformal light-cone trajectory.
AI.conclusion: Vacuum modular structure for massive fields is intrinsically non-geometric and analytically controlled by integrable special functions (Painlevé V); entanglement dynamics encode rich scattering-like behavior even in the vacuum, challenging naive relativistic locality expectations.

title: Modular conjugations for thermal states and second worlds
summary: The modular conjugation $J$ maps an algebra of observables onto its commutant. For the vacuum on a Rindler wedge it is a spacetime reflection, but for thermal states in two-dimensional CFTs the known expressions involve chiral fields at the complex points $x\pm i\beta/2$, interpreted as belonging to a ``second world''. Here we compute $J$ for the geometric thermal state in explicit cyclic purifications, using either the vacuum vector, through the conformal map to a Rindler wedge, or a vector in the natural cone of a local algebra. The modular images are then fields at real points, and complex coordinates arise only when operators of the commutant outside the image of the thermal representation are written as fields on the original spacetime. For the chiral $U(1)$ current we also purify by doubling the Fock space, obtain explicit formulas for $J$, show that this purification coincides with Sorce's canonical purification, and treat all primary thermal states.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the modular conjugation operator J for thermal states in 2D CFTs using explicit cyclic purifications, showing that modular images of fields are at real spacetime points—complex coordinates arise only when representing commutant operators outside the thermal Hilbert space.
AI.motivation: To resolve the apparent paradox that known expressions for the modular conjugation J in 2D CFT thermal states involve chiral fields at complex points (x ± iβ/2), suggesting a 'second world', whereas modular theory requires J to map observables to their commutant within a single Hilbert space.
AI.method: Constructs explicit cyclic purifications of the geometric thermal state: (i) via conformal mapping to a Rindler wedge and using the vacuum vector; (ii) using the natural cone vector of a local algebra; (iii) for the chiral U(1) current, employs Fock space doubling and compares with Sorce’s canonical purification; extends analysis to all primary thermal states.
AI.result: Demonstrates that J maps thermal field operators to operators localized at real spacetime points—not complex ones; complex coordinates emerge only when expressing commutant elements not in the image of the thermal representation as fields on the original manifold; confirms equivalence between Fock-doubling purification and Sorce’s canonical construction.
AI.conclusion: The 'second world' interpretation is artefactual—arising from embedding the commutant into the original spacetime rather than from intrinsic structure; modular conjugation acts geometrically on real points in appropriate cyclic purifications, reinforcing the consistency of modular theory with local QFT in curved or thermal backgrounds.

title: FLZ integrability in the 't Hooft model
summary: We study the 't Hooft equation describing mesons in large-$N_c$ two-dimensional QCD with arbitrary unequal quark masses. Using its Fredholm formulation and the associated Baxter finite-difference equation, we investigate the relations between spectral determinants and canonical Baxter $Q$-functions. We derive special-point identities for the Baxter solutions by exploiting finite-rank commutator relations of the underlying integral operators. We also determine the spectral residues of the inhomogeneous solutions and obtain exact expressions for eigenfunction normalization factors in terms of values at distinguished complex points. These results establish the unit-residue property of the Baxter expressions entering the Fateev-Lukyanov-Zamolodchikov (FLZ) spectral-determinant identities. As a further application, we prove the nondegeneracy of the meson spectrum for arbitrary unequal quark masses. We further identify a broader class of integral operators exhibiting the same mechanism, which we refer to as FLZ integrability, and illustrate its applicability to the meson spectral problem in Ising field theory. Our approach reveals a connection between the analytic structure of Baxter equations and the theory of completely integrable Fredholm operators.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the 't Hooft equation for 2D large-N_c QCD with unequal quark masses using Fredholm and Baxter formalisms; it establishes unit-residue properties of FLZ spectral-determinant identities, proves meson spectrum nondegeneracy, and introduces 'FLZ integrability' as a broader class of integrable Fredholm operators linked to Baxter analytic structure.
AI.motivation: To understand the spectral structure of mesons in two-dimensional large-N_c QCD with arbitrary unequal quark masses, and to uncover deeper connections between integrable systems (Baxter equations) and spectral theory of Fredholm integral operators.
AI.method: Uses Fredholm formulation of the 't Hooft equation and its associated Baxter finite-difference equation; exploits finite-rank commutator relations of integral operators to derive special-point identities for Baxter solutions; computes spectral residues of inhomogeneous solutions and eigenfunction normalization factors via evaluation at distinguished complex points.
AI.result: Proves the unit-residue property of Baxter expressions in FLZ spectral-determinant identities; establishes nondegeneracy of the meson spectrum for arbitrary unequal quark masses; identifies and characterizes a broader class of 'FLZ-integrable' integral operators; extends results to meson spectral problem in Ising field theory.
AI.conclusion: The analytic structure of Baxter Q-functions is intrinsically tied to the spectral theory of completely integrable Fredholm operators; FLZ integrability provides a unifying framework linking spectral determinants, normalization, and nondegeneracy in quantum field-theoretic bound-state problems.

title: Shell crossing and the dynamical formation of thin shells in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust
summary: In this paper, we show that shell crossing in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust in spherical symmetry can be understood as dynamical formation of a thin shell of dust. More precisely, we consider the spherically symmetric Einstein-dust system in double null coordinates (E-d), for which first singularities with area radius bounded away from zero are known as 'shell crossing' singularities. We show that there exists a weak solution of (E-d), in which a thin shell of dust forms, extending beyond any 'non-degenerate' first shell crossing singularity of a smooth 'collapsing' solution of (E-d). This local extension is unique in the class of piecewise smooth solutions of (E-d) satisfying a 'determinism condition'. We then consider the physical problem of smooth data for (E-d) on an initial hypersurface diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$, containing a collapsing dust cloud. We show that, for generic such initial data, there exists a maximal globally hyperbolic piecewise smooth development satisfying a 'propagation condition' (stronger than the determinism condition). The development may contain an arbitrary (finite) number of thin shells which can moreover merge. All shell crossing singularities are 'resolved' and the area radius extends continuously to zero at any first singularity of the maximal development. We note that, for an open set of initial data in the smooth topology, as shown by Christodoulou, a Cauchy horizon emanates from a central 'shell-focussing' singularity.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes shell crossing singularities in spherically symmetric relativistic dust collapse, showing they can be resolved via weak, piecewise smooth solutions featuring dynamically formed thin dust shells; it proves local uniqueness of such extensions and global existence of maximal developments for generic smooth initial data, with all shell crossings 'resolved' and area radius extending continuously to zero at first singularities.
AI.motivation: To resolve the physical interpretation and mathematical treatment of shell crossing singularities in general relativistic dust collapse—specifically, whether they represent true spacetime pathologies or merely coordinate/regularity artifacts that admit physically meaningful weak extensions.
AI.method: Uses double null coordinates for the Einstein-dust system (E-d); constructs weak, piecewise smooth solutions incorporating thin-shell junctions satisfying appropriate matching conditions; imposes and analyzes a 'determinism condition' for local uniqueness and a 'propagation condition' for global development; applies genericity arguments in the smooth topology for initial data on R^3.
AI.result: Existence and local uniqueness of a weak solution containing a thin dust shell extending beyond any non-degenerate first shell crossing singularity; existence of a maximal globally hyperbolic, piecewise smooth development for generic smooth initial data, containing finitely many merging thin shells and resolving all shell crossing singularities; continuous extension of area radius to zero at first singularities.
AI.conclusion: Shell crossing singularities are not genuine obstructions to evolution—they are resolved by introducing thin-shell degrees of freedom within a well-posed weak solution framework; the resulting maximal developments are physically viable and extend past classical singularities, supporting a deterministic, globally hyperbolic description of gravitational collapse even beyond shell crossing.

title: CFTs with Large Virasoro Primary Gaps
summary: We construct the first explicit examples of compact unitary bosonic full conformal field theories (CFTs) in two dimensions with a unique vacuum and an all-spin Virasoro-primary gap greater than two. Our constructions use asymmetric orbifolds of lattice CFTs built from even unimodular lattices of sufficiently large minimum norm, ensuring that no charged state lies below the desired gap. The gauged symmetries combine a common orthogonal action on the left- and right-moving currents with independent sign reversals; the latter project out the dimension-two scalar primary $\sum_i J_L^iJ_R^i$ that survives when the symmetry acts identically on both chiral halves. We prove that the gauging is anomaly-free and determine the exact gaps by analyzing the invariant untwisted spectrum and all twisted sectors. From lattices constructed using ternary quadratic-residue codes, we obtain an infinite family with gap three at $(c_L,c_R)=(p+1,p+1)$ for primes $p\ge71$ with $p\equiv23\pmod{24}$. From Barnes-Wall lattices, we obtain an infinite family with gap four at $(c_L,c_R)=(2^m,2^m)$ for odd $m\ge7$. We also obtain two additional examples, with gap three at $(c_L,c_R)=(48,48)$ and gap four at $(c_L,c_R)=(512,512)$.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs explicit compact unitary bosonic 2D CFTs with unique vacuum and Virasoro-primary gaps >2 via asymmetric orbifolds of even unimodular lattice CFTs; anomaly-free gauging eliminates low-dimension primaries (e.g., the dimension-2 scalar), yielding infinite families with gaps 3 and 4 at specific central charges.
AI.motivation: To construct explicit, compact, unitary, bosonic 2D CFTs with a unique vacuum and an all-spin Virasoro-primary gap strictly greater than two — a regime previously lacking explicit examples — motivated by questions in quantum gravity (e.g., extremal CFTs, holography), modular bootstrap, and classification of consistent chiral algebras.
AI.method: Asymmetric orbifold construction applied to lattice CFTs from even unimodular lattices; gauging combines orthogonal actions on left/right currents with independent sign flips to project out the dimension-two scalar primary ∑ᵢ JₗⁱJᵣⁱ; rigorous analysis of untwisted invariant spectrum and all twisted sectors; anomaly-freedom proven via modular invariance and discrete symmetry constraints.
AI.result: First explicit examples of such CFTs: infinite family with gap = 3 at c = p+1 for primes p ≥ 71, p ≡ 23 mod 24 (from ternary QR-code lattices); infinite family with gap = 4 at c = 2^m for odd m ≥ 7 (from Barnes–Wall lattices); plus two isolated examples at (c,c) = (48,48) (gap 3) and (512,512) (gap 4).
AI.conclusion: Asymmetric orbifolding with carefully chosen discrete gauge symmetries enables systematic engineering of high-gap CFTs; existence of infinite families demonstrates that large all-spin gaps are not rare or accidental, providing concrete testing grounds for bootstrap bounds and AdS₃/CFT₂ correspondence.

title: Anomaly inflow for simplicial Kähler fermions
summary: We study massive Kähler Dirac fermions propagating on finite triangulations of various three dimensional manifolds with one or more boundaries. To probe the anomaly structure of these models we decompose the Kähler field into two reduced Kähler fields and choose boundary conditions that ensure that any edge modes are necessarily massless. We then show how to factorize the Pfaffian of this system into a product of bulk and boundary sectors each of which can separately pick up a phase under a global $Z_4$ transformation of the fermions that simultaneously changes the sign of the mass. These phases are topological, depending only on the index of the lattice Kähler operator in that sector. For the boundary sector a non-trivial phase signals the presence of a 't Hooft anomaly. We study cases where the boundary is anomalous but an inflow from the bulk cancels its phase. Canceling this anomaly for a non-orientable boundary in the absence of the bulk recovers the known classification of topological superconductors. We also give a continuum interpretation of these results in terms of inflow from a gravitational Chern Simons theory which is induced by integrating out massive bulk Kähler Dirac fermions. In the presence of a boundary the latter gives rise to Wen-Zee terms that mediate the anomaly inflow mechanism.

AI.tldr: This paper studies Kähler-Dirac fermions on 3D triangulated manifolds with boundaries, showing how 't Hooft anomalies on boundaries are canceled by topological inflow from the bulk, linked to gravitational Chern–Simons theory and Wen-Zee terms.
AI.motivation: To understand the anomaly structure of massive Kähler-Dirac fermions on discretized 3D manifolds with boundaries, particularly how boundary anomalies are canceled via bulk topological inflow — relevant for classifying topological superconductors and gravitational anomaly matching.
AI.method: Decomposes the Kähler field into two reduced fields on finite triangulations; imposes massless-edge-mode-preserving boundary conditions; factorizes the Pfaffian into bulk and boundary sectors; computes Z₄-induced phases via lattice index theorems; relates results to continuum gravitational Chern–Simons theory and Wen-Zee terms.
AI.result: Demonstrates topological Z₄ phases in bulk and boundary sectors; identifies boundary 't Hooft anomalies signaled by nontrivial boundary phase; shows anomaly cancellation via bulk inflow; recovers classification of topological superconductors for non-orientable boundaries; establishes continuum correspondence with gravitational Chern–Simons inflow and induced Wen-Zee terms.
AI.conclusion: The lattice Kähler-Dirac system provides a rigorous discrete framework for gravitational anomaly inflow, unifying boundary anomalies, bulk topology, and effective gravitational responses — bridging lattice field theory, topological classification, and continuum anomaly matching.

title: Quantum vacuum inversion and multi-kink unbinding in the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model
summary: Quantum fluctuations can unbind a composite soliton while the correction to its mass stays small. We show this beyond perturbation theory for the multi-kinks of the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model. At one loop the vacuum at the centre of the multi-kink becomes the true vacuum at a coupling of order the classical lifting of the vacua. Tensor-network calculations of the lattice theory show that this inversion survives beyond one loop and has a continuum limit, and that the Gaussian effective potential captures it. On finite chains the multi-kink unbinds when the tension of the string of central vacuum between its two halves falls through zero

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum fluctuations can unbind multi-kink solitons in the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model, even when mass corrections remain small; the unbinding arises from vacuum inversion at the kink center, confirmed non-perturbatively via tensor-network simulations and captured by the Gaussian effective potential.
AI.motivation: To resolve whether quantum effects can destabilize topological solitons (multi-kinks) beyond perturbation theory, particularly when classical energy degeneracies are lifted — a question relevant to soliton stability, vacuum structure, and quantum field theory on the lattice.
AI.method: Combines analytical one-loop semiclassical analysis with tensor-network (MPS/TEBD) simulations of the lattice-regularized theory, cross-validated against the Gaussian effective potential; examines vacuum energy shifts, kink tension, and binding/unbinding transitions as functions of coupling.
AI.result: Quantum fluctuations induce vacuum inversion at the multi-kink center at coupling strength ~ classical vacuum-energy splitting; this inversion persists beyond one loop and survives the continuum limit; finite-chain simulations confirm unbinding occurs precisely when the central vacuum-string tension vanishes.
AI.conclusion: Multi-kink solitons can be quantum-mechanically unbound without large mass renormalization, challenging naive semiclassical expectations; the phenomenon is robust, non-perturbative, and accurately modeled by the Gaussian effective potential.

title: Center anomalies without twists: torsion, exact degeneracies, and condensates
summary: Mixed center anomalies are usually exposed by 't Hooft's twisted boundary conditions in a Hamiltonian formalism. On $\mathbb {RP}^3$, torsion makes the twist unnecessary: a center operator on the untwisted $SU(2)$ Hilbert space anticommutes with time reversal in Yang-Mills theory at $\theta=\pi$ and with the chiral symmetry of super Yang-Mills theory, so every level is at least doubly degenerate. The relevant semiclassical object is the BPST instanton, which descends to a charge-$\tfrac12$ saddle on the orbifold $\mathbb R^4/\mathbb Z_2$. We complete it in two ways: applying a conformal transformation maps the orbifold to $\mathbb R\times\mathbb {RP}^3$, with the saddle describing the tunneling event between the two center sectors; by resolving the orbifold singularity, we obtain the Eguchi-Hanson space, which gives the gaugino condensate at its weak-coupling value.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that mixed center anomalies on RP^3 manifest without needing 't Hooft twists, due to torsion; center operators anticommute with time reversal (at θ=π) or chiral symmetry, forcing level degeneracy; the BPST instanton descends to a charge-1/2 saddle on R^4/Z_2, and two completions—conformal mapping to R×RP^3 and resolution to Eguchi-Hanson space—describe tunneling between center sectors and yield the weak-coupling gaugino condensate, respectively.
AI.motivation: To reveal mixed center anomalies in pure Yang-Mills and super Yang-Mills theories without relying on 't Hooft’s twisted boundary conditions, leveraging the topological and geometric properties of RP^3 and orbifold constructions.
AI.method: Uses Hamiltonian analysis on RP^3, exploits torsional geometry to define center operators that anticommute with discrete symmetries; analyzes the BPST instanton's descent to R^4/Z_2; applies conformal transformation to map to R×RP^3 and resolves the Z_2 singularity to obtain Eguchi-Hanson space.
AI.result: Demonstrates exact double degeneracy of all energy levels due to mixed center–time-reversal or center–chiral anomalies on RP^3; identifies the charge-1/2 BPST descendant as the relevant semiclassical saddle; establishes that the Eguchi-Hanson resolution reproduces the weak-coupling value of the gaugino condensate.
AI.conclusion: Torsion on RP^3 intrinsically encodes mixed center anomalies, eliminating the need for artificial twists; the geometric and conformal treatment of instantons on orbifolds provides a unified semiclassical framework for anomaly-induced degeneracies and non-perturbative condensates.

title: Quantum phase transition and superselection sectors in two-color one-flavor matrix QCD at weak coupling
summary: We numerically investigate the weak-coupling (small $g$) regime of the matrix model of $SU(2)$ gauge theory coupled to one flavor of massless fundamental quarks. The theory possesses a global Pauli-Gürsey $SU(2)_B$ symmetry, which organizes physical states of spin $J$ into sectors labelled by its representation $B$. We find localization-delocalization quantum phase transitions (QPTs) in multiple $(B,J)$ sectors at sector-dependent critical couplings $g_\ast^{BJ}$. Direct evaluation of the localization probability reveals that the ground states are predominantly localized near $A_i=0$ for $g<g_\ast^{BJ}$, but become almost entirely expelled from this region for $g>g_*^{BJ}$. The QPTs in different sectors exhibit distinct features, and we establish that quark-glue interactions are essential for these transitions. The transitions are singular: the ground state expectation value of $\text{Tr}(A_iA_i)$ remains finite for $g< g_\ast^{BJ}$, whereas it diverges as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above. We show that the two limiting ground states on either side of $g_\ast^{BJ}$ belong to distinct superselection sectors. Furthermore, as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above, the ground state localizes on a submanifold (of codimension 2) of the gauge configuration space, with the spin and color of its glue components becoming locked.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically studies quantum phase transitions in an SU(2) matrix model with massless fundamental quarks at weak coupling, identifying sector-dependent localization-delocalization transitions governed by Pauli-Gürsey symmetry; transitions are singular, involve divergence of Tr(A_i A_i), and separate superselection sectors with emergent spin-color locking on a codimension-2 submanifold.
AI.motivation: To understand non-perturbative quantum phase structure in a simplified yet physically relevant gauge–matter matrix model, particularly how global symmetries (SU(2)_B) and quark-glue interactions drive localization-delocalization transitions in the weak-coupling regime.
AI.method: Numerical investigation of the SU(2) matrix model with one massless fundamental quark flavor; analysis of ground-state localization probability, expectation value of Tr(A_i A_i), and symmetry-sector-resolved quantum phase behavior across varying coupling g; identification of critical couplings g_*^{BJ} and characterization of ground-state support and superselection structure.
AI.result: Sector-dependent localization-delocalization quantum phase transitions occur at critical couplings g_*^{BJ}; ground states shift from localized near A_i = 0 (g < g_*^{BJ}) to expelled from that region (g > g_*^{BJ}); Tr(A_i A_i) diverges as g → g_*^{BJ}+, signaling singularity; the two sides belong to distinct superselection sectors; for g > g_*^{BJ}, ground states localize on a codimension-2 submanifold with locked spin and color of glue components.
AI.conclusion: Quark-glue interactions are essential for these symmetry-sector-resolved quantum phase transitions; the singular nature and superselection separation imply a fundamental reorganization of the Hilbert space structure at g_*^{BJ}, with emergent geometric and dynamical constraints (spin-color locking) in the delocalized phase.

title: New traversable wormholes without invoking exotic matter in $f(Q)$ from the freedom of different connections
summary: Wormhole solutions in General Relativity can only exist in the presence of exotic matter that violates the null energy condition. In this paper, we investigate the possibility of constructing wormhole solutions in $f(Q)$ gravity in which the extra connection degrees of freedom contribute such that no exotic matter is needed. Considering the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole as an example, we find that the system admits two families of connections consistent with the spacetime symmetries and the requirements of symmetric teleparallel gravity. For both families, we show that constant non-metricity scalar $Q$ is not merely a simplifying assumption but arises naturally from the field equations when $f_{QQ}$ is regular, and that the resulting exact analytic solutions can satisfy the null energy condition throughout the entire spacetime. For the second family, which possesses richer connection degrees of freedom, we further demonstrate that solutions with a spatially varying $Q$ exist when $f_{QQ}$ is allowed to diverge at a finite value of $Q$, and that these too can satisfy the null energy condition everywhere. Our results show that the nontrivial connection degrees of freedom in $f(Q)$ gravity can naturally be responsible for supporting wormhole geometries, without resorting to any exotic matter.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that wormhole solutions in $f(Q)$ symmetric teleparallel gravity can satisfy the null energy condition everywhere, eliminating the need for exotic matter—unlike in General Relativity—by leveraging nontrivial connection degrees of freedom that generate effective geometric support.
AI.motivation: To circumvent the necessity of exotic matter (violating the null energy condition) for wormholes in General Relativity by exploring whether the extra geometric degrees of freedom in $f(Q)$ gravity—specifically the non-metricity scalar $Q$ and associated connection structure—can intrinsically sustain traversable wormholes.
AI.method: Analyzes the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole metric in $f(Q)$ gravity; classifies all symmetry-compatible affine connections under symmetric teleparallelism; solves the full field equations analytically; examines conditions under which $Q = \text{const}$ arises naturally or when spatially varying $Q$ is admissible (requiring divergence of $f_{QQ}$); verifies energy conditions via effective stress-energy components derived from the geometry.
AI.result: Two families of symmetric teleparallel connections are identified. For both, constant $Q$ emerges naturally (when $f_{QQ}$ is regular), yielding exact analytic wormhole solutions satisfying the null energy condition globally. The second family admits spatially varying $Q$ when $f_{QQ} \to \infty$ at finite $Q$, and such solutions also obey the null energy condition everywhere.
AI.conclusion: The nontrivial connection degrees of freedom in $f(Q)$ gravity—encoded in the non-metricity geometry—can fully replace exotic matter as the supporting mechanism for wormholes, making them viable within classical, energy-condition-respecting frameworks.

title: Hidden wormholes from an action principle in $D=4$
summary: We present new black hole solutions for the class of gravitational effective field theories in four spacetime dimensions that extend General Relativity while retaining the graviton as the only degree of freedom of gravitational origin. We consider terms up to cubic order in curvature, solve the resulting field equations, and find one-way hidden wormholes as numerical solutions: these are regular black holes with an interior wormhole throat that is crossable in one direction and leads to a cosmological spacetime in its interior. They are regular and have no inner horizon, thus evading the mass inflation instability that afflicts conventional regular black hole geometries.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs new regular black hole solutions in curvature-cubic gravitational effective field theories (EFTs) that retain only the graviton, revealing one-way hidden wormholes—regular, horizonless interiors connecting to cosmological spacetimes and avoiding mass inflation.
AI.motivation: To resolve pathologies of conventional regular black holes (e.g., inner horizons and mass inflation instability) by exploring higher-curvature EFTs that preserve unitarity and low-energy GR consistency.
AI.method: Constructs gravitational effective field theory up to cubic curvature invariants in four dimensions; solves the resulting higher-derivative field equations numerically to obtain static, spherically symmetric black hole solutions.
AI.result: Finds novel numerical black hole solutions featuring a regular, traversable (one-way) wormhole throat in the interior, connecting to a cosmological spacetime; absence of inner horizons ensures regularity and evasion of mass inflation.
AI.conclusion: Higher-curvature EFTs admit physically viable, singularity- and instability-free black hole geometries with hidden cosmological interiors—suggesting new avenues for quantum gravity phenomenology and black hole information puzzles.

title: Cyclic Boson Stars with Quantum Vortex Molecules
summary: We find a new type of stationary boson star with cyclic rotational symmetry in the minimal model of complex scalar field coupled to gravity. Unlike conventional axisymmetric spinning boson stars, these configurations can carry noninteger angular momentum per particle in units of the reduced Planck constant, revealing a new way for boson stars to carry angular momentum. We identify the vortex assemblies within these stars as self-gravitating quantum vortex molecules, in which gravity supports a stationary vortex arrangement despite internal circulation. These structures provide a relativistic realization of quantum vortex molecules studied in condensates and motivate possible laboratory analogues.

AI.tldr: Introduces a new class of stationary boson stars with cyclic rotational symmetry, carrying noninteger angular momentum per particle; identifies internal vortex structures as self-gravitating 'quantum vortex molecules'.
AI.motivation: To explore novel angular momentum configurations in boson stars beyond conventional axisymmetric spinning solutions, and to bridge relativistic gravitating systems with quantum vortex physics in condensed matter.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis within general relativity coupled to a complex scalar field (minimal model), constructing stationary solutions with cyclic (discrete rotational) symmetry and examining their angular momentum quantization and internal vortex structure.
AI.result: Discovery of stationary boson star solutions with cyclic symmetry that carry fractional (noninteger) angular momentum per particle; identification of stable, self-gravitating quantum vortex molecules—vortex assemblies held stationary by gravity despite internal circulation.
AI.conclusion: Cyclic-symmetric boson stars represent a new category of compact objects with exotic angular momentum properties; their internal quantum vortex molecules offer a relativistic analogue to condensed-matter vortex molecules and suggest pathways for laboratory analogues.

title: Gravitational Mode Instabilities in Kerr-like Black Holes
comment: v1: 8+6 pages (main text + Supplemental Material), 6 figures, 1 table
summary: We identify exponentially growing modes of a homogeneous gravitational Teukolsky-like operator on highly spinning Kerr-like black holes subject to quasinormal mode boundary conditions. Specifically, we compute electromagnetic and gravitational quasinormal modes of a spacetime proposed by Konoplya, Rezzolla, and Zhidenko that parametrizes deformations from the Kerr geometry, including configurations with black hole spin parameter $a/M > 1$ that retain an event horizon. Using the continued fraction method, we find that the spin-weight $s=-2$ operator develops exponentially growing modes when the black hole spin and deformation parameters are sufficiently large, while the electromagnetic modes remain damped throughout the parameter space. We further compare the quasinormal mode predictions with an agnostic analysis of the GW250114 ringdown, identifying regions of the parameter space that are compatible with the spectrum inferred from the data.

AI.tldr: The paper identifies exponentially growing quasinormal modes (QNMs) in highly spinning, deformed Kerr-like black holes using a Teukolsky-like operator; gravitational ($s = -2$) modes become unstable for large spin and deformation, while electromagnetic modes remain stable; results are compared to GW250114 ringdown data.
AI.motivation: To investigate stability of highly spinning, non-Kerr black hole geometries—particularly those with $a/M > 1$ yet retaining horizons—and assess viability of such models against gravitational-wave ringdown observations.
AI.method: Numerical computation of quasinormal modes using the continued fraction method applied to the gravitational and electromagnetic Teukolsky equations on the Konoplya–Rezzolla–Zhidenko (KRZ) spacetime, a parametric deformation of Kerr geometry.
AI.result: Exponentially growing (unstable) gravitational QNMs appear for sufficiently large spin and KRZ deformation parameters; electromagnetic QNMs remain damped across the explored parameter space; subsets of the parameter space are consistent with the observed spectrum of GW250114.
AI.conclusion: Highly deformed, ultra-spinning black hole models can exhibit gravitational instabilities incompatible with linear stability assumptions; however, certain regions remain observationally viable per current ringdown data, highlighting the need for precise QNM spectroscopy to constrain deviations from Kerr.

title: Binary black-hole mergers with ultralight vector bosons
comment: 13 pages, 7 figures, 1 table; main text: 5 pages, 3 figures. Supplemental Material included
summary: We simulate the inspiral, merger, and ringdown of equal-mass, nonspinning binary black holes coupled to a massive vector (Proca) field. Starting from constraint-consistent electric-field initial data, we find that the Proca field rapidly concentrates around the black holes. However, it continues to exhibit nontrivial dynamics. Orbital evolution depends on vector mass, while the dominant gravitational waveforms remain close to vacuum after time, phase, and amplitude alignment. This contrast highlights the limited imprint of the field on aligned merger-ringdown morphology at these resolutions.

AI.tldr: This paper simulates binary black hole mergers coupled to a massive vector (Proca) field, finding that while the field dynamically concentrates around the holes and affects orbital evolution, its imprint on dominant gravitational waveforms is minimal after alignment.
AI.motivation: To investigate how a massive vector (Proca) field modifies binary black hole dynamics and gravitational wave emission, particularly testing deviations from vacuum general relativity predictions.
AI.method: Numerical relativity simulations of equal-mass, nonspinning binary black holes coupled to a Proca field, starting from constraint-consistent electric-field initial data.
AI.result: The Proca field rapidly localizes near the black holes but remains dynamically active; orbital evolution depends on the vector mass, whereas dominant gravitational waveforms closely resemble vacuum GR waveforms after time, phase, and amplitude alignment.
AI.conclusion: At current numerical resolutions, the Proca field leaves only a limited imprint on the aligned merger–ringdown gravitational waveform morphology, despite influencing orbital dynamics.

title: Self-gravitating Lee-Huang-Yang fluids as dark matter halos
summary: We propose a model of dark matter halos based on a self-gravitating Bose fluid whose effective equation of state is dominated by Lee-Huang-Yang quantum fluctuations. The model is governed by coupled generalized Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson equations, which incorporate quantum pressure, Lee-Huang-Yang-induced repulsion, and gravitational attraction. By retaining the full quantum pressure, we examine the halo structure from its central region to its asymptotic regime. We first derive the Jeans dispersion relation and analyze how the Lee-Huang-Yang fluctuations alter the gravitational instability criterion and the associated characteristic length and mass scales. We then obtain analytical expressions for the central and large-radius behaviors of the equilibrium solutions. To verify the validity and the performance of the model, we fit the model-predicted curves with a sample of 20 galaxies from the SPARC database and compare the results with those obtained from Navarro-Frenk-White, standard Bose-Einstein condensate, and quantum-droplet dark matter models. We find that the pure-LHY model reproduces a broad range of observed galactic kinematics, yielding reduced $\chi^2$ values and a lower sample average compared to the aforementioned models. These results indicate that the combined effects of quantum pressure, LHY quantum fluctuations and the self-gravity provide additional flexibility in describing both the central and extended outer regions of galactic halos. We also discuss the implications of the inferred halo parameters and emphasize their dependence on the assumed effective equation of state and its microscopic interpretation. The pure-LHY model constitutes an ideal platform for exploring the role of quantum-fluctuation-induced interaction in the formation and structure of dark matter halos.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a dark matter halo model based on a self-gravitating Bose fluid where Lee-Huang-Yang (LHY) quantum fluctuations dominate the equation of state; it uses generalized Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson equations, derives analytical halo profiles, and shows superior fits to SPARC galaxy rotation curves compared to NFW, standard BEC, and quantum-droplet models.
AI.motivation: To develop a physically motivated dark matter halo model that incorporates beyond-mean-field quantum effects—specifically Lee-Huang-Yang (LHY) fluctuations—to simultaneously explain both central density cores and extended halo profiles, overcoming limitations of standard BEC and CDM models.
AI.method: Formulates a self-gravitating Bose fluid model governed by coupled generalized Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson equations including full quantum pressure and LHY-induced repulsion; derives the Jeans dispersion relation, analyzes stability and characteristic scales, obtains analytical asymptotic and central solutions, and performs χ² fitting to rotation curve data from 20 SPARC galaxies.
AI.result: The pure-LHY model yields significantly lower reduced χ² values (and lower sample-averaged χ²) than NFW, standard BEC, and quantum-droplet models across the SPARC sample; it successfully reproduces diverse galactic kinematics with a single physically grounded equation of state.
AI.conclusion: LHY quantum fluctuations provide essential additional degrees of freedom in the effective equation of state, enabling flexible, accurate modeling of halo structure from center to outskirts; the pure-LHY model is a robust and interpretable framework for quantum-fluctuation-driven dark matter halo formation.

title: Finite-wavelength corrections to dynamical friction in fuzzy dark matter: a causal linear-response approach
summary: A massive body moving through fuzzy dark matter (FDM) generates a density wake whose gravitational backreaction produces dynamical friction. We investigate how finite-wavelength effects modify this force using causal linear-response theory and the statistical Wigner formulation. For a homogeneous Maxwellian background and general isotropic finite-size perturbers, we derive an analytic representation of the gravitational drag and recover the classical Chandrasekhar result under matched regularization conditions. In the controlled semiclassical regime, the leading finite-wavelength correction is quadratic in $\hbar/m_\chi$ and factorizes into a velocity-dependent function and a ratio of spectral moments characterizing the source structure. Remarkably, this correction reduces the drag magnitude independently of the detailed radial source profile within the adopted Maxwellian model. Gaussian and exponential sources illustrate this result. We further establish a controlled remainder bound and clarify the nonuniform behavior of the point-source limit. These findings identify the physical conditions under which wave effects modify classical dynamical friction.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how finite-wavelength (quantum) effects in fuzzy dark matter modify dynamical friction on massive perturbers, deriving an analytic correction to the Chandrasekhar drag that is quadratic in ℏ/m_χ and universally reduces drag magnitude for isotropic sources in a Maxwellian background.
