AI.motivation: To understand how wave-like (quantum) properties of fuzzy dark matter—specifically its finite de Broglie wavelength—affect dynamical friction, which is traditionally treated classically via Chandrasekhar's formalism.
AI.method: Uses causal linear-response theory and the statistical Wigner formulation to model FDM as a quantum scalar field; derives gravitational drag analytically for homogeneous Maxwellian backgrounds and general isotropic finite-size perturbers; employs semiclassical expansion and spectral moment analysis.
AI.result: Derives a leading finite-wavelength correction to dynamical friction that is O((ℏ/m_χ)²), factorizes into velocity-dependent and source-structure-dependent parts, and universally reduces drag magnitude regardless of radial source profile (e.g., Gaussian or exponential); establishes remainder bounds and clarifies breakdown of point-source limit.
AI.conclusion: Wave effects in FDM systematically suppress classical dynamical friction under controlled semiclassical conditions, with implications for structure formation, satellite galaxy dynamics, and observational tests of ultralight dark matter.

title: Gravitational waves from cosmological first-order phase transitions with fluctuation-induced friction
summary: We study gravitational-wave production in a cosmological first-order phase transition with fluctuation-induced friction using three-dimensional lattice simulations of two coupled scalar fields. Kinetic and gradient energy in the additional field $s$ accumulates near the expanding bubble walls of $\phi$ and affects their motion. The contribution from $s$ exceeds that from $\phi$ at the spectral peak and has a slope similar to that of the bulk flow model over a finite interval above the peak. In the high-wave-number (UV) direction, $\phi$ dominates and the total spectrum develops a broad feature. For the larger coupling, slowly contracting false vacuum remnants persist long after bubble merger.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates gravitational-wave (GW) production during cosmological first-order phase transitions using 3D lattice simulations of two coupled scalar fields (φ and s), revealing that the auxiliary field s dominates GW emission at the spectral peak and introduces distinct features in the GW spectrum, including UV dominance by φ and long-lived false-vacuum remnants for strong coupling.
AI.motivation: To understand the gravitational-wave signature of cosmological first-order phase transitions beyond standard bulk-flow or envelope approximations, particularly when additional scalar degrees of freedom introduce fluctuation-induced friction and modify bubble dynamics.
AI.method: Three-dimensional lattice simulations of two coupled scalar fields (φ and s), where φ drives the phase transition and s accumulates kinetic/gradient energy near expanding bubble walls; spectral analysis of the resulting gravitational-wave power spectrum.
AI.result: The s-field contributes more than φ to the GW spectrum at the peak frequency, with a spectral slope matching the bulk-flow model over a finite range above the peak; at high wave numbers (UV), φ dominates, producing a broad spectral feature; for larger coupling, false-vacuum remnants undergo slow contraction and persist long after bubble merger.
AI.conclusion: Fluctuation-induced friction from an auxiliary scalar field qualitatively alters gravitational-wave production in first-order phase transitions—enhancing low-frequency emission, modifying spectral shape, and inducing long-lived non-equilibrium structures, implying that multi-field dynamics must be accounted for in GW forecasts from early-universe phase transitions.

title: What makes the gravito-thermodynamic arrow of time coincide with that of proper time?
summary: In the pursuit of a geometrical resolution to this important question for the evolution of spherically symmetric perfect fluids in general relativity, we excavated a novel result: the presence of volume distortions and inhomogeneities are, though necessary, but not sufficient for the total gravitational entropy to monotonically increase with proper time. We need a further refinement of the space of distortions and only those that favour shell crossing caustics, causing local flocculations and structure formations, can ensure the alignment. This result will have far reaching consequences for the study of thermodynamical viability of various gravitational collapse and cosmological solutions of Einstein field equations.

AI.tldr: The paper identifies that volume distortions and inhomogeneities alone are insufficient for monotonic gravitational entropy growth in spherically symmetric perfect fluid collapse; only distortions inducing shell-crossing caustics—and thus local structure formation—guarantee monotonic entropy increase.
AI.motivation: To resolve the geometrical conditions under which gravitational entropy monotonically increases during relativistic spherical collapse, addressing a key thermodynamic consistency issue in general relativity.
AI.method: Geometrical analysis of spherically symmetric perfect fluid solutions in general relativity, focusing on volume distortions, inhomogeneity, and their causal relationship with shell-crossing caustics and local flocculation.
AI.result: Volume distortions and inhomogeneities are necessary but not sufficient for monotonic gravitational entropy growth; only those distortions that generate shell-crossing caustics—and thereby drive local structure formation—ensure proper-time monotonicity of total gravitational entropy.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational entropy alignment with cosmic evolution requires not just generic inhomogeneity, but specifically caustic-forming geometric distortions—a refined criterion with implications for viability assessments of collapse models and cosmological solutions.

title: Gravitational Light Deflection via Fractional Calculus and Chebyshev Polynomial Approximation
summary: We develop a fractional-calculus-based framework for evaluating gravitational light deflection in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes. By introducing a suitable transformation of the radial coordinate, the deflection integral is recast into an Abel-type integral equation, from which the associated kernel is reconstructed using fractional integration. The leading singular behaviour near the photon sphere is isolated analytically, and the remaining regular part is approximated by a finite Chebyshev polynomial expansion. This combination retains the correct strong-field behaviour while providing an efficient numerical representation of the deflection integral. We demonstrate the accuracy of the method using the Schwarzschild spacetime as a benchmark and compare the resulting deflection angles with the standard strong-deflection approximation and a two-term weak-deflection expansion. We further apply the method to calculate strong-field lensing observables, including the limiting angular position, angular separation, and relative magnification of relativistic images, for the supermassive black holes Sgr A*. The results show that the proposed approach provides an accurate and flexible means of evaluating gravitational deflection angles across a broad range of closest-approach radii. The framework can be extended to other static, spherically symmetric black-hole geometries, including solutions arising in modified theories of gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a fractional-calculus-based method to compute gravitational light deflection in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes—especially in the strong-field regime—by reformulating the deflection integral as an Abel-type equation, isolating photon-sphere singularities analytically, and approximating the regular part via Chebyshev polynomials; it achieves high accuracy for Schwarzschild and Sgr A*, and is generalizable to modified gravity black-hole metrics.
AI.motivation: To overcome numerical inaccuracies and inefficiencies in evaluating gravitational light deflection near the photon sphere in strong-field lensing, especially for arbitrary static, spherically symmetric spacetimes where standard weak- or strong-deflection approximations fail or lack flexibility.
AI.method: Transforms the radial coordinate to recast the deflection integral into an Abel-type integral equation; reconstructs its kernel using fractional integration; analytically isolates the leading singular behaviour near the photon sphere; approximates the remaining regular part with a finite Chebyshev polynomial expansion.
AI.result: High-accuracy deflection angles across wide ranges of closest-approach radii; validated against Schwarzschild benchmark, standard strong-deflection approximation, and weak-deflection expansion; successfully computes relativistic image observables (limiting angular position, angular separation, relative magnification) for Sgr A*.
AI.conclusion: The fractional-calculus framework provides an accurate, efficient, and extendable method for strong-field gravitational lensing calculations in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes—including those from modified gravity theories.

title: Geometric optics for gravitational waves in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity: amplitude birefringence and tensor-scalar mixing on general backgrounds
summary: We study the propagation of high-frequency gravitational waves in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity within the geometric optics approximation. In contrast to previous work, we allow for a general background with a nonvanishing scalar field, which enables a covariant treatment of amplitude birefringence. The background scalar gradient introduces third-derivative terms into the linearized field equations. These must be treated as subleading for the linearized system to be free of ghosts, which yields a covariant upper bound on the frequency. Tensor-scalar mixing is induced by the Weyl curvature through the Newman-Penrose scalar $\Psi_0$ along the ray. When the mixing is efficient, the propagation eigenmodes consist of one luminal, one subluminal, and one superluminal mode, and a violation of the ghost-free condition leads to a classical instability. From the transport equations at next-to-leading order, we show that, when the mixing is negligible, the relative amplitude of the two helicities depends only on the scalar-field gradients along the ray at the emission and observation events, independently of the path in between.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes high-frequency gravitational wave propagation in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity using geometric optics, introducing a covariant treatment of amplitude birefringence via a nontrivial scalar background; it derives a frequency upper bound to avoid ghosts, identifies tensor-scalar mixing mediated by the Weyl scalar Ψ₀, characterizes three propagation eigenmodes (luminal, subluminal, superluminal) under strong mixing, and shows that helicity amplitude ratios depend only on scalar gradients at emission and detection when mixing is negligible.
AI.motivation: To extend gravitational wave propagation analysis in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity beyond vacuum or constant-scalar backgrounds, enabling a fully covariant treatment of amplitude birefringence and ghost constraints in realistic, nontrivial scalar field environments.
AI.method: Geometric optics approximation applied to linearized gravitational and scalar perturbations on a general curved background with nonvanishing scalar field; derivation and analysis of third-derivative terms in field equations; classification of propagation eigenmodes via dispersion relations; transport equation analysis at next-to-leading order for amplitude evolution.
AI.result: A covariant upper bound on gravitational wave frequency arises from requiring absence of ghosts due to third-derivative terms; tensor-scalar mixing is governed by the Newman-Penrose scalar Ψ₀; efficient mixing yields three distinct propagation modes (luminal, subluminal, superluminal), with ghost violation causing classical instability; in the weak-mixing limit, helicity amplitude ratio depends solely on scalar-field gradients at source and observer, path-independent.
AI.conclusion: Amplitude birefringence in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity is fundamentally controlled by scalar-field gradients at boundary events—not the intervening geometry—when tensor-scalar mixing is suppressed; however, generic backgrounds with strong curvature and scalar variation induce rich mode structure and impose strict high-frequency cutoffs to preserve theoretical consistency.

title: Shadows and Images of Black Holes with Purely Nonlinear Scalarization
summary: We investigate the shadows and radiative images of static, spherically symmetric black holes with purely nonlinear scalarization in Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet gravity. The quartic exponential coupling supports scalarized backgrounds without a linear tachyonic instability of Schwarzschild black holes. We compare mass and coupling dependences and construct images on radially stable backgrounds using optically thin spherical emission and face-on thin disks. On the sampled radially stable branches, we find smaller shadow radii than those of Schwarzschild black holes at the same mass, with reductions reaching approximately $21.7\%$. The sampled radially unstable branches show much smaller shadow-size deviations. The photon-orbit index, which measures radial instability per unit orbital angle, varies nonmonotonically even when the normalized shadow radius changes monotonically. The index also controls the asymptotic compression of higher-order images, providing information complementary to shadow size. For spherical emission, radial infall produces a darker center relative to the bright ring than static emission. For circular disks, we find that smooth metric variations can create an unstable interval separating two stable regions of timelike circular motion. When the disk occupies the stable region connected to infinity, its inner edge moves outward across this transition, suppressing emission inside the geometric shadow boundary while the normalized shadow radius changes only slightly. Our results show that purely nonlinear scalarization can alter images through both photon propagation and the orbital structure of emitting matter, with the visible features depending on the emission model.

AI.tldr: This paper studies black hole shadows and radiative images in Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity with purely nonlinear scalarization, finding reduced shadow sizes (up to ~21.7%) on radially stable branches, nonmonotonic photon-orbit instability behavior, and emission-model-dependent image features—including dark-center suppression for spherical infall and inner-disk edge shifts crossing stability transitions.
AI.motivation: To explore how purely nonlinear scalarization—enabled by quartic exponential coupling in Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity—affects observable black hole images and shadows, bypassing linear tachyonic instabilities while probing deviations from Schwarzschild predictions.
AI.method: Analyzes static, spherically symmetric scalarized black hole solutions; computes photon orbits and shadow boundaries; constructs radiative images using optically thin spherical emission (static and radial infall) and face-on thin accretion disks; assesses radial stability of timelike circular orbits; introduces and computes the photon-orbit index as a measure of orbital instability per unit angle.
AI.result: Radially stable scalarized black holes exhibit up to ~21.7% smaller shadow radii than Schwarzschild at same mass; radially unstable branches show negligible shadow-size deviation; photon-orbit index varies nonmonotonically despite monotonic shadow-radius trends; spherical infall yields darker centers vs. static emission; disk inner edges shift outward across stability transitions, suppressing emission inside geometric shadow while normalized shadow radius remains nearly unchanged.
AI.conclusion: Purely nonlinear scalarization modifies black hole images through both null geodesic structure (shadows, photon-orbit index) and timelike orbital dynamics (disk emission geometry), with observable signatures strongly dependent on the physical emission model—highlighting the need for joint modeling of spacetime and astrophysical accretion to interpret EHT-like observations.

title: Beyond the point lens: radial structure and the horizon in wave-optics gravitational lensing
summary: Gravitational-wave lensing in the wave-optics regime is sensitive to the structure of the lens beyond its total mass: to its exterior radial profile and, as we show, to the boundary condition at its centre. We develop an analytic framework to compute these effects for a scalar wave, as corrections to the wave lensed by a Newtonian point mass. The corrections are organized in inverse powers of the distance from the lens and computed with dressed radial kernels, which include the Newtonian interaction to all orders and resum the long-range phase that invalidates the Born expansion around the free wave. Retaining wavefront curvature, we find that the scattered wave is not the whole response: an inverse-square deformation changes the direct wave by an equal amount, even when the scattered wave is faint. Steeper terms of the exterior potential lead to short-distance divergences, which signal that the exterior geometry alone does not determine the lensed wave: the missing information is a set of local terms fixed by the inner boundary condition. For a Schwarzschild black hole we determine them by matching to the ingoing solution at the horizon. The horizon enters the amplification factor as an absorptive contact term, which reproduces the horizon-area cross section; it is absent for a non-absorbing lens of the same mass, and cannot be described by the thin-lens diffraction integral. It completes the correction quadratic in the mass, where it appears at the same order as finite-distance optical corrections, and largely cancels against them for an aligned source. Together, these results connect Newtonian dressing, diffraction and inner boundary conditions, in a systematic description of corrections to point-mass gravitational-wave lensing.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an analytic framework for gravitational-wave lensing in the wave-optics regime, going beyond the point-mass approximation by incorporating exterior radial profile effects and central boundary conditions—especially horizon absorption for Schwarzschild black holes—via dressed radial kernels and resummed phase corrections.
AI.motivation: To extend gravitational-wave lensing theory beyond the Newtonian point-mass approximation by accounting for finite-size effects, wavefront curvature, and inner boundary physics (e.g., horizon absorption), which are missed by standard thin-lens or Born-approximation treatments.
AI.method: Develops an analytic wave-optics formalism for scalar gravitational waves scattering off a spherically symmetric lens; uses dressed radial kernels to resum the long-range Newtonian phase, retains wavefront curvature, and matches asymptotic solutions to inner boundary conditions (e.g., ingoing horizon condition for Schwarzschild BH).
AI.result: Identifies that exterior potential steepness induces short-distance divergences requiring local boundary terms; for Schwarzschild BH, horizon absorption enters as an absorptive contact term in the amplification factor—reproducing the horizon-area cross section—and cancels finite-distance optical corrections at quadratic order in mass for aligned sources.
AI.conclusion: A complete description of wave-optical gravitational lensing requires joint treatment of Newtonian dressing (long-range phase), diffraction (wavefront curvature), and inner boundary conditions (e.g., horizon absorption); the point-mass approximation is insufficient even for weak-field, far-field observables when high precision is needed.

title: Inflation with an Exponential Power-Law Potential:Analytical Slow-Roll Relations, Branch Dynamics, and Conditional Reheating Matching
summary: We study canonical single-field inflation driven by the potential $V(\phi)=M^4\exp(\phi/M_{\rm Pl})(1+k\phi/M_{\rm Pl})^{-1/k}$ with $k<0$. We retain the canonical Einstein--scalar action and derive analytical relations within the slow-roll approximation. Expressing the local spectra through the logarithmic slope $A=kx/(1+kx)$, with $x=\phi/M_{\rm Pl}$, yields an endpoint-independent consistency relation among the scalar tilt, tensor ratio, and running at their stated approximation orders. On the negative-field branch, an exact phase-space argument shows that an initially downhill, inflationary hilltop trajectory cannot end inflation within the bare single-field model. We specify the endpoint as a phenomenological input and use a Lambert-$W$ solution of the slow-roll e-fold integral. Tables and figures illustrate the fixed choice $x_e=-2$ and must be interpreted conditionally on a completion that implements this endpoint and preserves the adiabatic spectrum. The reheating-matching relation uses explicit scale and thermal conventions and imposes both endpoint energy bounds and nonnegative reheating duration. The observational comparison uses published marginalized intervals rather than reconstructed joint posteriors. These results establish local analytical structure and conditional numerical benchmarks. A complete exit mechanism, a unique reheating equation of state, and precision spectral predictions remain unestablished.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes a specific exponential-scaled inflationary potential with a negative parameter k, deriving analytical slow-roll predictions for spectral indices and tensor-to-scalar ratio; it identifies an inherent incompleteness in the single-field model’s ability to end inflation on the negative-field branch and emphasizes conditional numerical benchmarks pending UV completion and reheating specification.
AI.motivation: To establish analytically tractable, endpoint-independent consistency relations among inflationary observables (ns, r, αs) for a class of potentials that generalize hilltop inflation while retaining canonical kinetic term and Einstein gravity.
AI.method: Analytical slow-roll analysis using logarithmic slope parametrization A = kx/(1 + kx); exact phase-space argument to prove impossibility of graceful exit within bare model; Lambert-W function solution for e-fold integral; reheating-matching via explicit scale/thermal conventions; comparison to published marginalized likelihood intervals.
AI.result: Derivation of an endpoint-independent consistency relation linking ns, r, and αs at leading slow-roll order; proof that inflation cannot self-terminate on the negative-field branch without external completion; numerical benchmarks (tables/figures) conditional on fixed field endpoint xe = −2; reheating constraints yielding energy bounds and nonnegative duration.
AI.conclusion: The potential supports well-defined local inflationary dynamics and yields robust analytical structure, but a physically complete description—requiring a UV completion for termination, unique reheating equation of state, and precision spectral predictions—remains open.

title: Gravitational Waves Population Study for Testing Kerr Hypothesis: Are Non-Kerr Deformations Universal or Source-Dependent?
summary: Gravitational-wave observations of binary black hole mergers can test the Kerr black hole hypothesis in the strong-field and dynamical regime. In our previous works, we constrained the deformation parameters $\alpha_{13}$ and $\epsilon_3$ of the Johannsen metric using individual inspiral-dominated events from GWTC-3 and GWTC-4 and found no evidence of deviations from the Kerr solution. Here we combine 17 of these events to test whether black holes are Kerr, share a common non-zero deformation, or have deformations that vary from source to source. We first estimate the Savage--Dickey Bayes factor of each event, and we test how it depends on the prior range and on the removal of single events. We then combine the event likelihoods assuming a universal deformation, yielding a tighter joint constraint. Next, we perform a simple hierarchical analysis by assuming that the event-level deformation parameters are drawn from a population with mean $\mu$ and intrinsic scatter $\sigma$. A universal deformation is constrained to $\alpha_{13}=-0.01^{+0.14}_{-0.12}$ and $\epsilon_3=0.06^{+0.59}_{-0.54}$. The means from the population are consistent with zero for both parameters, and the scatter is not resolved by the current data. Our results are consistent with the Kerr hypothesis, but they cannot yet distinguish a shared deformation from a source-dependent one.

AI.tldr: This paper combines 17 gravitational-wave binary black hole events from GWTC-3 and GWTC-4 to test the Kerr black hole hypothesis by constraining deformation parameters α₁₃ and ε₃ of the Johannsen metric; it finds no statistically significant deviation from Kerr, with joint constraints α₁₃ = −0.01⁺⁰·¹⁴₋₀·₁₂ and ε₃ = 0.06⁺⁰·⁵⁹₋₀·₅₄, and hierarchical modeling shows population mean consistent with zero and unresolved intrinsic scatter.
AI.motivation: To test the Kerr black hole hypothesis in the strong-field, dynamical regime using gravitational-wave observations, specifically by probing whether observed black holes exhibit universal or source-dependent deviations from the Kerr metric via the Johannsen metric deformation parameters α₁₃ and ε₃.
AI.method: Combined likelihoods of 17 inspiral-dominated binary black hole events; computed Savage–Dickey Bayes factors per event and assessed their robustness to prior range and event removal; performed joint inference assuming a universal deformation; conducted hierarchical Bayesian analysis modeling event-level deformations as drawn from a Gaussian population with mean μ and intrinsic scatter σ.
AI.result: Universal deformation constraints: α₁₃ = −0.01⁺⁰·¹⁴₋₀·₁₂, ε₃ = 0.06⁺⁰·⁵⁹₋₀·₅₄ (90% credible intervals); population means μ_α₁₃ and μ_ε₃ consistent with zero; intrinsic scatter σ not resolved; Bayes factors show no evidence for deviation from Kerr, but cannot yet distinguish universal vs. source-dependent deformations.
AI.conclusion: Current data are consistent with the Kerr hypothesis; however, they lack the statistical power to discriminate between a universal non-zero deformation and source-dependent deformations — improved sensitivity and more events are needed for definitive tests.

title: The additive ambiguity of gravitational entropy fixed by the topology of the horizon
summary: In quantum gravity the algebra of observables of a subregion is of type III$_1$ at leading order in the semiclassical expansion, and it becomes of type II once the gravitational constraint is imposed. Hence generalized entropy acquires a trace, however it is defined only up to an additive constant. In this work we argue that in four-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity this constant is the Gauss--Bonnet contribution to the Wald entropy, and that it is carried by the normalization of the trace and not by the state. In particular, the conical expansion of the Gauss--Bonnet density is exactly linear in the deficit angle, and on smooth squashed cones it reduces to the intrinsic curvature of the cut, so that the term is a constant on every smooth cross-section and carries no boost energy. Its Noether charge is invariant under all deformations within a topological sector and central in any algebra that preserves the sector, and thus a state-independent constant on such an algebra can only rescale the trace. Additionally, when the boundary of the subregion is completed as the Euler action requires, the Gauss--Bonnet term does not contribute to the presymplectic form, the crossed product is inherited from Einstein gravity, and the constant is the Euler number of the excised Euclidean tip. We state the hypotheses, we weaken factoriality to a central decomposition, and we illustrate the mechanism in Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity and in topological black holes in anti-de Sitter space, where the topological weight displaces the Hawking--Page temperature and a black-hole merger shifts the coarse-grained boundary entropy by a state-independent amount.

AI.tldr: This paper argues that in 4D Einstein–Gauss–Bonnet gravity, the additive constant ambiguity in generalized entropy arises from the Gauss–Bonnet contribution to Wald entropy, which is trace-normalization–dependent—not state-dependent—and topologically fixed (e.g., Euler number of Euclidean tip); it demonstrates this via conical geometry, Noether charge centrality, and presymplectic invariance, with illustrations in JT gravity and AdS topological black holes.
AI.motivation: To resolve the state-independent additive ambiguity in generalized entropy arising from type III → II algebra transition in semiclassical quantum gravity, specifically identifying the physical origin of the constant in Gauss–Bonnet gravity.
AI.method: Analyzes the conical expansion of the Gauss–Bonnet density, computes its Noether charge and presymplectic contribution, examines trace normalization under crossed-product von Neumann algebras, invokes topological completion (Euler action), and verifies consistency in lower-dimensional (JT) and AdS topological black hole models.
AI.result: The Gauss–Bonnet term contributes a state-independent constant to generalized entropy—equal to its Wald entropy contribution—carried solely by the trace normalization; on smooth squashed cones it reduces to intrinsic curvature of the cut, its Noether charge is topologically invariant and central, and with Euler-completed boundary it decouples from the presymplectic form, yielding the Euler number of the excised Euclidean tip as the constant.
AI.conclusion: The additive constant in generalized entropy for Gauss–Bonnet gravity is topological and algebraic (trace-normalization–driven), not thermodynamic or state-dependent; this reconciles type II algebra structure with Wald entropy and extends to topological sectors in JT and AdS black holes.

title: \texttt{StochAXtic}: a JAX-Accelerated, End-to-End Differentiable Framework for Gravitational-Wave Backgrounds from Compact Binary Populations
summary: We present \texttt{StochAXtic}, a package for computing the dimensionless energy density spectrum $\Omega_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ of the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by compact binary coalescences. Rather than sampling binary populations via Monte Carlo, \texttt{StochAXtic} exploits the \emph{scale invariance} of the waveforms: at fixed mass ratio, spins and tidal deformabilities, the waveform depends on the total mass only through the dimensionless combination $Mf$. This allows all computationally expensive waveform evaluations using \texttt{LALSuite} to be performed once and stored in a population-independent lookup table. The subsequent integrals over mass and redshift can then be recast as convolutions and evaluated efficiently using fast Fourier transforms. We further employ truncated singular value decomposition to compress the lookup table, reducing both computational cost and memory requirements. Once the table has been computed and cached, \texttt{StochAXtic} evaluates $\Omega_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ in a few milliseconds, achieving a relative numerical error below $10^{-3}$ at frequencies up to $1$ kHz. Its results agree with those of \texttt{popstock} within the latter's statistical uncertainties. Implemented entirely in \texttt{JAX}, \texttt{StochAXtic} also provides gradients of $\Omega_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ with respect to population hyperparameters, enabling its direct integration with gradient-based inference methods including Hamiltonian Monte Carlo.

AI.tldr: StochAXtic is a JAX-based package that efficiently computes the stochastic gravitational-wave background energy density spectrum Ω_GW(f) from compact binary coalescences by leveraging waveform scale invariance, FFT-accelerated convolution, and SVD-based lookup table compression—enabling millisecond evaluations with <10⁻³ error and native gradient support for inference.
AI.motivation: To overcome computational bottlenecks in Monte Carlo–based population synthesis (e.g., popstock) for predicting the stochastic gravitational-wave background Ω_GW(f), especially for gradient-driven Bayesian inference.
AI.method: Exploits scale invariance of GW waveforms (Mf scaling at fixed q, spins, tides); precomputes and caches LALSuite waveforms in a population-independent lookup table; reformulates mass/redshift integrals as convolutions computed via FFT; applies truncated SVD to compress the table; implements fully in JAX for automatic differentiation.
AI.result: Ω_GW(f) evaluation in milliseconds (<10⁻³ relative error up to 1 kHz); agreement with popstock within its statistical uncertainties; gradients w.r.t. population hyperparameters enabled; reduced memory and compute cost via SVD compression.
AI.conclusion: StochAXtic provides a fast, accurate, differentiable, and scalable alternative to Monte Carlo sampling for computing Ω_GW(f), facilitating its use in hierarchical inference pipelines for LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA and future detectors.

title: Convergence of the quasinormal-mode expansion of the Kerr Green function
summary: Black-hole ringdown is usually modeled as a linear superposition of quasinormal modes, and fits to gravitational-wave observations increasingly include high overtones. However, the overtone sum does not necessarily converge: overtones are more strongly damped and thus decay faster in time, but their amplitudes in the Green function (the signal at an observer produced by an impulse at a source point) grow, so the mode description may break down before a finite time. We show that for a rotating (Kerr) black hole this time has a clear geometric meaning. For highly damped modes, the amplitudes grow exponentially with the optical distance from the source and the observer to a characteristic "bounce" radius close to the black hole, defined as the location where the mode amplitude is smallest. For one family of modes, the amplitudes are also suppressed the farther the source and observer sit from the equatorial plane. Rotation therefore makes the onset of convergence depend on direction as well as distance, extending the geometric picture from bounce radii to bounce surfaces. Combining these effects gives a sufficient condition for absolute convergence. For spin $a/M = 0.7$, we map how this time varies with source and observer position, and amplitudes computed numerically reproduce the predicted spatial dependence to better than one percent. These results set geometric limits on when the quasinormal-mode sums converge.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the convergence of quasinormal mode (QNM) sums in black-hole ringdown modeling, showing that for Kerr black holes, the convergence time has a geometric interpretation tied to optical distance to a 'bounce radius' near the horizon; rotation introduces directional dependence via bounce surfaces, and numerical tests confirm the predicted spatial scaling of amplitudes to <1% accuracy.
AI.motivation: To resolve whether and when the standard linear superposition of quasinormal modes converges for rotating black holes—especially given increasing use of high overtones in gravitational-wave data analysis—and to identify geometric conditions ensuring absolute convergence.
AI.method: Analytical asymptotic analysis of highly damped quasinormal modes in the Kerr spacetime, focusing on Green function behavior; derivation of amplitude scaling with optical distance to a characteristic bounce radius and angular dependence off the equatorial plane; numerical computation of mode amplitudes for comparison.
AI.result: A geometric sufficient condition for absolute convergence of QNM sums is established: convergence holds only after a finite time determined by optical distance from source/observer to a bounce radius (and bounce surface for rotating case); for a/M = 0.7, the predicted spatial dependence of convergence time is verified numerically to within 1%.
AI.conclusion: The quasinormal-mode expansion for Kerr black hole ringdown is not globally valid in time; its applicability is fundamentally constrained by spacetime geometry—specifically, source–observer optical paths to bounce structures—implying strict geometric limits on waveform modeling in gravitational-wave inference.

title: 'Forward-backward' flows and integration cycles for semiclassical Euclidean gravity
summary: Integrating Euclidean semiclassical gravity over real Riemannian metrics is subtle due to the conformal factor problem. A perturbative prescription was given by Gibbons-Hawking-Perry (GHP) where the integration contour for the conformal perturbations is rotated to be imaginary. A potential non-perturbative remedy is that the integration cycles associated to semiclassical saddle points should be deformed into the space of complex metrics in the sense of Picard-Lefschetz theory. Here we propose a non-perturbative construction of such complex integration cycles. This employs a 'forward-backward' gradient flow of the Einstein-Hilbert action, starting at a saddle point, along which the action has monotonically increasing real part and constant imaginary part. The flow is not parabolic. In a neighbourhood of a saddle point, the real part of the conformal factor flows forward and that of the conformal class backwards, with the opposite true of their imaginary parts. Starting the flow at a saddle point, then roughly speaking, one specifies the real part of the conformal class and the imaginary part of the conformal factor at the end of the flow. Solving the flow one finds the complex metrics along a one parameter path within the integration cycle of that saddle, and varying this final data generates the integration cycle, the Lefschetz thimble of the saddle point. We find that near to a real saddle point this reproduces the GHP prescription. We characterise the neighbourhood of a saddle where such forward-backward flows may exist, finding a weaker restriction than that of Kontsevich-Segal-Witten. We numerically demonstrate flows explicitly for 4-dimensional gravity, constructing sections through the integration contours for the saddles given by Euclidean de Sitter, and for Schwarzschild in a cavity.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a non-perturbative construction of complex integration cycles (Lefschetz thimbles) for Euclidean semiclassical gravity using a 'forward-backward' gradient flow of the Einstein-Hilbert action, resolving the conformal factor problem and reproducing the Gibbons-Hawking-Perry prescription near real saddle points.
AI.motivation: To resolve the conformal factor problem in Euclidean semiclassical gravity—where integration over real Riemannian metrics is ill-defined—by providing a rigorous, non-perturbative contour deformation into the space of complex metrics, consistent with Picard-Lefschetz theory.
AI.method: Introduces a non-parabolic 'forward-backward' gradient flow of the Einstein-Hilbert action: real part of conformal factor flows forward, real part of conformal class flows backward (and vice versa for imaginary parts); constructs Lefschetz thimbles as one-parameter families of complex metrics generated by varying boundary data at flow endpoints; validates via analytic characterization near saddles and numerical implementation in 4D for Euclidean de Sitter and Schwarzschild-in-a-cavity.
AI.result: Demonstrates that the forward-backward flow yields well-defined Lefschetz thimbles; recovers the GHP prescription perturbatively near real saddles; identifies a weaker domain of validity than the Kontsevich-Segal-Witten condition; provides first explicit numerical constructions of thimble sections for physically relevant gravitational saddles.
AI.conclusion: The forward-backward gradient flow furnishes a viable non-perturbative framework for defining the gravitational path integral in Euclidean signature, offering a geometrically transparent and computationally tractable realization of Picard-Lefschetz theory in quantum gravity.

title: Cosmic Censorship in the Landscape of SUSY-Broken AdS Vacua
summary: We investigate signatures of weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric vacua of both IIA and IIB string theory. In particular, we examine the Penrose Inequality, which can be proven holographically using Ryu-Takayanagi, and can be independently proven in SUSY AdS vacua for spherically symmetric initial data. We prove that any EFT of scalars coupled to gravity in AdS, including in particular those of string compactifications, satisfies both the Penrose Inequality and a positive mass theorem if a function that we call a "weak fake superpotential" exists. We demonstrate that this condition is satisfied globally for the DGKT skew-whiffed vacua in IIA. Since there is no known nonperturbative instability in this DGKT vacuum, this provides evidence that the IIA SUSY-broken AdS vacua may be absolutely stable. We also find the weak fake superpotential exists locally in field space in some SUSY-broken AdS vacua in a KKLT construction in IIB. Thus, within the framework considered here, some false SUSY-broken KKLT AdS vacua are stable against vacuum decay. Conversely, we find that some KKLT vacua do not have a weak fake superpotential, and correspondingly violate the Penrose Inequality and fail to have a positive mass theorem; the DGKT vacua only violate the Penrose Inequality in the presence of designer gravity boundary conditions. In all cases studied, this is due to false vacuum decay. We discuss the implications of these violations for holography and black hole thermodynamics in these SUSY-broken AdS vacua.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric AdS vacua of IIA/IIB string theory via the Penrose Inequality and positive mass theorem, introducing a 'weak fake superpotential' condition that ensures stability; it is globally satisfied in DGKT IIA vacua (suggesting absolute stability) and locally in some KKLT IIB vacua, while its absence signals instability via false vacuum decay.
AI.motivation: To test weak cosmic censorship and assess stability of non-SUSY AdS vacua in string theory—particularly whether they admit consistent holographic duals and avoid pathological gravitational collapse or vacuum decay.
AI.method: Holographic derivation of the Penrose Inequality using Ryu-Takayanagi, combined with geometric analysis of scalar-gravity effective field theories in AdS; construction and verification of a 'weak fake superpotential' as a sufficient condition for both the Penrose Inequality and positive mass theorem.
AI.result: DGKT skew-whiffed IIA vacua globally satisfy the weak fake superpotential condition and hence obey both inequalities; certain KKLT IIB vacua satisfy it only locally, implying metastability, while others violate it—correlating with Penrose Inequality violation, failure of positive mass theorem, and false vacuum decay. DGKT vacua violate Penrose only under designer gravity boundary conditions.
AI.conclusion: Existence of a weak fake superpotential serves as a robust stability criterion for non-SUSY AdS vacua in string compactifications; its presence supports weak cosmic censorship and holographic consistency, while its absence signals gravitational or quantum instability, with direct implications for black hole thermodynamics and AdS/CFT in broken SUSY settings.

title: Supersymmetric warped AdS$_3$ solutions in eleven-dimensional supergravity
summary: We construct new families of supersymmetric solutions of eleven-dimensional supergravity by deforming the half-BPS $\mathrm{AdS}_3\times \mathrm{S}^3_+\times \mathrm{S}^3_-\times\mathbb R^2$ background. We consider lightlike, spacelike and timelike warpings of the anti-de Sitter factor, accompanied by deformations of the two three-spheres, and determine the supporting four-form fluxes and the constraints imposed by the equations of motion. In particular, the deformation parameters of the two spheres are necessarily equal, although their radii need not coincide. We compute the conserved charges and determine the preserved supersymmetries and Killing superalgebras. Generic lightlike solutions preserve four real supercharges, whereas spacelike and timelike solutions preserve eight, with a Killing superalgebra containing a single exceptional $\mathfrak d(2,1;\alpha)$ factor.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs new supersymmetric solutions of 11D supergravity by deforming the half-BPS AdS₃×S³₊×S³₋×ℝ² background via lightlike, spacelike, or timelike warpings of AdS₃ and concurrent deformations of the two S³ factors; it determines the associated G₄ fluxes, equations-of-motion constraints, conserved charges, and preserved supersymmetries—finding that lightlike solutions preserve 4 real supercharges, while spacelike/timelike ones preserve 8 and feature a Killing superalgebra with an exceptional d(2,1;α) factor.
AI.motivation: To extend the landscape of known supersymmetric solutions in eleven-dimensional supergravity by systematically deforming a canonical half-BPS background (AdS₃×S³₊×S³₋×ℝ²), exploring how different causal types of AdS₃ warping affect supersymmetry preservation, flux structure, and symmetry algebras.
AI.method: Systematic deformation of the half-BPS AdS₃×S³₊×S³₋×ℝ² solution using lightlike, spacelike, and timelike warpings of the AdS₃ factor, coupled with simultaneous deformations of the two three-spheres; solving the 11D supergravity equations of motion and Killing spinor equations to determine allowed four-form flux G₄, geometric constraints (e.g., equal deformation parameters for both spheres), conserved charges, and Killing superalgebras.
AI.result: New families of supersymmetric 11D supergravity solutions are obtained: lightlike-warping preserves 4 real supercharges; spacelike/timelike warpings preserve 8; the deformation parameters of the two S³s must be equal (though radii may differ); supporting G₄ flux is explicitly constructed; the Killing superalgebra for spacelike/timelike cases contains a single exceptional factor d(2,1;α).
AI.conclusion: The deformation framework yields distinct classes of supersymmetric solutions distinguished by the causal nature of the AdS₃ warping, revealing a clear dichotomy in supersymmetry enhancement (4 vs. 8 supercharges) and algebraic structure (presence of d(2,1;α)), thereby enriching the classification of BPS geometries in M-theory with product-type AdS₃ compactifications.

title: Gravity/Thermodynamics Correspondence for Generic Dynamical Spacetimes
summary: Working within covariant phase space formalism, we establish \textit{gravity-thermodynamics correspondence} for generic dynamical spacetimes. We derive local first and second laws of thermodynamics on general null boundaries, for generic non-stationary solutions to Einstein gravity {with minimally coupled matter} for physical observers that we carefully specify. Entropy variation, which receives contribution only from the gravitational sector, is the surface charge variation associated with a vector field generating the null boundary, and temperature is its non-affinity parameter (divided by $2\pi$). The statement of the second law in our setting is that the entropy variation evaluated along the null vector field is strictly non-negative for the admissible positive-non-affinity clock and matter satisfying the null energy condition. Our dynamical entropy variation, which is non-integrable for generic non-stationary solutions, becomes integrable in near-stationary configurations, reproducing the Hollands--Wald--Zhang dynamical entropy formula. Strikingly, this local second law holds even when the boundary area is decreasing, disentangling thermodynamic irreversibility and the second law from standard area theorems. Our first-principles construction demonstrates that gravitational thermodynamics requires neither a stationary background, teleological event horizons, nor an exact entropy state function on individual codimension-1 spacelike slices of the null boundary (codimension two in spacetime).

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a gravity-thermodynamics correspondence for generic dynamical spacetimes using covariant phase space formalism, deriving local first and second laws on arbitrary null boundaries without requiring stationarity, event horizons, or integrable entropy.
AI.motivation: To generalize gravitational thermodynamics beyond stationary black holes and teleological horizons, establishing robust local thermodynamic laws for arbitrary dynamical spacetimes and null boundaries.
AI.method: Covariant phase space formalism; derivation of surface charge variation as entropy; identification of temperature via non-affinity parameter of the null generator; imposition of null energy condition for second law.
AI.result: Local first and second laws hold on general null boundaries for non-stationary Einstein–matter solutions; entropy variation is non-integrable generically but reduces to Hollands–Wald–Zhang formula near stationarity; second law holds even when area decreases.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational thermodynamics is fundamentally local, observer-dependent, and does not rely on global structures like event horizons, stationarity, or integrable entropy functions—irreversibility is encoded in sign-definite entropy variation along the null flow.

title: Regular/Singular Black Hole Thermodynamics from Renormalised Volume/Area
summary: We study the finite mismatch between the holographically and topologically renormalised Euclidean actions of the four-dimensional AdS C-metric. Starting from the relation between Renormalised Volume and the Einstein sector of Conformal Gravity, we separate the regular curvature contribution from the contributions supported on the two conical axes. After introducing the usual Euler normalisation for smooth manifolds, the residual difference between the regular action evaluations is determined by the tension-weighted Euler terms of the renormalised worldsheet area. We identify this difference with the Gauss--Bonnet entropy contribution at the polar conical points of the horizon. The ordinary Euler characteristic remains fixed, while the deficits determine how its curvature representation is divided between regular and singular contributions. At fixed total string tension, the difference of the renormalised worldsheet areas per unit Euclidean time determines the relative tension work, giving a geometric interpretation of the relative thermodynamic length.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the finite mismatch between holographically and topologically renormalised Euclidean actions for the 4D AdS C-metric, attributing the difference to Gauss–Bonnet entropy contributions at polar conical horizon points and interpreting tension-weighted worldsheet area differences as thermodynamic length.
AI.motivation: To resolve and interpret the finite discrepancy between two physically motivated renormalisation schemes—holographic (AdS/CFT) and topological (Conformal Gravity)—for the Euclidean action of the AdS C-metric, particularly in the presence of conical singularities.
AI.method: Uses the relation between Renormalised Volume and the Einstein sector of Conformal Gravity; decomposes curvature contributions into regular bulk and conical-axis-supported parts; applies Euler normalisation for smooth manifolds; isolates residual action difference via tension-weighted Euler terms of renormalised worldsheet area; identifies geometric/thermodynamic interpretations.
AI.result: The finite mismatch equals the Gauss–Bonnet entropy contribution localized at polar conical points of the horizon; the ordinary Euler characteristic is preserved, but deficits redistribute curvature between regular and singular parts; at fixed total string tension, the difference in renormalised worldsheet areas per unit Euclidean time equals relative tension work — interpreted as a geometric thermodynamic length.
AI.conclusion: The action mismatch encodes entropic and thermodynamic information tied to conical geometry; it bridges holographic renormalisation, topological gravity, and black hole thermodynamics in asymptotically AdS spacetimes with string-like defects.

title: Spectral recurrences and maximal analyticity: cosmological correlators at one and two loops
summary: We develop a method for computing de Sitter boundary correlators based on the maximal analyticity of the two-point function and differential--difference equations satisfied by Schwinger--Keldysh diagrams. The vertex integrations are analytically continued through the relevant de Sitter tuboids onto purely imaginary Lobachevskij cycles. Taking the Mehler--Fock transform of the invariant bubble kernels on these Riemannian cycles converts their differential--difference equations into algebraic recurrences in the spectral parameter. The mixed-branch kernel obeys a homogeneous recurrence, whereas the chronological and antichronological kernels satisfy sourced recurrences whose local terms are determined by dimensionally continued tadpoles. We solve these recurrences, constructing explicit particular solutions in terms of generalised hypergeometric functions and identifying the analytic conditions selecting their physical completion. Attachment to the external boundary points then yields an intrinsic spectral representation and a complete solution of the boundary in--in diagrams considered here. Our method is fully coordinate-independent. Specialising to a Poincaré chart readily gives expressions that can be compared directly with those obtained by the standard coordinate-dependent approach. Composing two or more bubbles yields a multi-loop chain whose spectral multiplier is determined by the one-loop building blocks and the sum over intermediate Schwinger--Keldysh branches.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a coordinate-independent method to compute de Sitter boundary correlators using analytic continuation onto Lobachevskij cycles, Mehler–Fock transforms, and algebraic recurrences in the spectral parameter—solving differential–difference equations for Schwinger–Keldysh kernels and yielding explicit hypergeometric solutions with physical boundary conditions.
AI.motivation: To overcome limitations of coordinate-dependent approaches in computing de Sitter boundary correlators, especially for Schwinger–Keldysh diagrams, by leveraging maximal analyticity and intrinsic geometric structures of de Sitter space.
AI.method: Analytic continuation of vertex integrals onto imaginary Lobachevskij cycles in de Sitter tuboids; application of the Mehler–Fock transform to invariant bubble kernels; reduction of differential–difference equations to algebraic recurrences in the spectral parameter; solving homogeneous (mixed-branch) and sourced (chronological/antichronological) recurrences using generalised hypergeometric functions; imposing analyticity conditions for physical completion; attaching external boundary points to obtain intrinsic spectral representation.
AI.result: Explicit particular solutions for all Schwinger–Keldysh two-point kernels in terms of generalised hypergeometric functions; full spectral representation of boundary in–in diagrams; coordinate-independent construction extendable to multi-loop chains via composition of one-loop building blocks and sum over intermediate branches.
AI.conclusion: The method provides a rigorous, geometrically intrinsic, and computationally effective framework for de Sitter correlators—unifying and generalising prior coordinate-based results while enabling systematic higher-loop extensions.

title: Fluid/Gravity Correspondence in 3d Flat Gravity with Non-Compact Boundaries
summary: We study 3d flat gravity on a restricted phase space with a non-compact spatial boundary. The charge algebra splits into two commuting chiral current algebras, which a fluid/gravity dictionary maps to the stress tensor of a two-dimensional conformal fluid, with energy bounded below by the momentum. On the line, finiteness of the charges selects integrable, square-integrable currents, and the global data are carried by the scattering variables of a Schrödinger operator rather than by a monodromy. We analyze Heisenberg-like and Dirichlet-like boundary conditions; the latter give independently propagating chiral kinks associated with the reflectionless Pöschl-Teller operator. Both admit first-law relations. We outline the quantization as a Weyl $C^*$-algebra with quasi-free states. Retaining the radial dependence, the quasi-local stress tensor obeys an exact, non-perturbative flow of square-root $T\bar T$ type, which integrates to a finite boost in the radial position.

AI.tldr: This paper studies 3D flat gravity with a non-compact spatial boundary, revealing a chiral current algebra dual to a 2D conformal fluid; it identifies integrable boundary conditions (Heisenberg/Dirichlet), links kinks to reflectionless Pöschl-Teller scattering, derives first-law thermodynamics, proposes $C^*$-algebra quantization, and finds an exact square-root $T ar{T}$-type flow for the quasi-local stress tensor.
AI.motivation: To understand the holographic structure and symmetries of 3D flat gravity on a non-compact boundary, particularly how boundary conditions constrain dynamics, encode global data, and relate to fluid/gravity duality and integrable systems.
AI.method: Analysis of charge algebra on a restricted phase space; application of fluid/gravity dictionary; classification of boundary conditions (Heisenberg-like and Dirichlet-like); spectral analysis of Schrödinger operators (scattering variables vs. monodromy); derivation of first-law relations; $C^*$-algebraic quantization framework; exact computation of quasi-local stress tensor flow using square-root $T\bar{T}$-type deformation.
AI.result: Charge algebra splits into two commuting chiral currents mapped to a 2D conformal fluid stress tensor with $E \geq |P|$; finite charges select square-integrable currents; global data encoded in Schrödinger scattering variables; Dirichlet conditions yield reflectionless Pöschl-Teller kinks; both boundary conditions admit first-law thermodynamics; quantization formulated as a Weyl $C^*$-algebra with quasi-free states; quasi-local stress tensor satisfies exact non-perturbative radial flow of square-root $T\bar{T}$ type, integrating to a finite boost.
AI.conclusion: 3D flat gravity with non-compact boundary admits rich integrable structure and holographic interpretation: chiral symmetry, fluid duality, scattering-based global characterization, and exact solvable deformations—unifying geometric, algebraic, and quantum aspects within a unified $C^*$-framework.

title: Isomorphisms of Class S Theories with IndexLab
summary: We use IndexLab to scan untwisted and twisted class $\mathcal{S}$ constructions based on ADE Lie algebras of rank up to seven, as well as $A_8$ and $E_8$. We consider surfaces of genus at most three with up to five punctures, covering 167,244,647 constructions in total. To find candidate pairs of isomorphic theories, we compare Schur and Hall-Littlewood indices, Weyl anomalies, Coulomb branch spectra, and flavor data. We set aside pairs explained by known mechanisms, leaving a catalogue of 5,278 candidate pairs. Recurring changes in rank, puncture labels, and twists suggest families of candidate isomorphisms. We group 99.58% of the pairs into 25 families and 6 finite families. IndexLab is available at this http URL.

AI.tldr: This paper uses IndexLab to systematically scan and compare 167M class S constructions from ADE Lie algebras (up to rank 8) and low-genus surfaces, identifying 5,278 candidate isomorphic theory pairs via index and geometric data; most are grouped into 25+6 families suggesting structural patterns in dualities.
AI.motivation: To systematically uncover hidden isomorphisms (dualities) among 4D N=2 SCFTs of class S, beyond known mechanisms, by leveraging computational enumeration and multi-invariant matching.
AI.method: Automated scanning of class S theories using IndexLab; comparison of Schur and Hall-Littlewood indices, Weyl anomalies, Coulomb branch spectra, and flavor symmetries across 167M constructions; filtering out known dualities; clustering remaining candidates into families based on shared structural transformations (rank, puncture labels, twist changes).
AI.result: Identification of 5,278 candidate isomorphic theory pairs; 99.58% grouped into 25 infinite and 6 finite families, revealing recurring patterns in rank, puncture labels, and twist assignments that hint at new duality families.
AI.conclusion: Systematic index-based classification reveals extensive, previously unrecognized candidate dualities in class S theories, organized into coherent families—providing concrete targets for analytical proof and enriching the landscape of 4D N=2 dualities.

title: An infrared-safe $S$-matrix for $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills
summary: Scattering amplitudes of massless gauge theories are not observables: they are infrared divergent, and the standard regulators are tied either to perturbation theory or the planar limit. We study $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory on rigid AdS$_4$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where the role of the amplitude is played by correlation functions of boundary operators. These are finite, and they are defined at any coupling and for any gauge group. Among them, the four-point function of the flavor-current supermultiplet is the counterpart of the $2\to2$ amplitude of the elementary supergluon states, and arguably the simplest non-trivial observable of the theory. In this paper, we compute it at weak coupling to one loop. The tree-level correlator follows directly from the microscopic theory, and the one-loop correlator, which we obtain from AdS unitarity, takes a remarkably simple form in Mellin space. In the flat-space limit, it reproduces the one-loop scattering amplitude, with the infrared divergences re-emerging as logarithms.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the four-point correlation function of the flavor-current supermultiplet in N=4 super Yang-Mills on AdS₄ at weak coupling (tree + one-loop), using AdS unitarity; the result is finite, well-defined beyond perturbation theory, and reproduces the flat-space 2→2 scattering amplitude (with IR divergences reappearing as logs) in the flat-space limit.
AI.motivation: To define a finite, non-perturbative, and gauge-group-agnostic observable that serves as the physical counterpart to the infrared-divergent scattering amplitudes of massless gauge theories — specifically, replacing flat-space amplitudes with boundary correlators in AdS₄ with Dirichlet conditions.
AI.method: Computes the tree-level four-point correlator from the microscopic Lagrangian and obtains the one-loop correction using AdS unitarity; expresses the result in Mellin space for simplicity and takes the flat-space limit to recover the known one-loop scattering amplitude.
AI.result: The one-loop four-point function of the flavor-current supermultiplet is explicitly obtained in Mellin space and shown to be remarkably simple; its flat-space limit correctly reproduces the one-loop 2→2 supergluon amplitude, with IR divergences manifesting as logarithmic terms.
AI.conclusion: Boundary correlation functions in AdS₄ provide well-defined, finite observables that generalize scattering amplitudes beyond perturbation theory and planar limits; the computed correlator validates this framework and establishes a precise amplitude/correlator dictionary including IR structure.

title: All-Genus 2D $\mathcal{N}=1$ Superconformal Blocks
summary: We develop a numerical algorithm for two dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal blocks at arbitrary genera, in arbitrary plumbing channels, and for arbitrary spin structures. The algorithm utilizes two commuting copies of Virasoro subalgebras of the direct sum of the $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal algebra with an auxiliary free fermion algebra, which allows us to reduce the $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal blocks to Virasoro conformal blocks.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a numerical algorithm to compute 2D N=1 superconformal blocks on Riemann surfaces of arbitrary genus, plumbing channel, and spin structure by embedding into a Virasoro framework via auxiliary free fermions.
AI.motivation: To enable systematic computation of N=1 superconformal blocks—essential for bootstrap and holographic studies—in general topological and spin-structure settings where closed-form expressions are unavailable.
AI.method: Constructs two commuting Virasoro subalgebras from the direct sum of the N=1 superconformal algebra and a free fermion algebra; uses this embedding to reduce N=1 superconformal blocks to computable Virasoro conformal blocks via plumbing fixture and sewing techniques.
AI.result: A general, numerically implementable algorithm for N=1 superconformal blocks on arbitrary-genus Riemann surfaces with arbitrary spin structures and plumbing channels.
AI.conclusion: The reduction to Virasoro blocks via auxiliary fermionic structure provides a robust computational pathway for higher-genus N=1 SCFT correlation functions, extending the reach of the conformal bootstrap to supersymmetric settings beyond sphere/torus.

title: Not All Holographic Entropy Inequalities Are Free of Area Law Ultraviolet Divergences
comment: 5 pages plus appendices, 3 figures. 200,000 extreme rays in an ancillary file
summary: In the AdS/CFT correspondence, linear constraints on subsystem entropies, which are necessary conditions for the validity of the Ryu-Takayanagi proposal, define the holographic entropy cone. We disprove a prior claim that all holographic constraints of this type are free of area law divergences (superbalanced). We analyze one explicit counterexample and explain how to easily find more; we report signatures of $\mathcal{O}(10^5)$ counterexamples. Our findings invalidate multiple prior claims and conjectures.

AI.tldr: This paper disproves the claim that all holographic entropy constraints are superbalanced (free of area-law divergences), presenting an explicit counterexample and reporting ~10⁵ more, thereby invalidating several prior conjectures.
AI.motivation: To test the validity of the conjecture that all linear holographic entropy inequalities (defining the holographic entropy cone) are superbalanced—i.e., free of UV-divergent area-law terms.
AI.method: Systematic analysis of linear entropy inequalities in holographic settings, leveraging known constructions of entropy cones and explicit evaluation of divergence structure in candidate inequalities; computational enumeration to detect superbalance violations.
AI.result: Identification of an explicit linear holographic entropy inequality violating superbalance; demonstration that such violations are abundant (~10⁵ instances found); classification of structural signatures enabling efficient detection.
AI.conclusion: The superbalance conjecture is false; holographic entropy constraints can carry area-law divergences, implying deeper subtleties in the relationship between bulk geometry, boundary entanglement, and renormalization in AdS/CFT.

title: From Top to Bottom: Quark Mass Hierarchies in Heterotic String Theory
summary: Standard Model fermion masses exhibit large hierarchies, spanning more than five orders of magnitude in the quark sector alone. In this paper, we study whether these hierarchies can be generated perturbatively at tree level in smooth heterotic Calabi-Yau compactifications, where the supergravity approximation remains under computational control. In such backgrounds, physical Yukawa couplings combine holomorphic superpotential integrals with matter field Kahler metrics. The former can be computed algebraically, while the latter require solving a coupled system of partial differential equations for the Ricci-flat metric, Hermitian Yang-Mills connections, and harmonic bundle-valued forms. Within this framework, we identify two new tree-level mechanisms by which complex structure moduli can generate fermion mass hierarchies and show analytically and numerically that both mechanisms are obstructed for previously studied tetra-quadric models. Motivated by these obstructions, we scan the existing databases of tens of thousands of complete intersection Calabi-Yau line bundle models and find a unique smooth quotient admitting a rank-three up-quark Yukawa matrix at tree level. Evaluating the physical couplings on this manifold and evolving them under the renormalization group, we obtain realistic mass hierarchies for the top, charm, up, and bottom quarks in the smooth supergravity regime.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether Standard Model fermion mass hierarchies can arise perturbatively at tree level in smooth heterotic Calabi-Yau compactifications; it identifies two new complex-structure-driven mechanisms, rules them out in tetra-quadric models, and discovers a unique quotient Calabi-Yau with a rank-three up-quark Yukawa matrix yielding realistic quark masses after RG evolution.
AI.motivation: To explain the five-order-of-magnitude fermion mass hierarchies in the Standard Model via computationally controlled, perturbative, tree-level physics in heterotic string theory on smooth Calabi-Yau manifolds—avoiding non-perturbative or singular approximations.
AI.method: Combines algebraic computation of holomorphic superpotential integrals with numerical solution of coupled PDEs for Ricci-flat metrics, Hermitian Yang-Mills connections, and harmonic bundle-valued forms to compute physical (Kähler-normalized) Yukawa couplings; performs analytic/numerical obstruction analysis in tetra-quadrics and systematic database scan over complete intersection Calabi-Yau line bundle models.
AI.result: Two new complex-structure-dependent tree-level mass-generation mechanisms are identified but analytically and numerically shown to be obstructed in tetra-quadric models; a unique smooth quotient Calabi-Yau is found supporting a rank-three up-quark Yukawa matrix, and its physical couplings—after RG evolution—reproduce realistic top, charm, up, and bottom quark masses within the smooth supergravity regime.
AI.conclusion: Realistic fermion mass hierarchies can emerge at tree level in computationally controlled heterotic compactifications, but require specific geometric structures beyond previously studied classes; the existence of such a model demonstrates viability of perturbative, smooth, geometric explanations for flavor structure in string theory.

title: Giant gravitons without giant gravitons
summary: We demonstrate that the partition function of a free bosonic $U(N)$ multi-matrix model admits a giant graviton expansion. For $d$ matrices, there are $d$ distinct giant gravitons, and the expansion can be characterized by a $d$-node quiver with bifundamentals connecting the nodes. This suggests the intriguing possibility of a more generalized holography where models without any obvious gravitational dual can nevertheless be given a dual brane interpretation. The giant graviton expansion of this multi-matrix model is somewhat unconventional though, as the giant graviton partition functions will necessarily have intrinsic $N$-dependence.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that a free bosonic U(N) multi-matrix model’s partition function admits a giant graviton expansion described by a d-node quiver, suggesting a generalized holographic interpretation even for models lacking an obvious gravitational dual.
AI.motivation: To explore whether matrix models without clear gravitational duals can still admit a brane (giant graviton) interpretation, extending the scope of holography.
AI.method: Analysis of the partition function of a free bosonic U(N) multi-matrix model with d matrices; identification of a giant graviton expansion encoded in a d-node quiver with bifundamental fields.
AI.result: The partition function decomposes into a giant graviton expansion with d distinct giant gravitons; the expansion is encoded in a d-node quiver; crucially, the giant graviton partition functions retain intrinsic N-dependence, making the expansion unconventional.
AI.conclusion: This work supports a broader notion of holography where brane interpretations (via giant gravitons) may exist even without standard AdS/CFT duals, though the N-dependence signals deviation from conventional giant graviton physics.

title: Simple Models of Thermal Order in $2+1$ Dimensions
summary: Heating need not destroy order. We show that it persists to arbitrarily high temperatures in simple quantum field theories in $2+1$ spacetime dimensions. In a $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ model of two real scalar fields, a sufficiently negative mixed quartic coupling drives one field to condense, spontaneously breaking its $\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry. When coupled to massless Dirac fermions through a Yukawa interaction, this condensate generates a fermion mass, thereby spontaneously breaking parity and time-reversal symmetries. We extend this construction to a $\mathbb Z_2\times O(n)$ scalar model, in which the Mermin-Wagner theorem precludes spontaneous breaking of the continuous $O(n)$ symmetry at finite temperatures. Nevertheless, for $n=2$, a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless superfluid phase persists to arbitrarily high temperatures. In this phase, spatial correlations decay algebraically, with an exponent that approaches zero as the temperature increases. For $n\geq 3$, we uncover a further unexpected feature of these models: the characteristic size of ordered domains grows asymptotically with temperature, revealing an unusual enhancement of spatial correlations upon heating. We establish our results using a controlled high-temperature expansion, with selected findings corroborated by numerical functional renormalization group analysis. The simplicity of the field content in these models provides a promising starting point for exploring experimental realizations of persistent thermal order in thin-film materials.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that certain quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions can sustain long-range or algebraic order at arbitrarily high temperatures—contrary to conventional expectations—via symmetry-breaking condensates (Z₂×Z₂ and Z₂×O(n) models) and BKT-type phases, with domain size *increasing* with temperature for n ≥ 3, validated by high-T expansion and FRG.
AI.motivation: To challenge the paradigm that thermal fluctuations necessarily destroy long-range order in low-dimensional systems, especially in light of Mermin-Wagner theorem, and to identify robust mechanisms for persistent thermal order relevant to thin-film materials.
AI.method: Controlled high-temperature expansion; functional renormalization group (FRG) numerical analysis; analytical study of Z₂×Z₂ and Z₂×O(n) scalar field theories coupled to Dirac fermions; examination of spontaneous symmetry breaking, BKT physics, and domain-size scaling.
AI.result: 1) In Z₂×Z₂ model, a negative quartic coupling induces scalar condensation and fermion mass generation, breaking parity and time-reversal at all T. 2) In Z₂×O(2) model, BKT superfluid phase with algebraically decaying correlations persists to arbitrarily high T, exponent → 0 as T → ∞. 3) In Z₂×O(n≥3) models, ordered domain size grows asymptotically with temperature—a counterintuitive enhancement of spatial correlations upon heating.
AI.conclusion: Persistent thermal order is possible in simple 2+1D QFTs beyond standard symmetry-breaking paradigms; BKT physics and novel domain-growth behavior defy naive thermal disorder expectations, offering concrete theoretical pathways toward experimental realization in 2D materials.

title: Structure Constants of Planar N=4 SYM at Any Coupling
summary: We recast a recent conjecture for structure constants in planar N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory in a separation-of-variables-inspired form suitable for non-perturbative analysis. All state-dependent information enters through the quantum spectral curve. As a showcase, we compute at finite coupling the three-point functions of two half-BPS operators and the spin-two member of the Konishi multiplet. Our results span weak to strong coupling, reproduce the known perturbative and string-theory limits, and are consistent with conformal-bootstrap bounds. We also obtain new six- and seven-loop perturbative coefficients and extract new strong-coupling data from high-precision numerical fits.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates a conjecture for planar N=4 SYM structure constants using a separation-of-variables framework tied to the quantum spectral curve, enabling non-perturbative computation of three-point functions—including two half-BPS and Konishi spin-two operators—across all couplings, matching known limits and yielding new high-loop and strong-coupling data.
AI.motivation: To enable non-perturbative analysis of structure constants in planar N=4 SYM by recasting a recent conjecture into a separation-of-variables-inspired form anchored on the quantum spectral curve.
AI.method: Reformulation of the structure constant conjecture using separation-of-variables formalism; explicit computation of three-point functions via the quantum spectral curve; numerical high-precision fitting and perturbative expansion up to seven loops.
AI.result: Finite-coupling three-point function for two half-BPS and Konishi spin-two operators; agreement with weak- and strong-coupling limits (perturbative and string-theory); consistency with conformal bootstrap bounds; new six- and seven-loop perturbative coefficients; new strong-coupling data extracted from numerical fits.
AI.conclusion: The quantum spectral curve fully encodes state-dependent information for planar N=4 SYM structure constants, enabling robust non-perturbative predictions across the coupling spectrum and validating the proposed framework against multiple analytic and numerical benchmarks.

title: Non-integrability of open strings via Pohlmeyer reduction
summary: We study integrable and non-integrable boundary conditions for classical strings from the point of view of Pohlmeyer reduction. We first consider the integrable case of strings ending on Y=0 non-maximal giant gravitons. Pohlmeyer reduction of such strings leads to a sine-Gordon model, for which a criterion for boundary integrability was provided by Ghoshal and Zamolodchikov. We confirm that the Pohlmeyer field satisfies this condition. We then turn to the main focus of our work, which is open strings on AdS3. By evaluating the Ghoshal-Zamolodchikov criterion for the corresponding Pohlmeyer-reduced models, we are able to distinguish between integrable and non-integrable cases, in line with expectations from recent analytic and numerical studies. We conclude that Pohlmeyer reduction can provide a useful perspective on open-string non-integrability.

AI.tldr: This paper uses Pohlmeyer reduction to analyze integrable and non-integrable boundary conditions for classical open strings, confirming integrability for strings on Y=0 giant gravitons (sine-Gordon), and classifying integrability of open strings in AdS₃ via the Ghoshal-Zamolodchikov boundary criterion.
AI.motivation: To determine when open-string boundary conditions preserve integrability, using Pohlmeyer reduction as a systematic tool—especially for cases where direct worldsheet analysis is difficult, such as in AdS₃.
AI.method: Applies Pohlmeyer reduction to classical open strings with various boundary conditions; verifies the Ghoshal-Zamolodchikov integrability criterion on the resulting reduced 1+1D field theories (e.g., sine-Gordon for giant gravitons, sinh-Gordon or related models for AdS₃); compares outcomes with recent analytic/numerical results.
