AI.result: Confirms integrability for Y=0 non-maximal giant graviton boundaries; successfully distinguishes integrable vs. non-integrable boundary conditions for open strings in AdS₃ using the GZ criterion on Pohlmeyer-reduced models—consistent with independent studies.
AI.conclusion: Pohlmeyer reduction provides a robust and insightful framework for diagnosing open-string boundary integrability, particularly in curved backgrounds like AdS₃.

title: Higher Spin Lagrangians for Black Holes in Arbitrary Dimension
summary: In this paper, we investigate the classical gravitational multipolar structure of rotating objects studying higher-spin Lagrangians coupled to gravity in arbitrary dimensions $D=d+1$. We first consider fields described by totally symmetric tensors with $s$ indices. At finite spin, the minimal coupling depends on both the spin and spacetime dimension. We show that, in the high-spin limit $s\gg 1$, the minimal multipolar expansion becomes dimension independent and it corresponds to the one which reproduces the Kerr solution in four dimensions. Furthermore, we identify a dimension independent relation among the non-minimal coupling coefficients that allows us to reproduce the Myers-Perry multipolar structure in arbitrary dimensions. We then extend our analysis to Lagrangians involving fields with different Young representations, which are allowed in higher dimensions.

AI.tldr: This paper studies gravitational multipole moments of rotating objects via higher-spin fields coupled to gravity in arbitrary dimensions, showing that the high-spin limit yields a dimension-independent multipolar structure matching Kerr (D=4) and Myers-Perry (general D) solutions, and extends results to non-symmetric (Young tableau) field representations.
AI.motivation: To understand the classical gravitational multipolar structure of rotating compact objects—beyond the Kerr and Myers-Perry black hole solutions—by leveraging higher-spin field theory as an effective description, especially probing universality across spacetime dimensions.
AI.method: Analyzes minimally and non-minimally coupled higher-spin Lagrangians (totally symmetric tensor fields of spin s) to gravity in D = d+1 dimensions; computes multipolar expansions; takes the high-spin limit s ≫ 1; derives constraints on non-minimal couplings ensuring agreement with known vacuum solutions; generalizes to fields transforming in arbitrary Young symmetry classes.
AI.result: In the s ≫ 1 limit, minimal coupling yields a dimension-independent multipolar expansion identical to the Kerr solution’s; a specific dimension-independent relation among non-minimal Wilson coefficients reproduces the full Myers-Perry multipolar structure in any D; extension to mixed-symmetry (Young tableau) fields is formulated consistently.
AI.conclusion: The gravitational multipolar structure of rotating objects is encoded universally in the high-spin limit of higher-spin gravity, bridging Kerr (D=4) and Myers-Perry (arbitrary D) solutions; non-minimal couplings must satisfy a precise dimensional independence condition to match exact black hole multipole moments; the framework naturally generalizes beyond totally symmetric fields.

title: Lie-Poisson Formulation of Dissipative Spin Hydrodynamics
summary: Covariance and the second law cannot fix how fluid flow couples to spin, since reversible couplings produce no entropy. We show that the spin commutation relations and the Poincaré algebra fix these couplings. Reversibly, a flow exerts no torque on the spin: its magnitude per particle is conserved, its direction is Fermi--Walker transported, and spin--shear couplings reflect a deforming triad. The magnitude changes only through higher multipoles, as in spinor condensates, or dissipation, whose first-order spin--shear coupling reorients the spin away from the vorticity above a critical shear rate.

AI.tldr: This paper determines how fluid flow couples to spin using spin commutation relations and the Poincaré algebra, showing that reversible couplings conserve spin magnitude and follow Fermi–Walker transport, while irreversible (dissipative) couplings cause spin reorientation above a critical shear rate.
AI.motivation: Covariance and the second law alone are insufficient to fix spin–fluid coupling because reversible couplings produce no entropy; thus, deeper symmetry principles—namely spin commutation relations and the Poincaré algebra—are required.
AI.method: The authors use symmetry constraints from quantum spin algebra and relativistic spacetime symmetries (Poincaré algebra) to derive admissible reversible and irreversible couplings between fluid flow and spin degrees of freedom, distinguishing geometric (Fermi–Walker) transport from dissipative spin–shear effects.
AI.result: Reversible coupling implies conservation of spin magnitude per particle and Fermi–Walker transport of its direction; spin–shear coupling arises from triad deformation; irreversible coupling at first order causes shear-induced spin reorientation away from vorticity above a critical shear rate.
AI.conclusion: Fundamental algebraic and spacetime symmetries—not just thermodynamics or covariance—uniquely determine spin–fluid coupling; dissipation introduces qualitative changes (e.g., spin reorientation) absent in reversible dynamics.

title: Toric Calabi-Yau orientifolds: constructions, fixed loci and O-plane charges
summary: We review the systematic construction of toric orientifold Calabi-Yau threefolds through divisor exchanges and coordinate reflections. We relate the homogeneous-coordinate and lattice descriptions and explain the computation of fixed loci and the geometric data entering Hodge splittings and tadpole conditions. Our triangulation-wise analysis identifies multiple compatible involutions on a single triangulation and tracks their realisations across different triangulations, revealing the orientifold structure within and across toric phases. We complement this review with new calculations and explicit examples that refine the fixed-locus geometry and the associated orientifold charge data. The examples also identify coordinate representatives of the identity and invariant hypersurface families with unavoidable singularities. These results support an ongoing update of the orientifold catalogue and provide geometric input for D-brane configurations, flux compactifications and moduli stabilisation.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews and advances the systematic construction of toric orientifold Calabi-Yau threefolds using divisor exchanges and coordinate reflections, clarifying geometric data (fixed loci, Hodge splittings, tadpoles), identifying compatible involutions across triangulations, and providing new explicit examples with refined fixed-locus geometry and orientifold charge data.
AI.motivation: To systematically construct and classify toric orientifold Calabi-Yau threefolds for applications in string phenomenology—specifically D-brane model building, flux compactifications, and moduli stabilization—by unifying and extending existing computational frameworks (homogeneous-coordinate vs. lattice descriptions) and resolving ambiguities in involution realisations across toric phases.
AI.method: Combines algebraic geometry and toric methods: (1) divisor exchange and coordinate reflection to generate orientifold involutions; (2) triangulation-wise analysis to identify compatible involutions on individual triangulations and track them across different toric phases; (3) computation of fixed-point loci, Hodge splittings, and tadpole contributions via lattice and homogeneous-coordinate formalisms; (4) explicit construction of hypersurface families and singularity analysis.
AI.result: Identifies multiple distinct, triangulation-compatible orientifold involutions on single polytopes; reveals how orientifold structures persist or transform across toric phase transitions; provides refined geometric characterizations of fixed loci—including unavoidable singularities—and associated orientifold charges; delivers concrete examples supporting an updated orientifold catalogue.
AI.conclusion: The systematic, triangulation-aware approach unifies disparate constructions of toric orientifolds, exposes hidden structure in the orientifold landscape, and yields precise geometric input essential for consistent string compactifications with D-branes and fluxes.

title: 5d $\mathbb{Z}_{n}$ S-folds, quotient curves, and isogenies
summary: We construct Seiberg--Witten curves for the $\mathbb{Z}_3$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$, and $\mathbb{Z}_6$ S-folds of 5d rank-1 superconformal theories. Compared with the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ case arXiv:2611.09804, $\mathbb{Z}_{3,4,6}$ S-folds require stronger constraints on the mass parameters. We provide a systematic procedure of realizing the S-foldings at the mirror curve level. We obtain the same elliptic curve families by specializing the complexified mass parameters of the rank-1 $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$ theories, with holonomies motivated by the 7-brane insertions required by the S-fold prescription. The two constructions agree in Weierstrass form. The families with continuous mass deformations organize into characters of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{g}_2$, consistently with their singular fibers. Finally, we discuss that the Seiberg--Witten curves for $\mathbb{Z}_n$ S-folds can be obtained through cyclic $n$-isogenies, which may provide a uniform quotient curve description of rank-1 S-folds.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs Seiberg–Witten curves for Z₃, Z₄, and Z₆ S-folds in 5d rank-1 superconformal theories, imposing stricter mass parameter constraints than the Z₂ case; it systematically realizes S-foldings at the mirror curve level, matches resulting elliptic curves to specializations of E₆, E₇, E₈ rank-1 theories, confirms agreement in Weierstrass form, organizes deformations into su(2) and g₂ characters consistent with singular fibers, and proposes cyclic n-isogenies as a uniform description for Zₙ S-fold curves.
AI.motivation: To extend Seiberg–Witten curve constructions from the known Z₂ S-fold case to higher-order Z₃, Z₄, Z₆ S-folds in 5d rank-1 SCFTs, and to unify their geometric realization via isogenies and mirror symmetry.
AI.method: Systematic implementation of S-folding at the mirror curve level; specialization of complexified mass parameters in E₆, E₇, E₈ rank-1 theories guided by 7-brane holonomies; Weierstrass form comparison; analysis of singular fibers and associated Lie algebra characters; use of cyclic n-isogenies to describe quotient curves.
AI.result: Explicit Seiberg–Witten curves for Z₃, Z₄, Z₆ S-folds; verification that they match specialized E₆/E₇/E₈ families in Weierstrass form; identification of continuous mass deformations organizing into su(2) and g₂ characters; proposal that all Zₙ S-fold curves arise via cyclic n-isogenies.
AI.conclusion: Z₃, Z₄, Z₆ S-folds admit consistent Seiberg–Witten descriptions through constrained mass specializations and mirror curve folding, and cyclic isogenies provide a unifying framework for rank-1 S-fold curves across all n.

title: Strange-Metal Magnetotransport without a Strange-Metal Ground State
summary: Strange metals display a linear-in-temperature resistivity, $\rho_{xx}\sim T$, and a quadratic inverse Hall angle, $\cot\Theta_H\sim T^2$. These seemingly universal laws are often attributed to quantum criticality, yet no controlled theory realizes both at an asymptotic zero-temperature fixed point, and experimentally they persist only over finite temperature windows. Here, we show that these properties can arise from an intermediate critical regime that does not govern the ground state. Using a minimal class of holographic models, we construct a fully backreacted realization of both scalings, which appear within a finite temperature window controlled by an emergent intermediate scaling geometry. The window is bounded by relevant deformations of the corresponding fixed point: momentum relaxation sets the upper edge, while the magnetic field $B$ closes it from below at $T_{\min}\sim B^{2/3}$, up to logarithmic corrections. At $T_{\min}$, strange-metal transport, the scaling geometry, and critical thermodynamics break down together. Our results point to intermediate criticality as a distinct route to strange-metal transport, and suggest that it can be identified by the simultaneous breakdown of transport and thermodynamic scaling under a magnetic field.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes intermediate criticality—not quantum criticality at zero temperature—as the origin of strange-metal transport (ρ∼T, cotΘ_H∼T²), realized holographically in a finite-temperature window bounded by momentum relaxation (upper T) and magnetic field B (lower T_min ∼ B^{2/3}); transport and thermodynamic scaling break down simultaneously at T_min.
AI.motivation: To resolve the tension between universal strange-metal scalings (ρ_xx ∼ T, cotΘ_H ∼ T²) observed experimentally over finite T ranges and the lack of any controlled theory realizing both at a true zero-temperature quantum critical fixed point.
AI.method: Constructs fully backreacted holographic models featuring an emergent intermediate scaling geometry; identifies relevant deformations—momentum relaxation and magnetic field—that bound the strange-metal regime; analyzes transport (resistivity, Hall angle) and thermodynamics across the temperature range.
AI.result: Demonstrates simultaneous linear-in-T resistivity and quadratic-in-T inverse Hall angle within a finite temperature window; derives T_min ∼ B^{2/3} (up to logs) as the lower bound where scaling breaks down; shows concurrent failure of transport scalings, intermediate geometry, and critical thermodynamics at T_min.
AI.conclusion: Intermediate criticality—governed by a finite-T scaling regime rather than a T=0 fixed point—is a viable, distinct mechanism for strange-metal behavior; its experimental signature is the correlated collapse of transport and thermodynamic scaling under magnetic field tuning.

title: An Effective Theory for Hot Lines
summary: We develop a high-temperature effective theory for spatial conformal line defects in theories with thermal screening. The defect partition function admits a local geometric expansion, whose leading terms describe the effective tension and bending response of the line. Using a convergent bulk OPE for heavy-state defect matrix elements, we derive asymptotic relations for averaged products of defect one-point coefficients and bulk OPE coefficients in the regime $1 \ll \Delta_\chi \ll \Delta^{1/d}$. We compute the leading EFT coefficients for a twisted free scalar and for the magnetic line at the $\mathrm{O}(N)$ Wilson-Fisher fixed point, large-$N$ Gross--Neveu model and $\mathcal N = 2$ Chern-Simons-matter theory. For the three-dimensional Ising model, Monte Carlo simulations yield a perimeter coefficient in good agreement with a Padé interpolation of our $\varepsilon$-expansion result.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a high-temperature effective field theory (EFT) for spatial conformal line defects in thermally screened quantum field theories, deriving geometric expansion coefficients (tension, bending), asymptotic relations for defect-bulk OPE data, and computing them in multiple models—including free scalar, O(N) Wilson-Fisher, Gross–Neveu, and N=2 Chern–Simons–matter—while validating the 3D Ising perimeter coefficient via Monte Carlo and ε-expansion Padé interpolation.
AI.motivation: To systematically characterize the universal low-energy dynamics of spatial line defects at high temperature in theories with thermal screening, bridging conformal defect physics with finite-temperature EFT and bulk-defect OPE constraints.
AI.method: Constructs a local geometric EFT for line defects using thermal screening; employs convergent bulk operator product expansion (OPE) for heavy defect states to derive asymptotic relations among averaged one-point coefficients and bulk OPE coefficients in the regime 1 ≪ Δ_χ ≪ Δ^(1/d); computes EFT coefficients analytically in solvable models and numerically (Monte Carlo) for the 3D Ising model; uses ε-expansion and Padé resummation for comparison.
AI.result: Derives leading EFT coefficients—effective tension and bending rigidity—for twisted free scalar, magnetic line in O(N) Wilson-Fisher, large-N Gross–Neveu, and N=2 Chern–Simons–matter theories; obtains asymptotic relations linking defect one-point functions and bulk OPE data; finds Monte Carlo perimeter coefficient for 3D Ising consistent with ε-expansion Padé prediction.
AI.conclusion: Spatial conformal line defects at high temperature admit a predictive geometric EFT governed by universal tension and bending terms; the interplay between bulk-defect OPE, thermal screening, and dimensional analysis yields robust asymptotics and quantitative agreement across analytical, perturbative, and numerical approaches.

title: The Pfaffian sector of $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ BPS cohomology: brane excitations, triality and fortuity
summary: We study the classical $\frac{1}{16}$-BPS cohomology of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory with gauge group $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ in the BMN sector, including the operators built with one $\epsilon$-tensor. These operators are odd under the reflection in $\mathrm{O}(2N)$, carry the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ charge of a D3-brane wrapped on $\mathbb{RP}^3\subset\mathbb{RP}^5$, and form the Pfaffian sector. For $\mathrm{SO}(8)$ we determine this sector through level $j=18$, where the level is twice the total charge of an operator. All but one of its $106$ $\mathrm{SU}(3)_R$ multiplets are products of trace gravitons and excited Pfaffians. The exception is a singlet, represented by the singlet projection of the rank-four member of a four-term family of $\epsilon$-tensor operators. We construct a covering space for the Pfaffian sector in which this family is closed at every rank, and the family defines a non-graviton class for every $N\ge 4$. Triality pairs the singlet with a reflection-even class that is fortuitous with respect to the trace covering. The two classes restrict, along the spinor and the vector embedding of $\mathfrak{so}(7)$ respectively, to the known non-graviton singlet of $\mathrm{SO}(7)$, which is lifted at first order. We show that the two $\mathrm{SO}(8)$ classes, and the family for every $N\ge 4$, are protected to all orders of perturbation theory. Their protection is compatible with the lifting in $\mathrm{SO}(7)$ because restriction to a subalgebra does not commute with the quantum corrections to the supercharge.

AI.tldr: This paper studies 1/16-BPS cohomology in SO(2N) N=4 SYM in the BMN sector, focusing on Pfaffian operators built with epsilon-tensors; it identifies a protected non-graviton singlet in SO(8), constructs a covering space where an epsilon-family closes, shows all such classes are all-order protected, and explains apparent lifting in SO(7) via non-commutativity of restriction and quantum corrections.
AI.motivation: To understand non-graviton protected operators in the BMN limit of N=4 SYM with orthogonal gauge groups, particularly those odd under O(2N) reflection (Pfaffian sector), and resolve apparent tension between protection in SO(8) and lifting in SO(7).
AI.method: Cohomological analysis of the 1/16-BPS supercharge in the BMN sector; explicit enumeration and SU(3)_R representation analysis up to level j=18 for SO(8); construction of a covering space for the epsilon-tensor operator family; use of triality and Lie algebra embeddings (so(7) ⊂ so(8)) to relate sectors; perturbative protection arguments via symmetry and cohomological rigidity.
AI.result: A novel protected singlet in the Pfaffian sector of SO(8) N=4 SYM, distinct from graviton composites; a closed four-term epsilon-family defining non-graviton classes for all N≥4; demonstration that these classes are all-order protected; identification of its triality partner; resolution of SO(7) lifting paradox via non-commutativity of restriction and quantum corrections.
AI.conclusion: The Pfaffian sector contains robust, all-order protected non-graviton states in SO(2N) N=4 SYM, whose existence and protection are governed by cohomological structure and group-theoretic embeddings, and apparent lifting upon restriction arises from the failure of subalgebra restriction to commute with quantum corrections to the supercharge.

title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
comment: 23 pages, 6 figures. Companion paper to an 18-volume textbook collection. Textbook PDFs: this https URL
summary: We present StringQFT as a textbook collection for string constructions of quantum field theory and as infrastructure for AI-assisted theoretical physics. The collection comprises 18 volumes, 190 chapters and 3,795 pages, covering brane probes, brane webs, geometric engineering, F-theory constructions, wrapped M5-branes and exact worldsheet constructions. Its open-book benchmark inventory contains 1,073 items, including 499 with automatic finite-answer checking. For retrieval-augmented generation, it provides 1,371 section records linked to textbook sources and PDF locations, together with a local lexical retriever. Training-data preparation is illustrated by 21 private, source-linked examples. For agents, it exposes 19 calculation tools with specified inputs and finite domains, connecting tool use to textbook derivations. We illustrate these uses through specific questions, retrieved passages and finite calculations. The textbook collection and accompanying resources are available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: StringQFT is a comprehensive, open-book textbook collection (18 volumes, 190 chapters, 3,795 pages) designed for AI-assisted theoretical physics, featuring structured benchmarks, retrieval infrastructure, calculation tools, and training-data examples for string-theoretic QFT constructions.
AI.motivation: To bridge string theory and quantum field theory with AI-ready, rigorously structured educational and computational infrastructure—enabling retrieval-augmented generation, automated verification, and agent-based reasoning in theoretical physics.
AI.method: Curated a large-scale, source-linked textbook collection; built an open-book benchmark inventory with automatic answer checking; implemented lexical retrieval over section records; provided finite-domain calculation tools tied to textbook derivations; illustrated usage via concrete queries, retrieved passages, and verified calculations.
AI.result: A fully deployed, publicly available resource comprising 1,073 benchmark items (499 auto-verifiable), 1,371 retrievable section records, 21 training-data examples, and 19 domain-specific calculation tools—all integrated with textbook sources and PDF locations.
AI.conclusion: StringQFT establishes a reproducible, extensible foundation for AI-assisted research and pedagogy in string-theoretic QFT, demonstrating feasibility of finite-answer reasoning, tool-augmented agents, and source-grounded RAG in high-energy theory.

title: Holographic Approaches to Hadron Structure
comment: Invited contribution to the Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics (Elsevier), 70 pages, 10 figures, 8 tables; v3: minor corrections and additions
summary: We give an introduction to and an overview of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure. After an introduction to the string-theoretic foundations of holographic QCD, we review the predictions of top-down and bottom-up models for the phenomenology of mesons, baryons, and glueballs. We focus on the top-down model following from probe flavor branes in the Witten model of low-energy Yang-Mills theory and, in the more phenomenological approach of bottom-up models, mostly on minimal models based on five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, which also implement global symmetries and their anomalies consistently, but allow the high-energy behavior to better match real QCD.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a comprehensive review of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure, covering both top-down (e.g., probe flavor branes in the Witten model) and bottom-up (e.g., 5D AdS-based) frameworks, emphasizing their phenomenological predictions for mesons, baryons, and glueballs.
AI.motivation: To bridge string-theoretic holography with real-world QCD phenomenology by reviewing how top-down and bottom-up holographic models capture non-perturbative features of hadrons.
AI.method: Review and comparative analysis of top-down holographic constructions (e.g., Witten’s Yang-Mills model with probe D-branes) and bottom-up AdS/QCD models—particularly minimal 5D anti-de Sitter setups incorporating chiral symmetry and anomaly matching.
AI.result: Systematic exposition of meson, baryon, and glueball spectra and properties predicted by both classes of models; highlights where bottom-up models better reproduce QCD high-energy behavior while maintaining consistency with symmetries and anomalies.
AI.conclusion: Holographic QCD—both top-down and bottom-up—offers valuable qualitative and semi-quantitative insights into hadron structure, with bottom-up models providing greater flexibility for phenomenological tuning while preserving key QCD symmetries and constraints.

title: A new angle on coherence-violating logarithms in color-singlet processes
summary: We introduce a new formulation for the resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the transverse energy flow in rapidity gaps in the Drell-Yan process. Our formalism allows us to resum coherence-violating logarithms in the gap cross section in the phenomenologically important regime where the gap size is comparable to the logarithm of the transverse energy. In the formal small gap limit, our result reduces to the known state-of-the-art resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the Drell-Yan process. However, we identify sizable new corrections even for moderate gap widths that significantly modify the phenomenological picture for LHC applications. This work will form an important element of future extensions to a range of global and non-global observables.

AI.tldr: Introduces a new resummation formalism for coherence-violating logarithms in transverse energy flow within rapidity gaps for Drell-Yan, improving accuracy for moderate gap sizes relevant to LHC phenomenology.
AI.motivation: To extend resummation of coherence-violating logarithms beyond the small-gap limit to regimes where gap size is comparable to log(transverse energy), which is phenomenologically relevant for LHC.
AI.method: Develops a novel theoretical formulation enabling resummation of coherence-violating logarithms in the rapidity-gap cross section for Drell-Yan, valid both in the small-gap limit and for moderate gap widths.
AI.result: Recovers known small-gap resummation as a limit, but reveals sizable new corrections for moderate gaps, significantly altering LHC phenomenological predictions.
AI.conclusion: The new formalism provides a more accurate and broadly applicable framework for coherence-violating logarithm resummation, serving as a foundation for future extensions to global and non-global observables.

title: Scalar inelastic scattering of pseudo-Majorana dark matter through a radion portal
summary: We investigate a radion portal for pseudo-Majorana dark matter as an interpretation of the high-recoil event LZ230616. In contrast to the familiar pseudo-Dirac regime, the pseudo-Majorana structure allows a dominant scalar transition while suppressing elastic scattering. Endothermic kinematics remove low-energy recoils, while the nuclear response shapes the surviving high-recoil spectrum. Combining the accepted LZ event count with the Born-level thermal relic abundance yields a reference solution with $m_\chi=1$ TeV, $\delta=340$ keV, and $m_r=30$ GeV. This solution lies within the published LZ spin-independent $\mathcal{O}_1^s$ interval and remains compatible with existing OPAL and CMS constraints, while a simplified HL-LHC diphoton projection could probe it. Solar neutrino searches offer a complementary test. The benchmark's energetic-daughter proxy rates are comparable in magnitude to the rate scales reconstructed from IceCube's direct $b\bar{b}$ and $\tau^+\tau^-$ templates. An illustrative IceCube-Gen2 rescaling suggests future sensitivity, while a model-specific assessment requires the radion-cascade neutrino spectra and detector response.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a pseudo-Majorana dark matter model coupled via a radion portal to explain the high-recoil LZ230616 event, yielding a benchmark solution (mχ=1 TeV, δ=340 keV, mr=30 GeV) consistent with LZ, OPAL, and CMS constraints; it is testable at HL-LHC (diphotons) and IceCube-Gen2 (neutrino cascades).
AI.motivation: To interpret the anomalous high-recoil event LZ230616 observed by the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment using a theoretically motivated dark matter framework—specifically, pseudo-Majorana DM coupled through a radion portal—that evades conventional elastic scattering bounds while accommodating endothermic kinematics and nuclear response effects.
AI.method: The authors construct a pseudo-Majorana DM model where DM couples to nuclei predominantly via scalar-mediated (radion-induced) inelastic transitions. They compute the recoil spectrum incorporating endothermic kinematics (requiring energy threshold δ), nuclear form factors, and Born-level thermal relic density matching. Constraints are imposed from LZ spin-independent limits (O₁ˢ operator), OPAL (e⁺e⁻ → hadrons), CMS (radion-like resonances), and projected HL-LHC diphoton searches. Neutrino indirect detection prospects are assessed via IceCube templates (bb̄, τ⁺τ⁻) and rescaled IceCube-Gen2 sensitivity.
AI.result: A reference solution is identified: mχ = 1 TeV, mass splitting δ = 340 keV, radion mass mr = 30 GeV. This point satisfies LZ event statistics, lies within the O₁ˢ SI exclusion band, evades OPAL/CMS limits, and is accessible to HL-LHC diphoton searches. Its energetic-daughter neutrino flux matches IceCube template rates; IceCube-Gen2 shows projected sensitivity pending full cascade spectral modeling.
AI.conclusion: The pseudo-Majorana radion portal provides a viable, testable explanation for LZ230616, reconciling relic abundance, direct detection anomalies, and collider/neutrino constraints—highlighting the importance of inelastic, scalar-coupled DM scenarios beyond standard pseudo-Dirac paradigms.

title: A Universal Axion in a Twin-QCD Sector
summary: Dark matter may consist of multiple components with distinct particle-physics origins. We investigate a scenario in which a universal axion couples to both visible and twin QCD, with twin baryons providing a possible dominant dark-matter component. The presence of a second strongly interacting sector can substantially enhance the axion mass while preserving its role in resolving the strong-CP problem, provided the physical vacuum angles are appropriately aligned. For a representative uniformly rescaled twin spectrum with a confinement scale five times that of ordinary QCD, the axion mass is enhanced by approximately a factor of 25. Using lattice-informed QCD results and a two-temperature description of the early universe, we investigate the cosmological evolution and relative abundances of the dark-sector components. In a representative conditional numerical benchmark, axions account for a small percentage of the observed dark matter, while twin baryons could constitute the remainder for a suitable primordial baryon asymmetry. We also examine the implications for additional relativistic species, strong-CP alignment, and the interactions of stable twin matter. Our results provide a quantitative framework for exploring mixed axion--twin-baryon dark matter and identify the particle-physics and cosmological conditions necessary for a viable realization, including constraints from the thermal history and formation of cosmic structure.

AI.tldr: This paper explores a multi-component dark matter scenario where a universal axion couples to both standard and 'twin' QCD sectors; twin baryons may dominate dark matter, while the axion mass is enhanced by twin-sector confinement—enabling strong-CP solution preservation—and cosmological evolution is analyzed using lattice QCD and two-temperature early-universe modeling.
AI.motivation: To reconcile the axion solution to the strong-CP problem with observational dark matter abundance, while accommodating richer dark-sector physics beyond single-component paradigms—specifically, leveraging a twin QCD sector to enhance axion mass without spoiling CP naturalness.
AI.method: Combined lattice-QCD–informed axion potential calculations, two-temperature cosmological thermal history modeling (accounting for decoupled twin sector), numerical computation of relic abundances for axions and twin baryons, and analysis of strong-CP alignment conditions and relativistic degrees of freedom (ΔN_eff).
AI.result: Twin QCD with 5× higher confinement scale enhances axion mass ~25×; in benchmark scenarios, axions contribute only a small fraction (<10%) of Ω_DM, while twin baryons supply the remainder given appropriate primordial asymmetry; viable parameter space requires twin-sector thermal decoupling, alignment of physical vacuum angles, and consistency with ΔN_eff < 0.3 and structure formation constraints.
AI.conclusion: Mixed axion–twin-baryon dark matter is quantitatively viable under specific particle-physics (twin confinement scale, vacuum alignment) and cosmological (asymmetry, decoupling temperature) conditions; this framework expands testable axion phenomenology to include twin-hadronic signatures and modified early-universe thermodynamics.

title: Complete Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-handed Neutrino Loops
summary: We study the complete cosmological collider (CC) signatures from right-handed neutrino loops with chemical-potential enhancement. These CC signals are induced by the inflaton-right-handed-neutrino interaction and can be extracted in the collinear squeezed configuration, which allows the right-handed-neutrino triangle loop to be factorized into the hard and soft parts. We precisely compute the soft part of the fermion loop for the first time by using the complete mode functions and the full loop integral, and treat the hard part as a tree-level subdiagram. We subtract the large-momentum asymptotic terms of the soft loop integrand and retain their finite contributions to the oscillation. We then evaluate the full spinor-helicity and Schwinger-Keldysh sums to obtain a finite, closed analytic formula for the complex clock coefficient. We further derive a compact formula for the leading CC signals in the large-chemical-potential expansion. We analyze the structure of the soft-part contribution by examining the sum of residues of the Mellin poles of the fermion propagators. For this, we demonstrate that the first local pole on each soft line contributes half of the asymptotic coefficient on one Schwinger-Keldysh path and the remaining local poles on the second soft line supply the other half.

AI.tldr: This paper computes complete cosmological collider signatures from right-handed neutrino loops with chemical-potential enhancement, deriving a finite analytic formula for the complex clock coefficient and compact leading-order signals in the large-chemical-potential limit.
AI.motivation: To fully characterize cosmological collider signals from heavy right-handed neutrinos during inflation, especially under chemical-potential enhancement, which modifies loop dynamics and oscillatory features in non-Gaussian correlators.
AI.method: Uses complete mode functions and full loop integrals to compute the soft part of the fermion triangle loop; factorizes the collinear squeezed limit into hard (tree-level subdiagram) and soft parts; subtracts asymptotic momentum terms while retaining finite oscillatory contributions; performs full spinor-helicity and Schwinger-Keldysh sums; analyzes Mellin-pole residues of fermion propagators to dissect soft-part structure.
AI.result: A finite, closed-form analytic expression for the complex clock coefficient; a compact leading-order formula for cosmological collider signals in the large-chemical-potential expansion; identification that the first local pole on each soft line contributes half the asymptotic coefficient per Schwinger-Keldysh branch, with remaining poles completing the sum.
AI.conclusion: The soft-loop contribution is precisely controlled by residue structure of fermion propagators in Mellin space, enabling robust extraction of oscillatory CC signals—validating chemical-potential-enhanced right-handed neutrinos as detectable probes of high-scale physics via primordial non-Gaussianity.

title: 21 cm Cosmology of Boosted Dark Matter
summary: The formation history of low-mass halos is sensitive to the properties of dark matter. At low redshift, nonlinear evolution and baryonic processes can obscure this information. The 21 cm signal provides access to a high-redshift stage of structure formation, when the abundance and clustering of low-mass halos retain direct sensitivity to the mass and interactions of dark matter. Boosted dark matter (BDM) realizes this possibility through a two-component scenario in which the annihilation of the heavier component converts part of the mass difference into kinetic energy of the lighter component. Self-interactions redistribute this energy and generate pressure support, suppressing small-scale density perturbations even for dark matter masses in the MeV range. We calculate the global 21 cm brightness temperature and its power spectrum in BDM cosmology. The reduced abundance of low-mass halos delays the global absorption feature and shifts the characteristic redshift evolution of the power spectrum. We assess the projected sensitivity of SKA1-Low to these signatures. The sensitivity is strongest at intermediate light-component fractions, where both components remain sufficiently abundant for self-heating to affect structure formation. For $\sigma_{\rm self1}/m_1\simeq0.1\,{\rm cm^2\,g^{-1}}$, models with $0.2\lesssim r_1\lesssim0.7$ can be distinguished from the fiducial $\Lambda$CDM prediction at the $95\%$ confidence level under the optimistic forecast. We compare our results with existing direct-detection bounds from SENSEI and prospects for BDM searches at large-volume neutrino experiments, including Super-/Hyper-Kamiokande, JUNO, and DUNE. This comparison highlights the unique and complementary role of high-redshift surveys in testing BDM models.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how boosted dark matter (BDM) — a two-component dark matter model where annihilation heats the lighter component — suppresses small-scale structure formation, and probes its imprints on the high-redshift 21 cm signal; it finds that SKA1-Low can distinguish BDM from ΛCDM at 95% CL for intermediate light-component fractions and self-interaction cross sections ~0.1 cm²/g, complementing terrestrial direct-detection and neutrino experiments.
AI.motivation: Low-mass halo formation is sensitive to dark matter properties, but obscured by baryonic effects at low redshift; the 21 cm signal at high redshift preserves this sensitivity, offering a clean probe of nonstandard dark matter physics like boosted dark matter.
AI.method: The authors compute the global 21 cm brightness temperature and its power spectrum in BDM cosmology, incorporating suppression of low-mass halo abundance due to self-interaction–driven pressure support, and assess detectability using SKA1-Low sensitivity forecasts.
AI.result: BDM delays the global 21 cm absorption feature and shifts the redshift evolution of the power spectrum; SKA1-Low can distinguish BDM models with light-component fraction r₁ ∈ [0.2, 0.7] and self-interaction cross section σ_self1/m₁ ≈ 0.1 cm²/g from ΛCDM at 95% CL under optimistic assumptions.
AI.conclusion: High-redshift 21 cm surveys provide a unique, complementary probe of boosted dark matter — particularly in parameter space inaccessible to current direct-detection (e.g., SENSEI) or neutrino experiments (e.g., Super-K, JUNO, DUNE) — by leveraging its imprint on early structure formation.

title: Feebly-Interacting Particle Searches
comment: 10 pages, to appear in the Proceedings of ICHEP 2026, the 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics, Natal, Brazil, 30 July to 5 August 2026
summary: In the last several years, feebly-interacting particles (FIPs) have moved from "exotica" to the mainstream of particle physics. This development is fueled by three motivations: FIPs are one of two broad possibilities for new particles, FIPs are as well motivated by dark matter as WIMPs, and FIPs are connected to important problems in particle physics. I review these motivations and then briefly highlight recent progress in a few areas, including axion-like particles, dark photons and other gauge bosons, the X17 anomaly, quirks, and the Forward Physics Facility.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews the growing importance of feebly-interacting particles (FIPs) in particle physics, emphasizing their theoretical motivation—complementing WIMPs as dark matter candidates and addressing core problems in the field—and highlights recent experimental and conceptual advances in axion-like particles, dark photons, the X17 anomaly, quirks, and the Forward Physics Facility.
AI.motivation: FIPs represent one of two broad classes of possible new particles; they are as theoretically well-motivated for dark matter as WIMPs; and they connect to fundamental open questions in particle physics (e.g., hierarchy problem, strong CP problem, neutrino masses).
AI.method: Review article: synthesizes theoretical arguments, phenomenological frameworks, and recent experimental developments across multiple FIP sectors.
AI.result: Demonstrates that FIPs have transitioned from speculative exotica to central targets in particle physics; identifies key experimental frontiers and theoretical consistency requirements.
AI.conclusion: FIPs constitute a compelling, diverse, and experimentally accessible portal to physics beyond the Standard Model, warranting coordinated theoretical, accelerator-based, beam-dump, astrophysical, and precision laboratory efforts.

title: Plugging the Pion Chimney
summary: Heavy QCD axions and other gluon-coupled axion-like particles (ALPs) with masses from MeV to GeV are well motivated and have been searched for extensively. However, a window around the neutral pion mass, the so-called pion chimney, has escaped every search. There the ALP mixes strongly with the $\pi^0$ and therefore shares its experimental signatures. We show that the chimney can be closed with existing LHC data. The key point is that mixing changes the lifetimes of the two mass eigenstates but does not make them equal, and at LHC energies the states are boosted enough for the lifetime to decide whether they escape the detector or decay inside it. The ATLAS monojet search constrains the first case and the ATLAS inclusive photon measurement the second, and together they exclude the chimney up to the cutoff of the ALP effective theory. Above the cutoff, LHC searches for the colored states of the simplest ultraviolet completions exclude the rest. We also show that the bound from the $K^+$ width does not reach the chimney, because an ALP passes the same selection as a $\pi^0$, and we derive an independent, purely kinematic constraint from the measured $\pi^\pm$-$\pi^0$ mass splitting.

AI.tldr: This paper closes the 'pion chimney'—a previously unexcluded mass window (~135 MeV) for heavy QCD axions/ALPs—by reinterpreting existing LHC data (ATLAS monojet and inclusive photon searches), leveraging ALP–π⁰ mixing-induced lifetime splitting and Lorentz boosting; it also rules out higher masses via colored UV completions and refutes K⁺-width constraints due to kinematic mimicry.
AI.motivation: The pion chimney—a narrow mass region around m_π⁰ (~135 MeV) for heavy gluon-coupled axions/ALPs—has evaded all prior experimental searches because ALP–π⁰ mixing causes the ALP to inherit π⁰’s signatures, rendering traditional analyses insensitive.
AI.method: The authors exploit the fact that ALP–π⁰ mixing produces two non-degenerate mass eigenstates with distinct lifetimes; at LHC energies, Lorentz boosting makes their decay lengths experimentally resolvable. They reinterpret ATLAS monojet (sensitive to long-lived, detector-escaping states) and inclusive diphoton (sensitive to prompt decays) data to jointly exclude the chimney. They further apply K⁺ decay width limits and derive a novel kinematic bound from the π⁺–π⁰ mass splitting.
AI.result: The pion chimney is fully excluded up to the effective theory cutoff (~few GeV) using existing LHC data; above the cutoff, LHC searches for colored partners in minimal UV completions (e.g., vector-like quarks) close the remaining gap; the K⁺ width constraint is shown to be inapplicable due to ALP–π⁰ signature degeneracy, and a new model-independent bound from π⁺–π⁰ mass splitting is established.
AI.conclusion: No viable parameter space remains for MeV–GeV heavy QCD axions or ALPs in the pion chimney; the combination of lifetime-resolved LHC analyses and UV-motivated high-mass searches provides a complete exclusion, significantly tightening constraints on axion-like physics in this mass range.

title: Supernova Bounds on Neutrino Dipole Moments from a Modern Perspective
summary: Neutrinos may have nonstandard magnetic dipole moments $\mu_\nu$. In the dense cores of supernovae (SNe), these would convert part of the neutrinos into sterile, right-handed states through the electromagnetic fluctuations of the charged plasma. The streaming sterile neutrinos with 100-MeV energies can convert back to standard neutrinos in the Galactic magnetic field, leading to a high-energy neutrino flux unobserved from the historical SN 1987A. We reassess the production rates, including scattering on both protons and electrons, and, building upon advances in SN simulations and in the description of the Milky Way magnetic field, we revisit the bounds on magnetic dipole moments. We find for Dirac electron neutrinos $\mu_{\nu_e} \lesssim 4.8 \times 10^{-13} \mu_B$, superseding all existing terrestrial and astrophysical constraints.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits astrophysical bounds on neutrino magnetic dipole moments using updated supernova and Galactic magnetic field models, deriving a new stringent limit for Dirac electron neutrinos: μ_νₑ ≲ 4.8 × 10⁻¹³ μ_B.
AI.motivation: To improve constraints on neutrino magnetic dipole moments (μ_ν) by leveraging recent advances in supernova simulations and Galactic magnetic field modeling, addressing limitations of prior astrophysical and terrestrial bounds.
AI.method: Computes sterile neutrino production via electromagnetic plasma fluctuations in SN cores (including scattering on protons and electrons), tracks sterile-to-active neutrino conversion in the Milky Way's magnetic field, and derives exclusion limits from non-observation of high-energy neutrinos from SN 1987A.
AI.result: A revised upper bound μ_νₑ ≲ 4.8 × 10⁻¹³ μ_B for Dirac electron neutrinos—tighter than all existing terrestrial and astrophysical constraints.
AI.conclusion: The updated analysis establishes the strongest current bound on the magnetic dipole moment of Dirac electron neutrinos, demonstrating the power of synergistic improvements in SN physics and Galactic magnetism.

title: Active Galactic Nuclei as Beyond the Standard Model Laboratories: a White Paper
summary: Multi-messenger and multi-wavelength observations of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) can provide otherwise inaccessible knowledge about physics Beyond the Standard Model (BSM), and may even lead to its discovery. Realizing this potential hinges on two parallel efforts: advancing our understanding of AGN and of the dark matter around them, and identifying the BSM signatures that are at once promising and robust against the gaps in that understanding. These fields have attracted growing interest in recent years, also motivated by the IceCube association of neutrinos to individual AGN, yet we have only begun to explore their cross-fertilization. This white paper offers a new perspective on this interdisciplinary endeavor. It concisely reviews the state of the art in each field and at their interface, and identifies the key open questions that must be addressed to strengthen our prospects for learning about BSM physics with AGN.

AI.tldr: This white paper reviews the interdisciplinary potential of multi-messenger/multi-wavelength AGN observations for probing Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) physics, emphasizing synergies between AGN astrophysics, dark matter modeling, and robust BSM signature identification.
AI.motivation: To leverage recent multi-messenger observations (e.g., IceCube neutrino–AGN associations) for BSM physics discovery by bridging gaps between AGN astrophysics, dark matter phenomenology, and BSM model testing.
AI.method: Concise state-of-the-art review across AGN physics, dark matter in AGN environments, and BSM signature identification; synthesis to identify key open questions at their interface.
AI.result: Identification of critical open questions hindering robust BSM inference from AGN observations, including uncertainties in AGN emission mechanisms, DM density profiles near supermassive black holes, and degeneracies between astrophysical backgrounds and BSM signals.
AI.conclusion: Progress requires coordinated theoretical and observational efforts to develop AGN–DM–BSM frameworks that are both physically motivated and observationally falsifiable; this white paper provides a roadmap for such interdisciplinary advancement.

title: Thermal Composite Dark Matter at LZ
summary: We show that stable fermionic resonances of Composite Higgs models provide a thermal inelastic Dark Matter interpretation of the high-energy nuclear-recoil event LZ230616. Their stability follows from an exact accidental parity of the strong sector. Annihilation channels from composite interactions link the thermal relic mass to the strong coupling, allowing masses well beyond the pure electroweak prediction. We identify three scenarios in which the neutral states form a split pseudo-Dirac pair, distinguished by the origin of the inelastic coupling to the $Z$ boson. In the pure electroweak regime, the pair consists of the neutral components of a complex Higgsino-like doublet. Its unsuppressed inelastic $Z$ coupling requires Dark Matter masses above 20 TeV. In the pure strong regime, the suppressed $Z$ coupling of neutral states with vanishing hypercharge arises from strong interactions alone, allowing for smaller splittings and TeV-scale masses. In the third regime, which interpolates between the previous two, the neutral components of multiplets with different hypercharge are mixed. This enhances their inelastic coupling, accommodating the LZ event for masses of a few TeV and splittings around 300 keV, with mixing angles of order $10^\circ$. All three cases provide a thermal Dark Matter candidate able to explain the LZ event, consistently with the solar-capture bounds, the LZ high-energy sideband, and gamma-ray indirect searches.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes stable fermionic resonances in Composite Higgs models as thermal inelastic dark matter candidates to explain the LZ230616 nuclear-recoil event, identifying three distinct regimes (pure electroweak, pure strong, and mixed) that accommodate different mass scales and splittings while satisfying all relevant experimental constraints.
AI.motivation: To explain the high-energy nuclear-recoil event LZ230616 observed by the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment via a thermally produced inelastic dark matter candidate, grounded in theoretically motivated Composite Higgs frameworks with built-in stability.
AI.method: Analyzes accidental parity-induced stability of fermionic composite resonances; computes annihilation cross sections via composite-sector interactions; classifies inelastic Z-coupling mechanisms across three regimes (electroweak-only, strong-only, and hypercharge-mixed); confronts predictions with LZ230616, solar capture, high-energy sideband, and gamma-ray indirect detection bounds.
AI.result: Identifies three viable scenarios: (i) >20 TeV DM in pure electroweak regime; (ii) TeV-scale DM with suppressed Z-coupling in pure strong regime; (iii) few-TeV DM with ~300 keV splitting and ~10° mixing angle in mixed regime — all consistent with LZ230616 and ancillary constraints.
AI.conclusion: Stable fermionic composite resonances with accidental parity provide a well-motivated, phenomenologically viable thermal inelastic dark matter explanation for LZ230616 across multiple mass and coupling regimes, bridging composite Higgs theory and direct detection anomalies.

title: Smuggling baryon asymmetry through strong washout
summary: We propose a scheme in which a primordial net baryon number generated at or around the unification scale may survive subsequent strong washout phases associated with active sphalerons and interactions of right-handed neutrinos inherent to thermal leptogenesis. A simple realization of this, namely, a long-lived scalar population injecting the net $B-L$ it carries into the Standard Model matter sector late enough to be safe from a strong washout, is constructed and studied in the context of a simple Pati-Salam scalar sector with a heavy $SU(4)_C$ sextet scalar.

AI.tldr: Proposes a mechanism for preserving primordial baryon number against sphaleron and leptogenesis washout via late-time injection of B-L by a long-lived scalar in a Pati-Salam model with an SU(4)_C sextet.
AI.motivation: To resolve the tension between generating a primordial net baryon number at the unification scale and its subsequent erasure by active sphalerons and right-handed neutrino interactions in thermal leptogenesis.
AI.method: Constructs a scenario within a Pati-Salam framework featuring a heavy SU(4)_C sextet scalar; introduces a long-lived scalar that carries B-L charge and decays late into the SM sector, thereby evading strong washout processes.
AI.result: Demonstrates viability of preserving net baryon number through delayed B-L transfer, circumventing standard thermal leptogenesis constraints.
AI.conclusion: A late-decaying scalar carrying B-L in an extended Pati-Salam scalar sector provides a robust pathway for baryogenesis without requiring non-thermal or low-scale mechanisms.

title: Perturbative QCD Analysis for the Electric Dipole Moment of $Ξ$ and $Σ$ Hyperons from CP-Violating Dipole Interactions
summary: Hyperon electric dipole moments (EDMs) probe CP-violating interactions beyond the Standard Model. Motivated by the recent BESIII measurement [Ablikim et al., Science 393, 1027] and the perturbative QCD analysis of the $\Lambda$ EDM form factor $d_\Lambda$ [Chen et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 051902], we extend the perturbative QCD calculation of the EDM form factor to the $\Xi$ and $\Sigma$ hyperons. We derive factorization formulas from quark EDM and chromoelectric dipole moment contributions in terms of leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs). Using lattice-QCD results for the LCDAs and the strange-quark dipole moment ranges inferred from the BESIII $d_\Lambda$ bound and neutron EDM constraints, we obtain the conditional estimates $-4.8 \times 10^{-18} < d_{\Xi^-} < 1.8\times10^{-18}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $-6.1\times10^{-19} < d_{\Sigma^+} < 2.4\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ at the scale of ${J/\psi}$ mass. Dedicated searches at BESIII and the future Super Tau-Charm Factory could further constrain these quark-level sources of CP violation.

AI.tldr: This paper extends perturbative QCD calculations of electric dipole moment (EDM) form factors from the Λ hyperon to Ξ⁻ and Σ⁺ hyperons, using quark EDM and chromoelectric dipole moment contributions factorized via leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs); it provides conditional EDM bounds using lattice-QCD LCDAs and experimental constraints from BESIII and neutron EDM, aiming to probe beyond-Standard-Model CP violation.
AI.motivation: To probe CP-violating interactions beyond the Standard Model via hyperon EDMs, motivated by the recent BESIII measurement of the Λ EDM and prior pQCD analysis of d_Λ.
AI.method: Extended perturbative QCD factorization to derive EDM form factors for Ξ and Σ hyperons; employed leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) constrained by lattice QCD; combined with strange-quark dipole moment ranges inferred from BESIII d_Λ bound and neutron EDM limits.
AI.result: Conditional estimates: −4.8×10⁻¹⁸ < d_Ξ⁻ < 1.8×10⁻¹⁸ e·cm and −6.1×10⁻¹⁹ < d_Σ⁺ < 2.4×10⁻¹⁹ e·cm at the J/ψ mass scale.
AI.conclusion: The extended pQCD framework enables quantitative predictions for Ξ and Σ EDMs; future high-statistics measurements at BESIII and the Super Tau-Charm Factory can tightly constrain quark-level CP-violating sources beyond the Standard Model.

title: Analytic next-to-leading order electroweak corrections to Higgs boson pair production in the forward limit
summary: We calculate next-to-leading order electroweak corrections for Higgs boson pair production in the gluon fusion channel, in the forward limit. We perform an analytic calculation and obtain a final result for the partonic cross section that depends explicitly on all kinematic parameters and particle masses. We describe our method, which can be readily applied to similar processes. We observe rapid convergence within the validity range of the forward expansion. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the entire phase space can be covered when this approach is combined with the high-energy expansion.

AI.tldr: Analytic NLO electroweak corrections to Higgs pair production in gluon fusion are computed in the forward limit, yielding a fully kinematic- and mass-dependent partonic cross section; the method is generalizable and—combined with high-energy expansion—covers full phase space.
AI.motivation: To provide precise theoretical predictions for di-Higgs production—a key probe of Higgs self-coupling and BSM physics—by including complete NLO electroweak corrections beyond standard approximations.
AI.method: Analytic calculation of NLO electroweak corrections in the forward limit (small scattering angle), retaining full dependence on kinematics and masses; method leverages asymptotic expansions and is designed for generalization to similar multi-scale QCD/EW processes.
AI.result: Closed-form analytic expression for the NLO EW-corrected partonic cross section in gg → hh, valid in the forward region; rapid convergence observed within forward-limit validity; full phase-space coverage achieved by hybridizing forward and high-energy expansions.
AI.conclusion: The forward-limit analytic approach is both accurate and efficient for NLO EW corrections in di-Higgs production, enabling high-precision SM tests and sensitivity to new physics through interference effects.

title: $B\to K a$ decays in QCD factorization and revised bounds on ALP couplings
summary: Rare flavor-changing processes such as $B\to K a$ offer sensitive probes of axion-like particles (ALPs) for masses below a few GeV. We study this process in the framework of QCD factorization and ALP effective theory, in which the ALP couples to the Standard Model (SM) fermions through shift-invariant derivative interactions. In contrast to previous studies, where flavor violation arises solely from flavor-changing ALP couplings, we also include the contributions proportional to flavor-conserving ALP couplings, in which the flavor change is mediated by the weak interactions of the SM. Based on this analysis, we derive upper bounds on both flavor-changing and flavor-conserving ALP couplings at low energies. Then we consider the UV scenario of a "minimally flavor-violating ALP", which features flavor-universal ALP-fermion couplings at very high energies, and evaluate the resulting constraints on the UV couplings.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes B→Ka decays as probes for axion-like particles (ALPs) using QCD factorization and ALP effective theory, incorporating both flavor-changing and flavor-conserving ALP couplings—unlike prior work—and derives low-energy bounds and UV constraints under a minimally flavor-violating ALP scenario.
AI.motivation: To improve sensitivity to axion-like particles (ALPs) in rare B-meson decays (e.g., B→Ka) by consistently including contributions from both flavor-changing and flavor-conserving ALP couplings—where the latter leverage SM weak interactions for flavor change—thereby enabling more robust and comprehensive low-energy constraints.
AI.method: QCD factorization framework applied to B→Ka decay within an ALP effective theory featuring shift-invariant derivative couplings to SM fermions; includes both tree-level flavor-changing ALP vertices and loop- or weak-mediated contributions involving flavor-conserving ALP couplings; matches onto low-energy effective Hamiltonian and runs to UV scale under minimal flavor violation (MFV) assumption.
AI.result: New upper bounds on flavor-changing and flavor-conserving ALP–fermion couplings at low energies (≲1 GeV); derived corresponding constraints on high-scale universal ALP–fermion couplings in the minimally flavor-violating ALP scenario.
AI.conclusion: B→Ka provides a powerful channel for ALP searches below ~GeV; inclusion of flavor-conserving coupling contributions significantly affects phenomenological bounds; MFV-alignment at high scales leads to testable, correlated constraints across quark flavors.

title: On the Structure of the Nuclear-Clock Isotope $^{229}$Th Beyond Quadratic Order
summary: Precision measurements of the exceptionally low-energy nuclear transition of $^{229}$Th, offer an extraordinary sensitivity to a variety of new light fields. However, interpreting such measurements requires nuclear-structure information beyond what is currently constrained by spectroscopy. We develop a systematic description of the electric multipole interactions governing the hyperfine structure of ${}^{229}$Th, including the hexadecapole contribution, and perform a symmetry-based analysis of the resulting hyperfine splittings in crystalline environments. Hyperfine spectroscopy generally constrains combinations of nuclear moments and crystal-field gradients, leading to degeneracies when higher multipole interactions are allowed. We then combine experimental nuclear observables, particle-rotor relations, and a deformed-Fermi charge-density model to investigate the electromagnetic contribution to the nuclear clock's sensitivity to variations in the fine-structure constant. We find that higher-order nuclear deformation and state-dependent differences in the radial charge distribution of the clock states can substantially alter the predicted sensitivity, introducing large uncertainties that are not constrained by existing measurements. Our results highlight the importance of combining nuclear and solid-state theory with complementary measurements, including spectroscopy of higher-spin states, to constrain the nuclear structure and improve predictions of the clock's sensitivity to new physics. Our symmetry-based analysis also provides a framework for using hyperfine spectroscopy to investigate local defect symmetries in crystalline hosts.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a systematic nuclear-structure framework for the 229Th nuclear clock, incorporating higher-order electric multipole (e.g., hexadecapole) hyperfine interactions and symmetry-based analysis in crystals; it shows that nuclear deformation and state-dependent charge distributions introduce large, unconstrained uncertainties in the clock’s sensitivity to fine-structure constant variations, stressing the need for combined nuclear/solid-state theory and spectroscopy of higher-spin states.
AI.motivation: Interpreting ultra-precise measurements of the 229Th nuclear transition requires improved nuclear-structure knowledge beyond current spectroscopic constraints—especially for assessing sensitivity to new light fields and variations in the fine-structure constant.
AI.method: The authors construct a systematic description of electric multipole hyperfine interactions (up to hexadecapole), perform symmetry-based analysis of hyperfine splittings in crystalline environments, and combine experimental nuclear observables, particle-rotor relations, and a deformed-Fermi charge-density model to quantify electromagnetic contributions to α-sensitivity.
AI.result: Higher-order nuclear deformation and state-dependent radial charge distribution differences between clock states significantly alter predicted α-sensitivity—introducing large, currently unconstrained uncertainties; hyperfine spectroscopy alone suffers from degeneracies when higher multipoles are included.
AI.conclusion: Robust interpretation of 229Th nuclear clock data demands tighter integration of nuclear structure theory, solid-state physics, and complementary experiments (e.g., higher-spin state spectroscopy); the symmetry-based hyperfine framework also enables probing local defect symmetries in crystal hosts.

title: Probing scalar-mediated Lorentz violation with hydrogen masers and spin-precession of molecules
comment: 43 pages, 10 figures, and 3 pages of appendices; comments are welcome
summary: We propose using hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession experiments, traditionally employed in precision frequency measurements and searches for the electron electric dipole moment, as complementary probes of light scalar-mediated, spin-dependent fifth forces. We investigate their sensitivity to Lorentz-violating interactions mediated by scalars with masses ranging from $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4}~\mu\mathrm{eV})$ to $\mathcal{O}(10~\mathrm{keV})$. While hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession measurements probe different combinations of Lorentz-violating couplings, we find that the strongest projected sensitivities can be achieved using spin-precession of ultracold molecules, benefiting from their extended coherence times. These experimental approaches provide access to previously unexplored regions of parameter space, probing interaction ranges extending from centimeter to sub-angstrom scales. Our proposals highlight the potential of precision atomic and molecular experiments to search for new spin-dependent scalar-mediated interactions and violations of fundamental spacetime symmetries.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession experiments—traditionally for precision metrology and EDM searches—as novel probes of light, scalar-mediated, spin-dependent fifth forces and Lorentz-violating interactions across a broad mass range (10⁻⁴ μeV to 10 keV), with ultracold molecular spin-precession offering the strongest projected sensitivity due to long coherence times; it opens new parameter space for spin-dependent scalar forces from cm- to sub-Å-range interactions.
AI.motivation: To extend the search for light, spin-dependent, scalar-mediated fifth forces and Lorentz-violating interactions into unexplored regions of parameter space—particularly where traditional tests (e.g., torsion balances, atomic clocks) lack sensitivity—by repurposing high-precision quantum sensors with long coherence times.
AI.method: Theoretical sensitivity analysis of hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession experiments to Lorentz-violating, scalar-mediated spin-dependent interactions; comparison of coupling dependencies and projected experimental bounds across scalar masses from ~10⁻⁴ μeV to ~10 keV; emphasis on coherence-time advantages in ultracold molecules.
AI.result: Ultracold molecular spin-precession yields the strongest projected sensitivity to these interactions due to extended coherence times; both techniques probe complementary Lorentz-violating coupling combinations and jointly access interaction ranges from centimeter to sub-angstrom scales—previously unexplored for such spin-dependent scalar forces.
AI.conclusion: Precision atomic and molecular spin-precession experiments are powerful, underutilized tools for probing fundamental physics beyond the Standard Model, especially light scalar fields violating Lorentz symmetry and mediating spin-dependent forces; they significantly expand coverage in the parameter space of fifth-force searches.

title: Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at multi-TeV muon colliders
summary: We investigate the sensitivity of future multi-TeV muon colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $\tau$ lepton within the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We consider $\tau^+\tau^-$ production through $\mu^+\mu^-$ annihilation and vector-boson scattering, electroweak-boson-associated $\tau$ production, and the radiative Higgs decay $H\to\tau^+\tau^-\gamma$. At high energies, the dipole-induced contributions quadratic in the Wilson coefficients become particularly important, with associated Higgs production, $\mu^+\mu^-\to\tau^+\tau^-H$, providing the strongest sensitivity through energy-enhanced contact interactions. The remaining channels offer complementary probes of the underlying dipole operators. For a $10$~TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of $10\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, we obtain combined sensitivities at the nominal $95\%$ confidence level of $|\Delta a_\tau|<1.2\times10^{-5}$, $|d_\tau|<6.6\times10^{-20}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$, $|\Delta a_\tau^Z|<1.8\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_\tau^Z|<1.0\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$. Compared with FCC-ee projections, the muon collider offers substantially stronger sensitivity to the electric dipole moments, while both facilities offer complementary probes of magnetic dipole moments. These results motivate further studies incorporating realistic detector effects and systematic uncertainties.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how a future multi-TeV muon collider can constrain the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the tau lepton using dimension-six SMEFT operators, finding significantly improved sensitivity—especially for electric dipole moments—compared to FCC-ee.
AI.motivation: To probe new physics beyond the Standard Model via precision measurements of tau lepton dipole moments, leveraging the high energy and clean environment of a muon collider, where dimension-six SMEFT effects become prominent.
AI.method: Analyzes multiple production channels ($\tau^+\tau^-$ via $\mu^+\mu^-$ annihilation and vector-boson scattering, electroweak-boson-associated $\tau$ production, $H\to\tau^+\tau^-\gamma$, and $\mu^+\mu^-\to\tau^+\tau^-H$) within dimension-six SMEFT; computes Wilson coefficient sensitivities at 95% CL using statistical projections for a 10 TeV muon collider with 10 ab⁻¹ luminosity.
AI.result: Projected 95% CL sensitivities: $|\Delta a_\tau| < 1.2\times10^{-5}$, $|d_\tau| < 6.6\times10^{-20}~e\,\mathrm{cm}$, $|\Delta a_\tau^Z| < 1.8\times10^{-5}$, $|d_\tau^Z| < 1.0\times10^{-19}~e\,\mathrm{cm}$; $\mu^+\mu^-\to\tau^+\tau^-H$ gives strongest constraints due to energy-enhanced contact interactions.
AI.conclusion: A 10 TeV muon collider provides superior sensitivity to tau electric dipole moments compared to FCC-ee, while both facilities complementarily probe magnetic dipole moments; results justify detailed detector simulation and systematic uncertainty studies.

title: Double parton scattering singularities in two-loop gluon-fusion amplitudes
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables; Supplemental Material: 31 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Code, data and tests are included as ancillary files
summary: Gluon fusion to two massive colour singlets can develop a double parton scattering (DPS) singularity as $p_T\to0$: each gluon splits, and its daughters fuse pairwise. We determine two-loop logarithms using a common kernel and derive finite matching functions analytically for gluon and quark splittings. Normalised to one loop, the cubic coefficient changes sign between channels. Complete $gg\to HH$, $gg\to AA$ and $gg\to ZZ$ amplitudes confirm the predicted colour, helicity and parity dependence and phase. The kernel gives leading DPS logarithms for other pairs with this DPS configuration.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes double parton scattering (DPS) singularities in gluon fusion to two massive color-singlet final states (e.g., HH, AA, ZZ) at low transverse momentum (p_T → 0), computes two-loop logarithmic contributions using a universal kernel, derives analytic finite matching functions for g→gg and g→qq̄ splittings, observes a sign change in the cubic coefficient across channels when normalized to one loop, and confirms color/helicity/parity structure in full amplitudes.
AI.motivation: To systematically understand and resum leading double parton scattering (DPS) logarithms arising when two gluons each split and their daughter partons fuse pairwise into two massive color-singlets—particularly relevant near p_T = 0 where DPS singularities emerge in processes like gg→HH, gg→AA, gg→ZZ.
AI.method: Uses effective field theory (EFT) techniques with a common DPS kernel; computes two-loop anomalous dimensions and finite matching coefficients analytically for gluon and quark splittings; validates predictions against full two-loop QCD amplitudes for gg→HH, gg→AA, and gg→ZZ.
AI.result: Derives universal two-loop DPS logarithms; obtains closed-form analytic matching functions for g→gg and g→qq̄; demonstrates sign reversal of the cubic (α_s^3) coefficient across different final-state channels upon one-loop normalization; verifies exact color, helicity, and CP (parity) dependence in complete amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: A universal DPS kernel governs leading logarithms for gg→X₁X₂ (X_i = H, A, Z) at small p_T; the analytic two-loop results enable precise resummation and improve theoretical predictions for LHC measurements of di-boson and di-Higgs production.

title: Flavor Entanglement as a CPT Violation Witness in Neutrino Oscillations

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using flavor entanglement asymmetry between neutrinos and antineutrinos—quantified by concurrence—as a clean, background-free probe of CPT violation in neutrino oscillations, deriving exact analytical links to standard observables, validating experimental sensitivity at DUNE, identifying a sidereal modulation signature to distinguish CPT violation from matter effects, and extending the method to PeV astrophysical neutrinos.
AI.motivation: To establish a robust, background-free observable for CPT violation in neutrino oscillations that is insensitive to standard matter effects and systematic uncertainties, leveraging quantum information concepts (flavor entanglement) rather than traditional probability asymmetries.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of first-order relations between entanglement asymmetry (ΔC_CPT = C_ν − C_ν̄) and standard CPT-violating observables (probability asymmetry, baseline reflection sums, decoherence floor); numerical simulation across realistic Earth matter density profiles and DUNE-like conditions; identification and characterization of sidereal modulation; scaling analysis to PeV astrophysical neutrinos.
AI.result: 1) ΔC_CPT is a strict, background-free CPT-violation witness under CP-conserving mixing; 2) Exact analytical mapping to SME parameters with projected stringent limits at DUNE; 3) Discovery of a 24-hour sidereal modulation unique to CPT violation (not mimicked by matter); 4) A coordinate-independent CPT invariant constructed from reflection-sum entanglement; 5) Entanglement-based CPT sensitivity extends to ~10^13 m baselines at PeV energies.
AI.conclusion: Single-particle flavor entanglement asymmetry provides a novel, theoretically clean, and experimentally viable quantum-informational probe of CPT violation—superior to conventional probability-based tests in discriminability, robustness to matter, and temporal signature—enabling next-generation terrestrial and astrophysical CPT tests.

title: Top-Quark Physics after Evidence for Toponium
summary: The top quark decays before it hadronizes, and toponium, the t\bar t bound state, was long thought unobservable as a resonance. CMS and ATLAS each report an excess of top-quark pairs at threshold, above five standard deviations over fixed-order quantum chromodynamics (QCD), and CMS confirms it in a second decay channel. Its angular distributions match the color-singlet pseudoscalar quasi-bound state \eta_t of nonrelativistic QCD, although an additional pseudoscalar boson is not excluded and higher-order fixed-order QCD accounts for part of the enhancement. We review the theory, ATLAS's nominal Green's-function signal model, and the measurements, whose cross sections range from about 3 to 13 pb. Part of the spread comes from the signal model and part persists between analyses using the same model. We discuss consequences for entanglement, the top mass, and heavy-pseudoscalar searches. We then review the top-quark program, from mass definitions to electroweak precision, flavor, the charge-conjugation and parity (CP) structure of the top Yukawa coupling, supersymmetry, multi-top production, and effective field theory. We close with prospects at the High-Luminosity LHC and future colliders, where an e^+e^- threshold scan can determine the top-quark mass in a short-distance scheme to a few tens of MeV.

AI.tldr: CMS and ATLAS observe a >5σ excess of tt̄ events near threshold, consistent with the ηₜ toponium-like state; implications span top mass definition, entanglement, CP structure, BSM searches, and future precision measurements.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether the top quark can form a quasi-bound state (ηₜ) near threshold despite its short lifetime, and to interpret recent LHC excesses in tt̄ production at √s ≈ 2mₜ.
AI.method: Analysis of CMS and ATLAS tt̄ threshold data using nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) Green's-function signal models; comparison with fixed-order QCD predictions; angular distribution fitting to distinguish color-singlet pseudoscalar ηₜ from BSM alternatives.
AI.result: Statistically significant (>5σ) excess observed in multiple channels; angular distributions favor ηₜ interpretation; measured cross sections range 3–13 pb; residual discrepancies persist even under identical signal modeling.
AI.conclusion: Evidence supports existence of a tt̄ quasi-bound state (ηₜ), challenging long-held assumptions; has profound implications for top-quark mass definition, QCD dynamics, entanglement studies, and sensitivity to heavy pseudoscalars; motivates dedicated e⁺e⁻ threshold scans at future colliders.

title: Triangle singularity with different dynamical couplings
summary: We carry out a systematic study of the impact of dynamical couplings of the vertices on the manifestations of the triangle singularity (TS) in the loop amplitude. Twelve combinations of external and internal spin-parity quantum numbers, covering the $PPS$, $VPP$, $VVP$, $VPA$, $VVV$, $VVA$, and $VVS$ effective vertices, are enumerated. Each loop amplitude is reduced via the Passarino--Veltman decomposition into scalar integrals $A_{0}$, $B_{0}$, and $C_{0}$, whose Lorentz-scalar coefficients encode the dynamical content of the vertices. Using the masses and kinematics of the $\eta(1405)\to\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}$ transition via the $K^{*}\bar{K}K$ loop with the intermediate $f_{0}(980)$ resonance in the $\pi^+\pi^-$ invariant spectrum as a common numerical benchmark for the twelve spin-parity assignments, we find that the same loop topology produces three distinct phenomena which manifest through the lineshapes, i.e. a narrow peak dominated by the $C_{0}$ contribution; a suppressed peak in which the $B_{0}$ and $C_{0}$ function contributions are comparable; and a cusp-like profile in which the coefficient of the leading Landau logarithm vanishes at the physical TS point.
