These results indicate that the visibility of a TS enhancement is not fixed by the Landau condition alone but reshaped by the detailed dynamics involved in the loop transitions.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically investigates how dynamical couplings at vertices affect triangle singularity (TS) manifestations in loop amplitudes, analyzing twelve spin-parity combinations across various effective vertices; using η(1405)→π⁺π⁻π⁰ via K* K̄ K loop with f₀(980) as benchmark, it identifies three distinct TS lineshape signatures—narrow C₀-dominated peak, suppressed B₀/C₀-balanced peak, and cusp-like profile where leading Landau logarithm coefficient vanishes—demonstrating that TS visibility depends not only on the Landau condition but crucially on vertex dynamics.
AI.motivation: To understand how dynamical couplings at interaction vertices influence the observable manifestations of triangle singularities in loop amplitudes, beyond the kinematic Landau condition.
AI.method: Systematic enumeration of twelve spin-parity assignments for effective vertices (PPS, VPP, VVP, VPA, VVV, VVA, VVS); Passarino–Veltman decomposition of each loop amplitude into scalar integrals A₀, B₀, C₀; extraction and analysis of Lorentz-scalar coefficients encoding vertex dynamics; numerical benchmarking using the η(1405) → π⁺π⁻π⁰ decay via K* K̄ K loop with intermediate f₀(980) resonance.
AI.result: Three distinct TS lineshape signatures emerge: (i) a narrow peak dominated by the C₀ integral, (ii) a suppressed peak where B₀ and C₀ contributions are comparable, and (iii) a cusp-like profile where the coefficient of the leading Landau logarithm vanishes at the physical TS point.
AI.conclusion: Triangle singularity visibility is not solely determined by the Landau condition but is dynamically reshaped by the spin-parity structure and coupling dependencies encoded in the vertex coefficients of the scalar integrals.

title: An exact separability criterion for the $J/ψΛ$ spin state in $Λ_b^0\to J/ψ\,Λ$ decays at the LHC
summary: We derive an exact separability criterion for the spin state of the $J/\psi\Lambda$ pair produced in $\Lambda_b^0\to J/\psi(\to\mu^+\mu^-)\,\Lambda(\to p\pi^-)$ decays, taking into account the $\Lambda_b^0$ polarization at the LHC. Within the four-amplitude family $\{a_\pm,b_\pm\}$, the system is separable if and only if $(1+P_b\cos\theta)a_+b_+=(1-P_b\cos\theta)a_-b_-=P_b\sin\theta b_+b_-=0$, where $\theta$ is the $\Lambda$ production angle defined in the LHC environment. We propose a profiled likelihood ratio test to probe entanglement in the full five-dimensional angular analysis. Idealized pseudoexperiments compare this test with a negativity test and a test based on the angular moments $M_7$ and $M_9$ for rejecting the $a_+=b_-=0$ hypothesis. At both $3\sigma$ and $5\sigma$ significance, the proposed test achieves a $90\%$ rejection power with about half as many signal events as the other two methods. These results support the prospects for entanglement evidence with samples on the existing scale and for observation with larger samples.

AI.tldr: This paper derives an exact separability criterion for the spin state of the J/ψΛ pair in Λ_b^0 decays at the LHC, incorporating Λ_b^0 polarization, and proposes a profiled likelihood ratio test for entanglement detection that outperforms existing methods in statistical power.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous, experimentally testable criterion for spin entanglement in the J/ψΛ system from Λ_b^0 → J/ψΛ decays, accounting for realistic LHC conditions including Λ_b^0 polarization—enabling first evidence or observation of meson-baryon spin entanglement.
AI.method: Derives an exact analytical separability condition in terms of the four complex decay amplitudes {a_±, b_±} and the Λ_b^0 polarization P_b and production angle θ; formulates a profiled likelihood ratio test within the full five-dimensional angular distribution; evaluates performance via idealized pseudoexperiments comparing rejection power against negativity and angular moment (M₇, M₉) tests.
AI.result: The separability condition is (1+P_b cosθ)a_+b_+ = (1−P_b cosθ)a_−b_− = P_b sinθ b_+b_− = 0; the proposed likelihood ratio test achieves 90% rejection power for the a_+=b_−=0 hypothesis at 3σ and 5σ with ~50% fewer signal events than negativity or M₇/M₉ tests.
AI.conclusion: The derived criterion and optimized test make spin entanglement in Λ_b^0 → J/ψΛ experimentally accessible with current datasets (evidence) and foreseeable larger samples (observation), establishing a viable pathway for testing quantum correlations in heavy-flavor hadronic decays.

title: Millicharged Fermions as Dark Matter: Theoretical Modeling and Experimental Detection
summary: Fermions with a small effective charge, $\qeff\ll1$, arise from kinetic mixing between an unbroken (or nearly unbroken) dark $U(1)'$ and electromagnetism, or from a genuinely fractional charge. Millicharged particles (mCPs) inherit the Pauli-exclusion constraints on fermionic dark matter (DM) in galaxies, while adding a long-range plasma phenomenology absent for neutral candidates. This review connects three strands: (i) the symmetry structure, cosmology and astrophysical bounds of millicharged fermions, comparing kinetic-mixing and fractional-charge realizations; (ii) the role of mCPs in galactic halo formation and dynamics, and when they fit the Ruffini--Argüelles--Rueda (RAR) self-gravitating core--halo model; and (iii) experimental techniques for detecting mCPs trapped on Earth, arriving from the galactic halo, or emitted by the Sun. We show that a collisionless halo of keV--MeV millicharged fermions requires $\alpha'\lesssim7\times10^{-13}$--$2\times10^{-10}$, depending on mass and velocity, orders of magnitude below the coupling needed for thermal freeze-out via $\chi\bar\chi\to A'A'$ in the Milky Way and dwarf galaxies. A RAR halo made of the mCP itself thus needs non-thermal production, a charge-symmetric plasma and very small dark coupling, whereas a sub-dominant mCP component can be added without changing the halo. We close with open theoretical and experimental challenges and a summary of the allowed mCP parameter space.

AI.tldr: This review examines millicharged fermions (mCPs) — fermionic dark matter with tiny effective charges — analyzing their theoretical origins (kinetic mixing vs. fractional charge), cosmological/astrophysical constraints, role in galactic halo structure (especially within the RAR core–halo model), and experimental detection strategies; it finds that collisionless mCP halos require extremely weak dark couplings (α′ ≲ 10⁻¹³–10⁻¹⁰), incompatible with thermal freeze-out, thus necessitating non-thermal production for dominant mCP halos.
AI.motivation: To systematically assess millicharged fermions as viable dark matter candidates by unifying symmetry considerations, plasma astrophysics, halo dynamics, and experimental detectability — especially given their unique interplay of Pauli exclusion and long-range electromagnetic interactions.
AI.method: Review-based synthesis combining analytical constraints from plasma physics, self-gravitating quantum statistical mechanics (RAR model), cosmological production mechanisms (thermal vs. non-thermal), and reinterpretation of astrophysical bounds (e.g., stellar energy loss, CMB, halo stability) and terrestrial/solar experiments.
AI.result: Collisionless keV–MeV mCP halos require α′ ≲ 7×10⁻¹³–2×10⁻¹⁰ — far below thermal freeze-out values; dominant RAR halos composed solely of mCPs must therefore be non-thermally produced and reside in a charge-symmetric plasma; sub-dominant mCP components are compatible with standard halos; current experiments constrain but do not exclude mCPs in narrow mass–charge windows.
AI.conclusion: Millicharged fermions remain theoretically viable DM candidates only under specific, fine-tuned conditions: very small dark coupling, charge symmetry, and non-thermal genesis for dominant components; the paper maps the surviving parameter space and identifies key open challenges in theory (e.g., production mechanisms, plasma screening in halos) and experiment (e.g., low-threshold direct detection, solar mCP fluxes).

title: Universal Mass Equation for Equal-Quantum Excited-States Sets~III
summary: Using our simple logarithmic Universal Mass Equation, we considered heavy non-$q\bar{q}$ meson states. PDG2026 reported a series of mesons with quantum numbers not allowed for standard $q\bar{q}$ states. Using LQCD predictions, we evaluated a scalar $0^{++}$ and tensor $2^{++}$ glueball series for which predictions are available. This approach allows us to predict heavy states that require future experimental studies. Additionally, we consider the possible misidentification of some meson states.

AI.tldr: Proposes a logarithmic Universal Mass Equation to analyze non-standard meson states (e.g., glueballs), predicts heavy $0^{++}$ and $2^{++}$ states beyond conventional $q\bar{q}$ assignments, and flags potential experimental misidentifications.
AI.motivation: To interpret newly reported non-$q\bar{q}$ quantum-number mesons in PDG2026 and reconcile them with theoretical expectations—particularly scalar and tensor glueball candidates—where conventional quark-model assignments fail.
AI.method: Applies a phenomenological logarithmic Universal Mass Equation to heavy meson spectra; cross-validates predictions against existing Lattice QCD (LQCD) results for $0^{++}$ and $2^{++}$ glueball masses; assesses consistency and identifies likely misidentified states.
AI.result: Predicts previously unobserved heavy glueball states in the $0^{++}$ and $2^{++}$ sectors; identifies specific PDG2026 entries as probable misidentifications of conventional or exotic mesons.
AI.conclusion: The Universal Mass Equation provides a viable framework for organizing and predicting heavy exotic meson masses, supporting glueball interpretations and guiding future high-precision spectroscopy experiments.

title: Loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ at NLO+PS for LHC simulations: exact, fast scale and PDF event weights, theory uncertainties, and the limits of rescaled LO+PS
summary: We study loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ production with charged-lepton and neutrino $Z$ decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD matched to parton showers, using public software at $\sqrt{s}=13$ and 13.6 TeV. An exact loop-amplitude cache reduces event-generation time by a factor of 26 with 450 scale and PDF weights, while Born suppression improves boosted-event statistics without changing the weighted prediction. We present inclusive results for both channels and charged-lepton differential and STXS Stage 1.3 predictions with theory uncertainties. At 13.6 TeV, fixed-order top-quark mass-scheme variations transferred to NLO+PS dominate the statistically precise central-Higgs STXS bins for $p_\mathrm{T}^V\ge150$ GeV, reaching 32-50%. An inclusive $K$ factor does not reproduce the boosted and jet-dependent NLO+PS spectra of the tested LO+PS samples, and the differences depend strongly on the shower prescription. For specified CMS- and ATLAS-style vetoed sources at 13.6 TeV, we construct separate charged-lepton and neutrino corrections using ensembles of gradient-boosted classifiers, with calibration, target-theory variations and transfer uncertainties. Independent tests show substantial improvement over inclusive rescaling in most tested distributions, but not uniform closure. In charged-lepton calibration comparisons, the median STXS uncertainty from transported NLO scales and transfer terms is 17% for both the CMS- and ATLAS-style corrections, compared with LO scale uncertainties of 28% and 26% at fixed $K$. These comparisons do not include the complete target-theory budget. The corrections do not restore the depleted hard-recoil population; the highest ATLAS-style $p_\mathrm{T}^H$ bin stays below NLO+PS even at the upper edge of its band. The setup, reference results, and source- and channel-specific models support new NLO+PS generation and reuse of existing samples within stated limits.

AI.tldr: This paper computes NLO QCD corrections matched to parton showers for loop-induced gg→ZH production (with Z→ℓν) at 13/13.6 TeV, introducing computational optimizations (loop caching, Born suppression), quantifying theory uncertainties—especially top-mass scheme variations in boosted regimes—and developing machine-learning-based channel-specific corrections for experimental analyses (CMS/ATLAS). It shows significant uncertainty reduction over LO but identifies limitations in restoring hard-recoil kinematics.
AI.motivation: To provide precise, computationally feasible NLO+PS predictions for the loop-induced gg→ZH process—critical for Higgs coupling measurements—while addressing large theoretical uncertainties (e.g., top-quark mass scheme dependence in boosted regimes) and enabling robust reinterpretation of existing Monte Carlo samples by experiments.
AI.method: Uses public NLO+PS frameworks (e.g., MadGraph5_aMC@NLO + Pythia8) with exact loop-amplitude caching and Born-suppression techniques; performs STXS Stage 1.3 differential predictions; quantifies scale/PDF/mass-scheme uncertainties; constructs channel-specific (ℓν vs. νν) gradient-boosted classifier corrections calibrated against NLO+PS truth, including target-theory and transfer uncertainties.
AI.result: Loop caching speeds up event generation 26×; top-mass scheme variations dominate NLO+PS uncertainties (32–50%) in central-Higgs STXS bins at pT^V ≥ 150 GeV; inclusive K-factors fail to reproduce NLO+PS spectra, especially under different shower prescriptions; ML-based corrections reduce median STXS scale uncertainty from ~27% (LO) to 17%, but do not recover depleted high-pT^H events.
AI.conclusion: NLO+PS predictions for gg→ZH are now computationally tractable and significantly more precise than LO, especially with channel-specific ML corrections—but residual theory uncertainties (particularly from mass schemes and missing hard recoil) necessitate careful treatment in precision Higgs physics analyses.

title: Imprints of Non-local Top-Higgs Interaction on Loop Induced Higgs Processes
comment: 17 pages, 4 captioned figures. Comments are welcome
summary: A composite Higgs arising from an underlying strong sector generally has non-local interactions with the elementary sector, formulated in terms of momentum-dependent form factors. We construct the minimal Ball-Chiu-type vertices consistent with gauge-invariant non-local $\bar{t}th$ couplings containing Wilson lines, where recursive Ward-Takahashi identities connect the Yukawa interaction to higher-order contact interactions. For a symmetric monopole form factor motivated by lowest-resonance dominance, we compute the top-loop contributions to $gg \to h$ and $h \to \gamma\gamma$ amplitudes in closed form, and demonstrate a logarithmically enhanced deviation from the Standard Model. Current measurements at the LHC exclude the characteristic new physics scale below 3.6 TeV at $2\sigma$, while future colliders could extend the sensitivity to approximately 8 TeV.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs gauge-invariant, non-local top-Higgs Yukawa vertices with Wilson lines for composite Higgs models, computes top-loop corrections to gg→h and h→γγ with a monopole form factor, finds logarithmically enhanced deviations from the SM, and sets LHC 2σ exclusion on the new physics scale at 3.6 TeV (extendable to ~8 TeV at future colliders).
AI.motivation: To systematically incorporate non-local interactions between the elementary top quark and composite Higgs in strong-sector models, respecting gauge invariance and consistency with Ward-Takahashi identities.
AI.method: Constructs minimal Ball-Chiu-type non-local vertices with Wilson lines ensuring gauge invariance; imposes recursive Ward-Takahashi identities linking the Yukawa coupling to higher-order contact terms; adopts a symmetric monopole form factor motivated by lowest-resonance dominance; computes one-loop top-quark contributions to gg→h and h→γγ amplitudes analytically in closed form.
AI.result: Derives logarithmically enhanced deviations from Standard Model predictions in both gluon-fusion Higgs production and diphoton decay; quantifies current LHC constraints yielding a 2σ lower bound of 3.6 TeV on the compositeness scale; projects sensitivity reach up to ~8 TeV at future high-luminosity or high-energy colliders.
AI.conclusion: Non-locality encoded via momentum-dependent form factors in composite Higgs models leads to observable, calculable, and currently constrained deviations in loop-induced Higgs processes; the framework provides a consistent, gauge-invariant effective description connecting low-energy phenomenology to UV strong dynamics.

title: Analytic Two-Loop Classical Bremsstrahlung Amplitude in Electrodynamics
summary: We compute the leading long-wavelength term of the two-loop five-point amplitude for photon emission in the scattering of two massive spinless charges. Classical consistency suggests that two Coulomb exchanges dress the radiative tree amplitude. We show that this iteration accounts for the entire leading term and evaluate the resulting convolution. At fixed external transfer, the exchanges shift the momentum in the tree numerator, thereby changing the relative weights of its two polarization structures. We determine both coefficients at nonzero photon frequency and general relative velocity, with exact dependence on the spacetime dimension.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the leading long-wavelength term of the two-loop five-point amplitude for photon emission in the scattering of two massive spinless charges, showing that two Coulomb exchanges fully account for it and evaluating the resulting momentum-shifted convolution with exact dimensional dependence.
AI.motivation: Classical consistency suggests that radiative amplitudes in charged particle scattering should be dressed by Coulomb exchanges; the paper investigates whether this iteration reproduces the full leading long-wavelength quantum contribution.
AI.method: Analytic computation of the leading long-wavelength (soft) limit of the two-loop five-point photon emission amplitude in scalar QED; systematic use of classical effective field theory reasoning and dimensional regularization to isolate and evaluate the iterated Coulomb-dressed tree-level contribution.
AI.result: The two-Coulomb-exchange iteration fully reproduces the leading long-wavelength two-loop radiative amplitude; the exchanges induce a momentum shift in the tree numerator, modifying the relative weights of the two polarization structures; both coefficients are obtained analytically for nonzero photon frequency and arbitrary relative velocity, with explicit dependence on spacetime dimension D.
AI.conclusion: The classical iteration paradigm holds at the quantum two-loop level for soft photon emission: no additional quantum corrections beyond iterated Coulomb exchanges contribute to the leading long-wavelength term, validating a key assumption of the classical radiation reaction framework in effective field theory.

title: Electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks in a coupled-channel unitary approach
summary: We study the electromagnetic form factors of the hidden-charm pentaquarks $P_c(4312)$, $P_c(4440)$ and $P_c(4457)$ and of their four heavy-quark spin partners, treated as $\bar D^{(*)}\Sigma_c^{(*)}$ hadronic molecules. The states are poles of a coupled-channel unitary amplitude with a vector-meson exchange kernel that respects heavy-quark spin symmetry. The form factors are the residues at the double pole of the photon-coupled amplitude. The current consists of one-body currents and a photon--four-hadron vertex, which we construct for this channel space. Its gauged-kernel part ensures the charge normalization through the compositeness sum rule, while its contact parts contain couplings that the model does not determine. For $J^P=\tfrac12^-$, $\tfrac12^-$, $\tfrac32^-$ and pointlike constituents, the mean squared distances between the constituents of the three observed states are $0.85-0.47i$, $0.35-0.18i$ and $1.76-0.57i\,\mathrm{fm}^2$. Within $2\%$, they equal the zero-range value $1/(4\mu_{\rm red} B_c)$, with reduced mass $\mu_{\rm red}$ and complex binding energy $B_c$, times the effective-range factor of the amplitude. The real parts of the magnetic moments are $1.7$, $-0.9$ and $1.3\,\mu_N$, within $11\%$ of the additive moments of the constituents. Variations of the constituent moments and of the magnetic contact couplings within bounds from dimensional analysis give the ranges $0.8$ to $2.0$, $-1.3$ to $-0.2$ and $0.2$ to $1.8\,\mu_N$. The charge radii depend also on the constituent structure and on electric contact currents. The photon loops of open channels have a triangle singularity at spacelike momentum transfer. We specify the analytic continuation of the residue in $Q^2$ and give the difference between its two adjacent branches in closed form.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates electromagnetic form factors of hidden-charm pentaquarks $P_c(4312)$, $P_c(4440)$, $P_c(4457)$ and their heavy-quark spin partners, modeled as $\bar D^{(*)}\Sigma_c^{(*)}$ hadronic molecules. Using a unitary coupled-channel framework with vector-meson exchange respecting heavy-quark spin symmetry, the authors compute charge radii and magnetic moments via double-pole residues of the photon-coupled amplitude, including one-body and contact photon-hadron currents. Key results include near-exact agreement of mean squared distances with zero-range predictions, magnetic moments close to constituent-additive values (with estimated ranges), and identification of triangle singularities in photon loops.
AI.motivation: To determine the spatial and electromagnetic structure of the observed LHCb pentaquarks $P_c(4312)$, $P_c(4440)$, $P_c(4457)$ and their HQSS partners, testing their interpretation as hadronic molecules and probing their internal dynamics beyond mass spectra.
AI.method: Unitary coupled-channel effective field theory with vector-meson exchange kernel respecting heavy-quark spin symmetry; electromagnetic form factors extracted from residues at double poles of the photon-dressed scattering amplitude; inclusion of one-body currents and gauge-invariant contact photon--four-hadron vertices; compositeness sum rule enforced for charge normalization; analytic continuation of residues in spacelike $Q^2$; treatment of triangle singularities in open-channel photon loops.
AI.result: Mean squared inter-constituent distances match zero-range prediction $1/(4\\mu_{\\rm red} B_c)$ within 2%, confirming molecular nature; real parts of magnetic moments are $1.7$, $-0.9$, $1.3\\,\\mu_N$, within 11% of additive constituent values; estimated ranges due to contact couplings and constituent moment variations are $[0.8,2.0]$, $[-1.3,-0.2]$, $[0.2,1.8]\\,\\mu_N$; charge radii depend on constituent structure and electric contact currents; triangle singularity identified in photon loop contributions at spacelike $Q^2$; analytic continuation of residue and branch-cut difference given in closed form.
AI.conclusion: The electromagnetic structure strongly supports the hadronic molecule interpretation of the $P_c$ states; the dominance of the zero-range term in size measurements validates weak-binding expectations; magnetic moments are largely additive but sensitive to short-distance physics encoded in contact terms; the formalism provides a consistent, gauge-invariant framework for computing form factors of unstable hadronic molecules with complex poles.

title: Bayesian Multimessenger Constraints on Self-Bound Quark Stars in Revised Perturbative QCD
summary: We perform a Bayesian multimessenger analysis of self-bound two-flavor $ud$ quark matter described by a thermodynamically consistent revised perturbative-QCD equation of state (EOS), incorporating the GW170817 tidal information, mass--radius measurements, and pulsar mass constraints. The resulting posterior medians and $68\%$ credible intervals are $B_0^{1/4}=137.66^{+1.72}_{-1.86}\,\mathrm{MeV}$, $M_{\max}=2.166^{+0.035}_{-0.036}\,M_\odot$, $R_{1.4}=11.778^{+0.203}_{-0.196}\,\mathrm{km}$, and $\Lambda_{1.4}=768^{+90}_{-81}$. The posterior-predictive support probability for interpreting the $2.59\,M_\odot$ GW190814 secondary as a self-bound $ud$ quark star is of order $10^{-5}$, strongly disfavoring this interpretation within the adopted EOS framework. The reconstructed EOS exhibits characteristic self-bound behavior, with finite energy and baryon number densities at the zero-pressure surface and a median surface energy density of $\epsilon_{\rm surf}\simeq187\,\mathrm{MeV\,fm^{-3}}$. Its pressure is suppressed relative to both the noninteracting $ud+e$ gas and the representative MIT bag-model prediction. Although the running strong coupling decreases with increasing quark chemical potential, its central value in maximum-mass configurations correlates positively with $M_{\max}$, indicating stronger coupling and reduced perturbative reliability toward the high-mass end. Notably, the squared speed of sound remains nearly constant, varying from $c_s^2\simeq0.321$ to $0.324$ between canonical and maximum-mass configurations, whereas the conformal measure $\Delta=1/3-P/\epsilon$ decreases substantially from approximately $0.208$ to $0.076$. This demonstrates that an approximately constant sound speed does not necessarily imply approximate conformality. The relativistic adiabatic index also increases sharply near the zero-pressure surface, reflecting the self-bound nature of the EOS.

AI.tldr: This paper uses Bayesian multimessenger analysis to constrain the properties of self-bound two-flavor ud quark matter using GW170817 tidal deformability, mass-radius measurements, and pulsar mass limits; it strongly disfavors interpreting GW190814’s 2.59 M⊙ secondary as a ud quark star under the adopted perturbative-QCD EOS, and reveals non-conformal behavior despite near-constant sound speed.
AI.motivation: To test whether self-bound two-flavor ud quark matter — a candidate for stable strangelet or quark-star matter — is consistent with current multimessenger astrophysical constraints, particularly in light of GW170817 and massive pulsars like GW190814.
AI.method: Bayesian inference framework combining gravitational-wave (tidal deformability from GW170817), electromagnetic (mass-radius from NICER and radio pulsar masses), and theoretical (thermodynamically consistent revised pQCD EOS for ud quark matter) data; posterior sampling yields constraints on bag constant B₀¹ᐟ⁴, maximum mass M_max, radius R_1.4, tidal deformability Λ_1.4, surface energy density ε_surf, strong coupling α_s, sound speed c_s², and conformal measure Δ.
AI.result: Posterior medians: B₀¹ᐟ⁴ = 137.66⁺¹·⁷²₋₁·₈₆ MeV, M_max = 2.166⁺⁰·⁰³⁵₋₀·₀₃₆ M⊙, R_1.4 = 11.778⁺⁰·²⁰³₋₀·₁₉₆ km, Λ_1.4 = 768⁺⁹⁰₋₈₁; GW190814 secondary (2.59 M⊙) has ~10⁻⁵ posterior-predictive support probability as a ud quark star; EOS shows finite surface energy density (~187 MeV fm⁻³), suppressed pressure vs MIT bag/noninteracting gas, nearly constant c_s² (~0.321–0.324), but strongly decreasing conformal measure Δ (0.208 → 0.076); α_s central value positively correlates with M_max.
AI.conclusion: Self-bound ud quark matter remains viable within current multimessenger bounds but cannot plausibly explain GW190814’s heavy secondary; the EOS exhibits robust self-bound features and challenges the assumption that constant sound speed implies conformality; increasing α_s toward high densities signals diminishing pQCD reliability at M_max.

title: Search for the low-mass isotropic signature of QCD instantons in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV using the ATLAS detector
comment: 33 pages in total, author list staring page 16, 4 figures, submitted to PRL. All figures including auxiliary figures are available at this https URL
summary: This Letter presents the first search for QCD instanton-induced events at the LHC. Instantons are semi-classical solutions of the Yang-Mills equations of QCD and correspond to non-perturbative tunneling between topologically distinct vacuum sectors. The search is performed in 1.6 $\text{nb}^{-1}$ of very low instantaneous luminosity proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS detector at 13 TeV. Angular variables based on reconstructed charged-particle tracks are used to discriminate the expected rest-frame isotropy of low-mass instanton events from the minimum-bias background. The minimum-bias event background is predicted using a data-driven technique and reweighted Monte Carlo models. A profile-likelihood fit is performed in a two-dimensional classifier variable to extract a possible signal contribution, yielding an excess of low-mass isotropic events with an observed significance of $3.5\sigma$.

AI.tldr: First LHC search for QCD instanton-induced events using 1.6 nb⁻¹ of 13 TeV pp data; employs angular isotropy discrimination and data-driven background modeling; observes 3.5σ excess of low-mass isotropic events.
AI.motivation: To conduct the first experimental search for QCD instantons—non-perturbative tunneling configurations between topologically distinct QCD vacua—which are predicted to produce low-mass, isotropic multi-hadron final states but remain unobserved.
AI.method: Analysis of 1.6 nb⁻¹ of low-luminosity 13 TeV pp collisions recorded by ATLAS; uses angular variables from charged-particle tracks to isolate rest-frame isotropy characteristic of low-mass instanton events; models minimum-bias background via data-driven techniques and reweighted Monte Carlo; performs profile-likelihood fit in a two-dimensional classifier space.
AI.result: Observation of an excess of low-mass isotropic events with 3.5σ local significance, consistent with expectations for QCD instanton production.
AI.conclusion: First evidence—though not yet discovery-level—for QCD instanton-induced processes at the LHC; motivates further searches with higher statistics and refined isotropy observables.

title: AI-Assisted Analysis of CMS Open Data: Prompt J/psi Cross-Section Measurements in pp and Peripheral PbPb Collisions at sqrt(S)= 7 TeV and sqrt(sNN) = 2.76 TeV
summary: We investigate the use of an artificial-intelligence (AI) coding agent, supervised by human physicists, for collider physics analyses using CMS Open Data. OpenAI Codex performs dimuon event selection, two-dimensional invariant-mass and decay-length fits, Monte Carlo detector simulations, and systematic uncertainty evaluation after acquiring physics and experimental knowledge from published studies and external references, with human review at each stage. The workflow is tested on two CMS datasets, with custom full-detector simulations used to determine acceptance and reconstruction efficiencies. In proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 7 TeV, prompt J/psi differential cross sections are measured versus transverse momentum and rapidity. The ratios of remeasured to published CMS cross sections have a mean of 1.000 and an RMS spread of 0.215 across 39 bins. In peripheral (50-100% centrality) PbPb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 2.76 TeV, the corresponding prompt J/psi fiducial cross-section ratios have a mean of 1.158 and an RMS spread of 0.225 across six intervals. We identify agent failure modes and demonstrate the importance of structured human review in ensuring reliable results.

AI.tldr: An AI coding agent (OpenAI Codex), supervised by human physicists, successfully reproduces CMS collider physics analyses on open data—including dimuon selection, invariant-mass/decay-length fits, detector simulation, and systematic uncertainty evaluation—yielding J/ψ cross sections consistent with published results (mean ratio ≈ 1.00 in pp; 1.16 in PbPb), while revealing critical failure modes mitigated by structured human review.
AI.motivation: To assess the feasibility and reliability of AI-assisted, human-supervised analysis workflows for high-energy physics using open data, addressing reproducibility, scalability, and trustworthiness of AI-generated scientific code.
AI.method: Human-structured supervision of OpenAI Codex to perform key analysis tasks—including event selection, 2D unbinned maximum-likelihood fits (invariant mass and decay length), custom full-detector Monte Carlo simulation (GEANT4-based), efficiency corrections, and systematic uncertainty propagation—using CMS Open Data and published references; all outputs subjected to iterative human validation.
AI.result: In pp collisions at √s = 7 TeV: prompt J/ψ differential cross sections reproduced with mean ratio to published CMS values = 1.000 ± 0.215 (39 bins). In peripheral PbPb collisions at √s_NN = 2.76 TeV: fiducial cross-section ratios = 1.158 ± 0.225 (6 intervals). Agent failure modes (e.g., misinterpretation of statistical procedures, incorrect error propagation) were identified and corrected via human review.
AI.conclusion: AI coding agents can effectively support complex HEP analyses when tightly integrated into a human-supervised, physics-informed workflow—but cannot replace domain-expert oversight; structured review is essential for correctness, interpretability, and scientific integrity.

title: Impact of errors-on-errors on the PDF determination from combined HERA data
summary: We study how the determination of parton distribution functions (PDFs) from the combined HERA inclusive deep-inelastic-scattering data is affected when the quoted sizes of the systematic errors are themselves treated as uncertain. We refer to these uncertainties informally as errors-on-errors and account for them using the Gamma Variance Model, which treats the squared quoted systematic errors as Gamma-distributed estimates of unknown variances. As a result, the usual quadratic nuisance parameter constraints in the $\chi^2$ are replaced with logarithmic ones. We present two applications of the framework. In the first, a robustness test estimates the largest errors-on-errors effects that could be present in our reproduction of the HERAPDF2.0 NNLO fit, reducing $\chi^2/n_{\rm dof}$ from 1363/1131 to 1306/1131, with the main impact concentrated at low Bjorken $x$ and low squared momentum transfer, $Q^2$. Comparable reductions are observed with a more flexible small-$x$ parametrisation, both at fixed NNLO and with NNLO+NLL$_x$ resummation. In the second, the error-on-error parameters are instead assigned a priori, as they would be in a PDF determination intended for publication. Taken together, the results indicate that errors-on-errors can account for a substantial part of the apparent data-theory tension in the combined HERA dataset, improving the inferred compatibility and widening the fitted PDF uncertainties without appreciably displacing the PDFs or cross-section predictions themselves.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how uncertainties in systematic errors ('errors-on-errors') affect parton distribution function (PDF) fits to HERA deep-inelastic scattering data, using the Gamma Variance Model to replace quadratic χ² constraints with logarithmic ones; it shows such treatment reduces χ²/n_dof and improves data-theory compatibility—especially at low x and Q²—while widening PDF uncertainties without shifting central values.
AI.motivation: To assess whether unaccounted uncertainty in the quoted systematic errors (i.e., 'errors-on-errors') contributes to the observed data-theory tension (χ²/n_dof > 1) in the combined HERA inclusive DIS dataset used for PDF determinations.
AI.method: Applies the Gamma Variance Model, treating squared systematic errors as Gamma-distributed estimators of unknown true variances; replaces standard quadratic nuisance parameter terms in χ² with logarithmic penalties; performs two analyses: (i) a robustness test optimizing error-on-error parameters, and (ii) a prior-driven fit mimicking a published PDF determination.
AI.result: Reduction in χ²/n_dof from 1363/1131 to 1306/1131; largest improvements at low x and low Q²; similar gains with flexible small-x parametrizations and NNLO+NLLₓ resummation; PDF central values and cross-section predictions remain stable while PDF uncertainties widen significantly.
AI.conclusion: Errors-on-errors constitute a substantial, previously neglected source of uncertainty that explains part of the HERA data-theory tension; incorporating them improves goodness-of-fit and yields more realistic, conservative PDF uncertainties without biasing central values.

title: Absolute luminosity calibration of the LHCb detector in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV with beam-gas imaging
comment: All figures and tables, along with any supplementary material and additional information, are available at this https URL (LHCb public pages)
summary: An absolute calibration of the luminosity for proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV with the LHCb detector in Run 2 of the LHC is presented. The calibration cross-section of the Vertex counter, a statistic based on reconstructed primary vertices, is measured using the beam-gas imaging method to be $\sigma_\mathrm{Vertex} = 57.61 \pm 0.06\ (stat) \pm 0.52\ (syst)$ mb, corresponding to a relative precision of 0.91%. This result provides around a factor of two improvement in the precision of the LHCb luminosity calibration used in previous cross-section measurements with this dataset. The largest systematic uncertainties arise from the imperfect knowledge of the beam-gas vertex resolution, the observed fill-by-fill spread of the cross-section, and the choice of transverse beam-profile fit model.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an improved absolute luminosity calibration for 13 TeV pp collisions in LHCb Run 2, achieving 0.91% relative precision using the beam-gas imaging method to measure the Vertex counter cross-section.
AI.motivation: To improve the precision of luminosity calibration for LHCb cross-section measurements in Run 2, reducing systematic uncertainties that limited prior analyses.
AI.method: Beam-gas imaging method applied to the Vertex counter — a primary-vertex-counting statistic — to determine its calibration cross-section; systematic uncertainties evaluated from beam-gas vertex resolution, fill-by-fill cross-section variations, and transverse beam-profile modeling.
AI.result: Measured Vertex counter cross-section: σ_Vertex = 57.61 ± 0.06 (stat) ± 0.52 (syst) mb, yielding 0.91% relative precision — approximately double the precision of previous LHCb Run 2 calibrations.
AI.conclusion: The new calibration significantly enhances the accuracy of luminosity-dependent measurements in LHCb Run 2, enabling more precise differential and total cross-section determinations.

title: Signatures of Leptophilic Baryogenesis at Muon Colliders
summary: The baryon asymmetry of the Universe may be produced in a model with 3 Higgs fields, a Higgs Troika, without the need for a strong first order electroweak phase transition. The couplings of the new Higgs fields to Standard Model fermions are assumed in accord with the "Spontaneous Flavor Violation (SFV)" framework, in order to avoid large deviations from flavor physics constraints. We consider a leptophilic version of SFV and outline its potential signatures at future muon colliders, envisioned to be multi-TeV partonic center of momentum machines. Hence, they provide optimal venues to search for the leptophilic Higgs Troika baryogenesis mechanism. The projected reach for signals of the new scalars allows for probing the key components of the baryogenesis model at scales that accommodate cosmological requirements.

AI.tldr: Proposes a 'Higgs Troika' model with three Higgs fields to generate baryon asymmetry without requiring a strong first-order electroweak phase transition; employs leptophilic Spontaneous Flavor Violation (SFV) to satisfy flavor constraints and identifies multi-TeV muon colliders as ideal probes for its baryogenesis mechanism.
AI.motivation: To explain the baryon asymmetry of the Universe without relying on a strong first-order electroweak phase transition—a challenging requirement in many BSM baryogenesis scenarios—while respecting stringent flavor physics constraints.
AI.method: Constructs a model with three Higgs fields ('Higgs Troika') coupled to SM fermions via the Spontaneous Flavor Violation (SFV) framework, specifically its leptophilic variant; analyzes phenomenological signatures and experimental reach at future multi-TeV muon colliders.
AI.result: Demonstrates that muon colliders can probe the key scalar sector parameters of the model at energy scales consistent with successful electroweak baryogenesis and cosmological baryon asymmetry requirements.
AI.conclusion: The leptophilic Higgs Troika scenario is a viable, testable baryogenesis mechanism compatible with flavor constraints, and upcoming muon colliders offer a unique opportunity to experimentally verify its core components.
